title: #220 Keyboard Warriors键盘侠
transcript:
大家好，欢迎回来 MaoMi Chinese！大家上网的时候，有没有见过这样的人？他们觉得自己很聪明，知道很多，也总是批评别人。在中文里，我们叫这些人“键盘侠”。今天我们来聊聊这个词。

你知道什么是键盘吗？就是电脑前的那一排排按键。我们平时常常在电脑的键盘上打字。那你知道什么是“侠”吗？这个字原来是“侠客”的意思。中国古代的侠客是很厉害的人，会功夫，帮助别人，保护弱小的人。可是，今天我们说的“键盘侠”不是这样的人。

“键盘侠”意思是那些在网上很爱说话的人。他们总是批评别人，说这个不对，说那个不好。但是，他们只会打字，只会说话，不会真的去做什么。你可以想一想，他们像“武士”，但是手里没有剑，只有键盘。

比如，有人在网上分享自己的生活，说带孩子、做饭、工作太累了，键盘侠就会跳出来，说：“你怎么这么懒？”“你这个人真自私。”可是，他们根本不认识那个人，可能也没有孩子，也没有工作。

又比如，可能我们在社交媒体上，说我们喜欢学英文，学中文，或者学日文，等等，可能有人就会给我们评论：“现在学外语也太笨了！有了AI，谁还需要学习外语？”可是，他们可能不懂AI，也不懂外语。

为什么有些人喜欢当键盘侠呢？一个原因是，在网上，人们不用自己的真名。 他们觉得安全，不怕别人知道自己是谁。因为不管说什么话，都没有责任，所以有些人就会在网上说一些很糟糕的话。

有时候，键盘侠也不一定是坏人。他们可能真的有自己的想法，也有自己的感情，只是不知道怎么说话，不知道怎么尊重别人。

所以，下次你看到有人在网上说很糟糕的话，你可以想一想：“他是不是一个键盘侠？”我们也可以想一想：“我是不是有时候也变成了键盘侠？”

在现实生活里，说话是一回事，做事是另一回事。如果我们真的关心一件事，我们可以用行动去改变，而不是只在网上说难听的话。

你有没有见过“键盘侠”？你觉得为什么有些人想当键盘侠？欢迎给我们留言，说说你的想法！

好啦，今天的MaoMi Chinese就先到这里。那我们下次再见吧！
translation:
Hello everyone, and welcome back to MaoMi Chinese! Have you ever seen people like this online? People who think they’re clever, that they know a lot, and are always criticising others? In Chinese, we call them “keyboard warriors” — 键盘侠. Today, let’s talk about this word.

Do you know what a keyboard is? It’s the row of buttons in front of a computer. We often use the keyboard to type. And do you know what 侠 means? It originally comes from 侠客, which refers to a kind of warrior in ancient China — someone strong, skilled in martial arts, who helped others and protected the weak.

But the “keyboard warriors” we talk about today are not like that at all.

A 键盘侠 is someone who loves to talk online. They’re always criticising others — saying this is wrong, that is bad. But all they do is type. They don’t really do anything in real life. You can imagine them as a “warrior” with no sword — only a keyboard in their hands.

For example, someone might post online about their life — maybe about looking after children, cooking, or being tired from work. Then a keyboard warrior jumps in to comment: “Why are you so lazy?” or “You’re so selfish.” But they don’t even know that person. Maybe they don’t even have kids, or a job themselves.

Or maybe you post on social media that you like learning English, Chinese, or Japanese. And someone comments: “Learning languages is stupid now! We have AI, who still needs to learn languages?” But they probably don’t understand AI, and they don’t know anything about languages either.

Why do some people like being keyboard warriors? One reason is that online, people don’t have to use their real names. They feel safe, and they’re not afraid of being found out. Because they don’t need to take responsibility for what they say, some people say really awful things online.

Sometimes, a keyboard warrior isn’t a bad person. They might have real thoughts and feelings — they just don’t know how to express themselves, or how to respect others when they speak.

So, next time you see someone saying horrible things online, maybe ask yourself: “Are they a keyboard warrior?” And also, “Have I ever been a keyboard warrior myself?”

In real life, saying something and doing something are two different things. If we really care about something, we can take action — not just post angry comments online.

Have you seen a keyboard warrior before? Why do you think some people want to be like that? Leave us a message and share your thoughts!

That’s all about today. We will see you again next time!

title: #221 Tasty Words: Chinese Food Metaphors 用食物说话
transcript:
大家好，欢迎回来 MaoMi Chinese！

大家都知道，中国人真的很爱吃。吃饭的时候要吃，聊天的时候也要说吃的。今天我们就来聊一聊中文里，那些用“食物”来说话的表达。你会发现，很多我们平时说的话，其实都是吃出来的！

比如，如果一个人脸上没有笑容，看起来很不开心，我们会说，他有一张“苦瓜脸”。苦瓜是很苦的蔬菜，很多人不喜欢吃。它看起来也皱皱的，不太可爱。所以“苦瓜脸”就是那种苦着脸、不高兴的样子。

再比如，“他被老板炒鱿鱼了”。什么意思呢？当然不是老板真的在厨房炒鱿鱼。这里的“炒鱿鱼”，其实就是“被辞职”、“被开除了”。这个表达是怎么来的呢？以前，人们在公司工作，有些人会被公司开除，也就是老板不要他们在公司工作了。他们要用一块布把自己的东西卷起来带走，就像卷鱿鱼一样。所以“炒鱿鱼”就变成了“被开除”的意思。

还有一个很常用的表达，叫“烫手山芋”。山芋就是红薯，也叫地瓜，热的时候很烫，你不想拿太久，会马上扔掉。那“烫手山芋”就是一件很麻烦、大家都不想做的事情。有时候，老板给你一个工作，但你一看就知道是个大麻烦，你就可以说：“这个工作是个烫手山芋啊！”

还有一个比较新一点的，叫“吃瓜”。这个表达现在年轻人特别爱用。“吃瓜”原来是说吃西瓜，后来变成了“看别人八卦，看热闹”的意思。以前，如果邻居吵架了，人们喜欢一边吃西瓜，一边看热闹。比如，如果有人在网上吵架，大家就在评论区留言说：“我来吃瓜了。”意思是我来看你们的热闹，不评论、不加入，只是安静地看。

又比如，吃软饭。还有很多人觉得，男人应该赚钱，女人应该照顾家庭。如果女人赚钱，男人照顾家庭，人们会说这个男人“吃软饭”。当然，这个是很不礼貌的表达，而且我们也知道这个表达有很多偏见。如果你听到别人说一个人“吃软饭”，那你可以告诉他们：“男女平等，男人和女人都可以照顾家庭。”

这些表达都很有意思。你会发现，中国人真的很喜欢用食物来说话，不只是为了吃饭，也是为了表达我们的感觉和生活。

在你的语言里，也有用食物来说话的表达吗？欢迎给我们留言，和我们分享！谢谢你的收听，那我们下次见吧！
translation:
Hello everyone, and welcome back to MaoMi Chinese!

As you probably know, Chinese people really love food. We love eating when we eat, and even when we chat, we talk about food. Today, let’s have a look at some fun expressions in Chinese that contained food. You’ll be surprised how many everyday phrases are actually “food-related”!

For example, if someone doesn’t smile and looks quite unhappy, we might say they have a “bitter melon face” (苦瓜脸). Bitter melon is a very bitter vegetable that many people don’t like. It’s also wrinkly and doesn’t look very cute. So, a “bitter melon face” means someone looks upset or miserable.

Here’s another one: “He got stir-fried squid by his boss” (他被老板炒鱿鱼了). What does that mean? Of course, it doesn’t mean the boss was cooking squid in the kitchen! In Chinese, “炒鱿鱼” actually means “to be fired” or “to be dismissed”. Where does this come from? In the past, when someone got fired from a company, they had to roll up their bedding and belongings to take away with them. It looked like rolled-up squid! That’s how this expression came to mean “being fired”.

Another commonly used expression is “hot sweet potato” (烫手山芋). A sweet potato, when it’s hot, is too hot to hold, and you want to drop it immediately. So a “hot sweet potato” is a tricky task or responsibility that no one wants to deal with. For example, your boss gives you a job, and you can tell straight away it’s full of trouble – you might say: “This task is a real hot sweet potato!”

Now let’s look at a newer expression: “eating melon” (吃瓜). Young people especially love this one. Originally, it meant literally eating watermelon, but now it means “watching gossip or drama”. In the past, when neighbours argued, people liked to sit around with some watermelon and watch the scene. Nowadays, if people are arguing online, you’ll often see comments like: “I’m just here eating melon.” That means: “I’m just here to watch, not getting involved.”

Another one is “eating soft rice” (吃软饭). In traditional thinking, people used to say men should earn money and women should look after the home. So if a man doesn’t work and is supported by his wife or girlfriend, some people would say he’s “eating soft rice”. Of course, this is not a polite expression at all, and we now understand that it’s full of prejudice. If you hear someone say it, you can say: “Men and women are equal – anyone can look after the home.”

Aren’t these expressions interesting? As you can see, Chinese people don’t just talk about food when we’re hungry – we also use food to express our feelings and daily life.

Does your language also use food as a metaphor? Come and leave us a comment – we’d love to hear your examples! Thank you for your listening today, and we will see again soon next time!

title: #222 The Bubble Tea Assassin 奶茶刺客
transcript:
大家好，欢迎回来 MaoMi Chinese！

你有没有买过一杯奶茶，付钱的时候才发现，哇！怎么这么贵？明明只是奶和茶，怎么要五十块、六十块？这时候，中国人可能会说：这是个奶茶刺客啊！今天我们来聊聊这个很有意思的词：刺客。

以前，“刺客”是古代的杀手，但是现在是年轻人很爱说的一个词。我们说“奶茶刺客”，就是那种看起来很普通，但是特别贵的奶茶。你看它的时候，感觉很好喝，很普通，应该也不贵，但付钱的时候，发现它特别贵！它像一个“刺客”一样，突然刺了你的钱包一下，让你心疼。

除了奶茶刺客，还有很多别的“刺客”。比如：

冰淇淋刺客。你拿了一根冰淇淋，肤浅要四十多块。

面包刺客。一个看起来很普通的小面包，六十块！

水果刺客。你以为是很普通的香蕉，结果是日本进口的香蕉，特别贵！

这些“刺客”都一样：它们看起来不贵，但是在你付钱的时候会突然让你的钱包受伤。如果买东西的时候，不想遇到刺客，一定要看好价钱，再去付钱。

现在，很多人还会用一个词：背刺。原来，背刺，意思是，你很相信一个人，但是这个人在你的背后偷偷地攻击你。现在，我们买东西的时候，也可以说背刺。

比如，你很喜欢去一家超市买东西，因为这家超市的东西很好。但是有一天，你在超市里看见一个老鼠，你觉得这家超市的东西可能也不干净。你就可以说：“我以为他们的东西很好，很干净，唉，这家超市背刺了我。”

又比如，你常常去一家饭店吃饭，因为这家饭店不但好吃，而且便宜。突然，有一天，你又去这家饭店吃饭，付钱的时候，你付了很多钱。老板说：“我们涨价了！ ”你就可以说：“唉，这家饭店背刺了我。”

刺客让你的钱包疼，背刺让你的心疼。

你有没有过这样的经历？欢迎给我们留言，和我们分享哦！好啦，今天的MaoMi Chinese就先到这里，那我们下次见吧！
translation:
Hello everyone, and welcome back to MaoMi Chinese!

Have you ever bought a cup of bubble tea, and only when you got to the checkout thought: wow! Why is it so expensive? It’s just milk and tea — why does it cost fifty or sixty yuan? At times like this, Chinese people might say: this is a bubble tea assassin! Today, let’s talk about this very interesting word: “assassin”.

In the past, an “assassin” was a killer from ancient times. But nowadays, it’s a word young people love to use. When we say “bubble tea assassin”, we mean bubble tea that looks very ordinary, but is actually really expensive. When you look at it, it seems tasty and nothing special, so it shouldn’t be expensive — but when you go to pay, you realise it’s really pricey! It’s like an “assassin” that suddenly stabs your wallet — and it hurts.

Besides bubble tea assassins, there are lots of other kinds of “assassins”. For example:

Ice cream assassin — you pick up a popsicle, and at the checkout, it costs over forty yuan.

Bread assassin — a small, plain-looking bun costs sixty yuan!

Fruit assassin — you thought it was just a regular banana, but it turns out to be imported from Japan — really expensive!

All of these “assassins” are similar: they don’t look expensive, but when it’s time to pay, your wallet suddenly takes a hit. If you don’t want to meet these assassins when shopping, make sure you check the price before heading to the till.

Nowadays, a lot of people also use another word: “backstab”. Originally, “backstab” means that you really trust someone, but they secretly attack you from behind. But now, we also use “backstab” when we talk about shopping.

For example, you really like shopping at a certain supermarket, because their things are usually great. But one day, you see a rat inside the shop, and start to feel that maybe their food isn’t so clean after all. Then you could say: “I thought their stuff was good and clean… sigh, this supermarket backstabbed me.”

Or maybe you often eat at a certain restaurant, because it’s tasty and cheap. But one day, you go again, and when you go to pay, the bill is a lot more. The owner says, “We’ve raised the prices!” You could say: “Sigh, this restaurant backstabbed me.”

Assassins make your wallet hurt. Backstabs make your heart hurt.

Have you ever had an experience like that? Feel free to leave us a comment and share your story with us! That’s all for today’s MaoMi Chinese — see you next time!

title: #223 Chinese start tipping? 中国开始给小费了？
transcript:
大家好，欢迎回来 MaoMi Chinese！

最近，很多中国人都在讨论一个新闻：海底捞开始让顾客给小费了。顾客，也就是去饭店里吃饭的人。小费是什么呢？如果你去饭店吃饭，你很喜欢服务员的服务，你就可以给服务员小费。比如，在美国，人们出去吃饭，是要给小费的。在英国和欧洲，如果你觉得服务员的服务很好，你也可以给小费。

海底捞开始让顾客给小费了，这是怎么回事呢？

海底捞是中国最有名的火锅店。很多人都说，海底捞的服务特别好。服务员给顾客送水果，送饮料。如果人很多，你在海底捞等座位，海底捞的服务员还会帮你做美甲。如果今天是你的生日，海底捞的服务员会给你送蛋糕，也会为你唱生日快乐。很多人觉得，去海底捞吃饭，不只是吃火锅，也是去享受服务。

在中国，吃饭是没有小费的。你去火锅店、饭馆、咖啡馆，点了菜，付了钱，就可以走，不用给服务员小费。中国人习惯了。

最近，海底捞说，如果你觉得服务很好，可以自己选择给一点小费。也就是说，我们可以给，也可以不给。

但是，很多中国人不同意。有人说：“中国没有小费的文化。海底捞比很多火锅店贵，但是因为服务好，我们才愿意来。”也有人说：“外国人要给小费，是因为服务员的工资很低，所以才要小费。”有人说：“海底捞应该给服务员更多的工资，而不是要顾客给小费。”也有人问：“以后不给小费，是不是服务就变差了？”

也有一些人担心，如果顾客给服务员小费，海底捞以后会不会少给服务员工资。不过，也有人觉得，服务员那么努力，如果客人愿意多给一点钱，也没有问题，是一种感谢。

最后怎么样了呢？因为中国人都不喜欢小费的文化，所以海底捞也取消小费了。

你怎么看？在你住的国家，吃饭要给小费吗？欢迎给我们留言，说说你的想法！那今天的MaoMi Chinese就先到这里，我们下次再见吧！
translation:
Hello everyone, and welcome back to MaoMi Chinese!

Recently, many people in China have been talking about a news story: Haidilao has started allowing customers to give tips. 顾客customers, are people who go to the restaurant to eat. But what are 小费tips? If you go to a restaurant and really like the service, you can give the waiter or waitress a little extra money — that’s called a tip. For example, in the United States, people are expected to tip when they eat out. In the UK and Europe, if you feel the service was particularly good, you can choose to leave a tip as well.

So, what’s going on with Haidilao and tips?

Haidilao is one of the most famous hotpot restaurants in China. Many people say the service there is excellent. The staff bring you fruit and drinks. If it’s busy and you have to wait for a table, the staff might even offer to do your nails. If it’s your birthday, they’ll bring you a cake and sing “Happy Birthday” for you. A lot of people feel that eating at Haidilao isn’t just about the food — it’s about enjoying the whole service experience.

In China, it’s not normal to tip when you eat out. You go to a restaurant, order your food, pay the bill, and that’s it. There’s no need to tip the staff. Chinese people are used to this.

Recently, Haidilao said that if you think the service was really good, you can choose to give a small tip. In other words, it’s completely optional — you can tip, or not tip.

But many Chinese people aren’t happy about it. Some say, “China doesn’t have a tipping culture. Haidilao is more expensive than many hot pot restaurants, but because its service is good, people are happy to go there.” Others argue, “In foreign countries, people tip because the waiters are paid very little — that’s why tipping is needed.” Some people say, “Haidilao should raise staff wages instead of asking customers to tip.” Others worry, “If we don’t tip, will the service get worse in the future?”

Some are also concerned that if customers start tipping, Haidilao might eventually reduce staff wages.

Still, there are people who think: the staff work very hard, so if customers want to show a bit of appreciation with a tip, that’s fine too.

So what happened in the end? Because Chinese people all dislike the culture of tipping, Haidilao cancelled it already.

What do you think? In your country, do people tip when they eat out? Feel free to leave us a comment and share your thoughts! That’s all about today. We will see you again next time!

title: #224 Stop the Comparison Game 和自己比
transcript:
大家好，欢迎回来 MaoMi Chinese！

最近，有一个听众跟我说，他以前觉得学中文很难，听到同学可以说很流利的中文，有时候也觉得很难过。我听了也很难过。今天我想和大家聊一句话，很多人小时候听过，大人也常常说：不用和别人比。

这句话听起来很简单，但是，其实很难做到。我们从小，就习惯了和别人比。很多中国人喜欢和别人比，因为我们的爸爸妈妈也喜欢和别人比。

小时候，我们有很多考试。考试完以后，我们爸爸妈妈会问：“考得怎么样？”他们也可能会说：“你的考试成绩比邻居的孩子差啊！” 有时候我们努力了，可是成绩还是比别人差，就会觉得：“我是不是不够聪明？” 我们跑步没有别人快，唱歌没有别人好听，也会想：“我是不是不够好？”

但是后来我发现，有些事情，真的不需要和别人比。

有一次，我教一个学生写中文汉字。她写得不快，也不完美，但她很认真。她说：“我以前很讨厌中文，因为我以前的老师总是说其他同学的中文比我好。”但是那天，她说：“我觉得我的中文比以前好了！”

我听了很开心，因为她开始不和别人比，只和自己比。

我们每个人都不一样。有的人数学好，有的人画画好，有的人做饭特别棒。我们不可能什么都比别人强，也不需要什么都赢。

慢慢长大以后，我越来越觉得，不用和别人比，是一种自由。

我们可以有自己的速度。别人三个月学会游泳，我们一年学会也没关系；别人二十岁找到好工作，我们三十岁才找到喜欢的事情，也很好。重要的不是我们跑得多快，而是我们有没有走在自己想走的路上。

最后我想说，不和别人比，不是不想变得更好，而是把眼睛从别人身上，放回你自己身上。

你今天有没有比昨天更开心？你这次有没有比上次更努力？你现在是不是更了解自己？

如果答案是“有”，那就够了。

我们聊了很多有“比”的句子。你怎么看呢？你觉得我们应该和别人比，还是和自己比？欢迎给我们留言，和我们分享你的故事！好啦，今天的MaoMi Chinese就先到这里，我们下次再见吧！
translation:
Hello everyone, and welcome back to MaoMi Chinese!

Recently, one of our listeners told me that he used to find learning Chinese really difficult. When he heard his classmates speaking fluent Chinese, he sometimes felt disheartened. I felt sad hearing that too. Today, I want to talk to you about a phrase many of us heard when we were children, and one that adults often say as well: Don’t compare yourself to others.

This phrase sounds simple, but in reality, it’s hard to do. From a young age, we’re used to comparing ourselves to others. Many Chinese people like to compare, because our parents liked to compare too.

When we were little, we had lots of exams. After an exam, our parents would ask, “How did you do?” They might even say, “Your results aren’t as good as the neighbour’s child!” Sometimes, even when we tried our best, if our grades were still lower than others’, we’d think, “Am I not clever enough?” If we couldn’t run as fast or sing as well as others, we’d wonder, “Am I just not good enough?”

But later, I realised that for some things, we really don’t need to compare ourselves to others.

Once, I was teaching a student how to write Chinese characters. She wasn’t quick, and her writing wasn’t perfect, but she was very focused. She told me, “I used to hate Chinese, because my old teacher always said other classmates were better than me.” But that day, she said, “I think my Chinese is better than it used to be!”

I was really happy to hear that, because she had stopped comparing herself to others, and was only comparing herself to her past self.

Each of us is different. Some people are good at maths, some are good at drawing, and some are brilliant at cooking. We can’t be the best at everything, and we don’t need to be.

As I’ve grown older, I’ve come to feel that not comparing yourself to others is a kind of freedom.

We can move at our own pace. If someone learns to swim in three months, it’s perfectly fine if it takes us a year. If someone lands a great job at twenty, it’s just as wonderful to find what we love at thirty. What matters isn’t how fast we run, but whether we’re moving in the direction we truly want.

And finally, I want to say this: not comparing yourself to others doesn’t mean you don’t want to improve. It just means you’re shifting your focus—from others, back to yourself.

Have you felt happier than yesterday? Have you worked harder this time than last time? Do you understand yourself better now?

If the answer is yes, then that’s enough.

We talked about many sentences using ‘比’. What’s your thought on this? Do you think we should compare with others, or simply ourselves? Feel free to leave us a comment, and share your story with us! That’s all about MaoMi Chinese today. We will see you again soon!

title: #225 The Secret World of Extra Classes in China 补课的秘密
transcript:
大家好，欢迎回来 MaoMi Chinese！你在学校上了一天的课以后，会做什么？和朋友玩，还是回家看电视？以前，在中国，很多的孩子放学后，都要补课。今天我们来聊一聊，“补课”。

“补课”是什么意思呢？就是学生在学校上完课以后，还要再上更多的课。可以在补习班，也可以请老师在家里教。很多中国学生，从小学到高中，都会补课。

为什么要补课呢？有两个主要的原因。第一个原因，家长希望孩子成绩更好，可以考上好学校。第二个原因是“竞争”。“竞争”就是很多人都想要同一个东西，比如一个好的大学，一个好的工作。如果别人都补课，你不补课，就可能落后，也就是比别人差。

所以，在中国，有很多年，学生们都经常补课。补课也是很赚钱的生意，一些补课的老师工资非常高，补课的学校赚了很多钱。

但是，2021年，中国政府出了一个新的政策，叫“双减”。“双减”的意思是：减少学生的作业，减少校外的补课。政府觉得，学生太累了，家长花的钱也太多，所以要“减”。

那大家怎么看呢？有的人很开心。他们觉得孩子终于可以早点休息，可以玩。家长也不用花那么多钱。但是，也有的人担心。他们怕没有补课，孩子成绩会不好。

那现在中国还有没有补课呢？其实还是有的，只是有点不一样了。比如，一些家长会请私人老师偷偷上课。有的补课班改名字，叫“兴趣班”。“兴趣”的意思是你喜欢的东西，比如画画、唱歌、跳舞，等等。但是，有时候这些“兴趣班”里，其实还是在教语文和数学。所以，政府好像禁止了补课，但是其实还有一些人在偷偷补课。因为家长的想法没有变，竞争也没有变。

我觉得，补课是一个很复杂的问题。一方面，孩子需要玩和休息。另一方面，家长又希望孩子学更多。

好啦，我们先来看看今天聊的词语：

补课：在学校以外上课，比如，我每天放学以后都要去补课。

竞争：很多人想要同一个东西。比如，这个学校的竞争很大，每个学生都得努力学习。

双减：一个中国政府的教育政策，减少作业和补课。比如，双减以后，我有更多时间玩了。

兴趣班：为了兴趣参加的课，比如画画、音乐。比如，我周末去上画画兴趣班。

你们国家有补课吗？你小时候补过课吗？欢迎给我们留言，和我们分享哦！
translation:
Hello everyone, welcome back to MaoMi Chinese! After all day lessons in school, what would you do? Have fun with friends, or go home to watch TV? In the past, children in China have to 补课bǔkè after school. Today we’re going to talk about 补课bǔkè.

What does “bǔkè” mean? It means that after finishing lessons at school, students still have to take more lessons. This could be in a tutoring centre, or with a teacher coming to teach at home. Many Chinese students, from primary school to high school, all have extra lessons.

So why do people have extra lessons? There are two main reasons.

The first reason is that parents want their children to get better marks and get into a good school.

The second reason is “competition”. “Competition” means that many people want the same thing, for example a good university place, or a good job. If everyone else is having extra lessons and you don’t, you might fall behind – in other words, you won’t do as well as others.

So in China, for many years, students often had extra lessons. It was also a very profitable business. Some tutoring teachers earned very high salaries, and the tutoring schools made a lot of money.

But in 2021, the Chinese government introduced a new policy called “double reduction” (双减). “Double reduction” means reducing students’ homework, and reducing extra lessons outside school. The government thought students were too tired, and parents were spending too much money, so they wanted to “reduce”.

What did people think of this policy? Some people were happy. They felt children could finally rest earlier and have time to play. Parents also didn’t need to spend so much money. But some people were worried. They were afraid that without extra lessons, their children’s marks would get worse.

So, are there still extra lessons in China now? Actually yes, but it’s a bit different. For example, some parents secretly hire private teachers. Some tutoring schools changed their names and became “interest classes”. “Interest” means something you like, such as painting, singing, or dancing. But sometimes, inside these “interest classes”, they are still teaching Chinese or Maths. So, it looks like the government banned extra lessons, but in reality some people are still doing them secretly. Because parents’ way of thinking hasn’t changed, and competition hasn’t changed either.

I think extra lessons are quite a complicated issue. On one hand, children need time to rest and play. On the other hand, parents still hope their children can learn more.

Alright, let’s review some of the words we talked about today:

补课 (bǔkè): extra lessons outside school. For example, I go to extra lessons every day after school.

竞争 (jìngzhēng): competition, when many people want the same thing. For example, the competition at this school is very strong, every student has to study hard.

双减 (shuāngjiǎn): a Chinese government policy to reduce homework and extra lessons. For example, after “double reduction”, I had more time to play.

兴趣班 (xìngqù bān): an interest class, for hobbies such as painting or music. For example, I go to a painting interest class at the weekend.

Do you have extra lessons in your country? Did you take them when you were a child? Feel free to leave me a message and share your experience!

title: #226 The War on Second-hand Smoke二手烟的战争
transcript:
大家好！欢迎回来MaoMi Chinese！

首先谢谢Maayot Chinese赞助今天的podcast！有时候，你是不是在想，在哪儿可以找到合适的中文阅读呢？Maayot Chinese就是一个很好的平台。你可以找到适合你的水平的中文阅读。欢迎去看看哦！

最近，在中国，有一个这样的新闻。有一个住在上海的外国人，他叫艾伦。他去一个饭店吃饭。饭店里有几个中国男人抽烟。在上海，人们是不可以在公共场所抽烟的。公共场所，就是公共的地方，很多人可以用的地方，比如，饭店，博物馆，医院，学校，等等。艾伦不喜欢抽二手烟，也就是不喜欢和抽烟的人在一起，所以他去告诉这几个男人，说这里禁止抽烟。但是呢，男人们不愿意，还骂他。艾伦拍了视频，发到了中国的社交媒体上。

他的视频很快就火了。很多人都觉得，他做得太好了，因为很多人都非常讨厌二手烟。也有很多人说，虽然他们也不喜欢二手烟，但是在中国禁烟太难了。这是为什么呢？

在中国，禁烟为什么这么难呢？

第一个原因是，中国抽烟的人特别多，有3.5亿人。中国是世界上抽烟的人最多的国家。很多人从年轻的时候就开始抽烟，到现在已经习惯了。所以，他们觉得，抽烟是很正常的事情。

第二个原因是，在中国，抽烟有时候是“社交”的一种方式。比如，有人见面的时候，会给对方一根烟。这是表示友好。如果你不要，有时候别人会觉得你不想和他做朋友。所以，抽烟不但是一个人的习惯，有时候也是一种社交。

第三个原因是，虽然法律说在公共场所不能抽烟，但是很多地方没有人去管。比如，在饭店里，老板可能不想客人走，所以客人抽烟也没关系。警察也不会一直来检查。所以，很多人觉得，就算法律说不能抽烟，也没有人真的会惩罚他们。

还有一个原因是，在中国卖烟的公司特别有钱，也很有影响力，也交很多税。他们不希望大家少抽烟，因为这样他们就赚不到钱了。

所以，虽然很多人讨厌二手烟，但是真的要“禁烟”，还是很难。可是，越来越多人在网上说，他们不喜欢二手烟，他们支持禁烟。以后中国可以禁烟吗？我们等一等吧！

那么，在你的国家，你们禁烟吗？你们是怎么禁烟的？你们国家禁烟，用了多长时间？欢迎给我们留言，和我们分享哦！
translation:
Hello everyone, and welcome back to MaoMi Chinese!

First of all, a big thank you to Maayot Chinese for sponsoring today’s podcast! Have you ever wondered where you can find suitable Chinese reading materials? Maayot Chinese is a great platform where you can discover readings that match your level. Do go and have a look!

Recently, there has been a news story in China. A foreigner living in Shanghai, called Alan, went to a restaurant for a meal. In the restaurant, there were several Chinese men smoking. Now in Shanghai, people are not allowed to smoke in public places. Public places are shared spaces, where many people may go, such as restaurants, museums, hospitals, schools, and so on. Alan doesn’t like second-hand smoke – that is, he doesn’t like being around people who are smoking – so he went over and told the men that smoking was forbidden there. But the men refused, and even swore at him. Alan filmed the whole incident and uploaded the video onto Chinese social media.

His video quickly went viral. Many people felt that what he did was excellent, because lots of people really dislike second-hand smoke. Others said that, although they too don’t like second-hand smoke, it is simply too difficult to ban smoking in China. But why is that?

So why is it so hard to ban smoking in China?

The first reason is that there are simply so many smokers. There are 350 million people who smoke in China, making it the country with the largest number of smokers in the world. Many people start smoking when they are young, and now it has become a habit. So, they think smoking is completely normal.

The second reason is that in China, smoking is sometimes a way of being social. For example, when people meet, one person may offer the other a cigarette as a gesture of friendliness. If you refuse, sometimes others may feel you don’t want to be friends with them. So smoking is not only a personal habit, but also, at times, a social custom.

The third reason is that, although the law says smoking is not allowed in public places, in reality many places are not monitored. For instance, in restaurants, the owner might not want to upset customers, so he will turn a blind eye if they smoke. The police will not be checking constantly either. As a result, many people feel that even if the law says smoking is forbidden, there will be no real punishment.

Another reason is that tobacco companies in China are extremely wealthy and influential, and they also contribute a great deal of tax revenue. They do not want people to smoke less, because then they would lose money.

So, although many people dislike second-hand smoke, a complete ban is still very difficult. However, more and more people are speaking out online, saying they don’t like second-hand smoke and that they support a smoking ban. Will China be able to implement a proper smoking ban in the future? Let’s wait and see!

What about in your country? Do you have a smoking ban? How was it put into place, and how long did it take? We’d love to hear from you. Please leave us a message and share your story!

title: #227 Dogs Eating Better Than Humans?  宠物吃得比人好
transcript:
大家好！欢迎回来MaoMi Chinese！

首先谢谢Maayot Chinese对我们的支持！如果你在准备考试，但是觉得很多词记不住，那可能是你没有记住怎么用这个词。用Maayot Chinese，你可以在句子中记词，也可以知道怎么用这个词。如果有兴趣，赶快试试吧！

你吃过麻辣烫吗？这是一种很多人喜欢的中国菜。你可以选你喜欢的肉和蔬菜，餐厅会把它们放在麻辣的汤里煮。在中国，很多人年轻人喜欢吃麻辣烫。最近，我看到一个很有意思的新闻。在上海，开了一家给狗狗吃的麻辣烫餐厅。主人们可以带狗狗来，给狗狗们选很多它们喜欢吃的菜，比如来自澳大利亚的牛肉，健康的鸡胸肉，还有很多蔬菜，等等。这些肉和蔬菜都是新鲜的，非常好。当然，狗狗的麻浪烫是不辣的，因为狗狗不能吃辣，也不能吃咸。选了菜以后，主人们可以去付钱，大概25元一斤，也就是50元一千克。

很多人说：狗狗吃得比我好！在中国，越来越多人愿意给他们的宠物花钱。很多宠物有自己的衣服，有自己的床，甚至有生日蛋糕。宠物就像家人一样。

为什么呢？我觉得有三个原因。第一个原因，中国人生活越来越好了。很多年轻人有钱了，也有空了，他们希望生活更开心。养宠物，让他们觉得很幸福。

第二个原因，很多年轻人离开家生活，或者一个人住。他们觉得很孤单。宠物可以陪他们，所以他们愿意给宠物最好的东西。

第三个原因，很多年轻人现在不愿意结婚，也不想生孩子。但是，他们更喜欢小动物，所以会养宠物。宠物就像是他们的孩子，他们也会给宠物买最好的东西。

所以，现在宠物在中国不只是“动物”，还是家人。人们愿意给它们花钱，也希望他们快乐、健康。不过，也有人说这样不太好。他们觉得给宠物花太多钱，是一种浪费。特别是在一些地方，还有人没有饭吃。

你怎么看呢？在你的国家，你们也有很多给宠物的餐厅吗？欢迎给我们留言，和我们分享哦！
translation:
Hello everyone, and welcome back to MaoMi Chinese!

First of all, a big thank you to Maayot Chinese for supporting us! If you are preparing for exams but feel that you just can’t remember many words, it might be because you haven’t remembered how to actually use them. With Maayot Chinese, you can learn words in full sentences and also see how they are used. If you’re interested, give it a try!

Have you ever eaten málàtàng? It’s a type of Chinese food that many people love. You can choose the meat and vegetables you like, and the restaurant will cook them in a spicy soup. In China, many young people enjoy eating málàtàng. Recently, I came across a very interesting piece of news. In Shanghai, a new málàtàng restaurant has opened—especially for dogs! Owners can take their dogs there and choose from lots of ingredients the dogs might enjoy, such as beef from Australia, healthy chicken breast, and a variety of vegetables. All of the meat and vegetables are fresh and of very good quality. Of course, the dogs’ málàtàng isn’t spicy, because dogs cannot eat spicy food, and they also cannot eat salty food. After choosing the ingredients, owners go to pay. The price is about 25 yuan per half a kilo, which is 50 yuan per kilogram.

Many people joke: “The dogs are eating better than me!” In China, more and more people are willing to spend money on their pets. Many pets even have their own clothes, their own beds, and even birthday cakes. Pets are just like family members.

But why is this happening? I think there are three reasons.

The first reason is that people in China are living better lives. Many young people have more money and more free time, and they want to enjoy life more. Keeping a pet makes them feel happy.

The second reason is that many young people live away from home, or live alone. They often feel lonely. Pets can keep them company, so they are willing to give their pets the very best.

The third reason is that many young people nowadays don’t want to get married, and don’t want to have children. Instead, they prefer small animals, so they choose to keep pets. Pets are like their children, and they buy the best things for them.

So now, pets in China are not just “animals”, but also family. People are happy to spend money on them, and they want their pets to be healthy and happy. But some people say this isn’t so good. They think spending too much money on pets is wasteful—especially when in some places, there are still people who don’t even have enough to eat.

What do you think? In your country, do you also have many restaurants for pets? Leave us a message and share your thoughts!

title: #228 The Registrar Who Stopped Divorces 最美红娘？
transcript:
大家好！欢迎回来MaoMi Chinese！今天也要谢谢Maayot Chinese的支持。这是一个可以让我们随时随地读中文的软件，我们都能在那里找到适合我们中文水平的中文文章。如果你感兴趣，快去试一试吧！

今天我们要聊一个很特别的故事。中文里有一个词：“红娘”。“红娘”不是红色的女人，而是一个工作。“红娘”也叫“媒人”，在以前的中国，男人和女人不能经常见面。如果他们要找人结婚，怎么办呢？他们需要“红娘”，或者“媒人”给他们介绍。“红娘”介绍两个人认识，帮助很多人结婚。在中国的武汉市，也有一个人，她的名字叫熊玲，人们叫她“最美红娘”。但是，也有很多人非常讨厌她。这是怎么样的故事呢？我们来听一听吧！

熊玲在武汉工作，她是一名婚姻登记员。每天都有很多夫妻来找她办结婚或者离婚。结婚的时候，人们脸上有笑容；可是在办离婚的时候，常常有眼泪，也有吵架。熊玲不想看到夫妻在生气的时候离婚。她觉得很多人其实只是生气，过一两天，可能会后悔，也就是觉得自己的决定不对。所以她想帮他们冷静。

她的方法很特别。她有时候会找一些小借口，让夫妻不要马上离婚。比如，她会说：“今天打印机坏了，不能办离婚。”有时候她会说：“网络有问题，你们明天再来吧。”这样一来，有些夫妻就会回家。回家以后，他们可能会想一想，冷静一下，有些人就决定不离婚了。在九年的时间里，她用这种方法救了大约五百对夫妻，没有离婚。

听了熊玲的事，很多人觉得她做得很好。有些人说，她的方法很好，帮助了很多的夫妻。但是，也有很多人觉得，这样做很不好。因为帮人离婚或者结婚，是她的工作。她也不应该帮人做决定。夫妻决定了要离婚，那么就让他们离婚吧。

好啦，我们先来说说今天学的词语吧！

那么，你觉得熊玲的做法对吗？欢迎给我们留言，说说你的想法！
translation:
Hello everyone! Welcome back to MaoMi Chinese! Today I’d also like to thank Maayot Chinese for their support. It’s an app that allows us to read Chinese anytime and anywhere, and we can always find articles that match our level of Chinese there. If you’re interested, go and give it a try!

Today I want to tell you a very special story. In Chinese, there’s a word: “红娘 (hóngniáng).” “红娘” doesn’t mean a woman dressed in red, but rather a job. “红娘” is also called “媒人,” which means a matchmaker. In the past in China, men and women couldn’t often meet each other. So, if they wanted to find someone to marry, what could they do? They needed a “红娘” or “matchmaker” to introduce them. The matchmaker would help two people meet and often helped many people get married.

In Wuhan, a city in China, there is a woman named Xiong Ling. People call her “the most beautiful matchmaker.” But at the same time, many people really dislike her. So, what kind of story is this? Let’s find out!

Xiong Ling works in Wuhan as a marriage registrar. Every day, many couples come to her either to get married or to get divorced. When they’re getting married, people usually have smiles on their faces. But when they’re getting divorced, there are often tears, and sometimes arguments too. Xiong Ling doesn’t want to see couples getting divorced when they’re angry. She thinks that many people are just upset in the moment. After a day or two, they may regret it, which means they might feel their decision wasn’t right. So, she wants to help them calm down.

Her method is quite unusual. Sometimes, she makes little excuses so that couples can’t divorce straight away. For example, she might say, “The printer is broken today, we can’t process your divorce.” Or she might say, “There’s a problem with the internet, please come back tomorrow.” In this way, some couples go home. After going home, they may reflect, calm down a bit, and some then decide not to go through with the divorce. Over nine years, she reportedly saved about five hundred couples from divorcing with this method.

After hearing about Xiong Ling, many people think what she did was very good. Some say her method is wonderful and helped many couples. But many others believe it’s not good at all. Helping people to marry or divorce is her official duty, but she shouldn’t be making decisions for them. If a couple has already decided to divorce, then they should be allowed to do so.

Now, let’s look at some of today’s key words.

“红娘 (hóngniáng)” – a person who helps people find a marriage partner. Since Xiong Ling prevented many couples from divorcing and protected their families, many also call her a “matchmaker.”

“后悔 (hòuhuǐ)” – to regret, meaning to feel that a past decision was wrong. For example, they decided to get divorced, but then they regretted it.

“借口 (jièkǒu)” – an excuse, which means a reason not to do something, often not a true reason. For example, he said he was ill and didn’t want to go to school, but I knew it was just his excuse.

So, what do you think of Xiong Ling’s actions? Do you agree with what she did? You’re welcome to leave us a message and share your thoughts!

title: #229 XiBei Restaurant and the Pre-Made Food Debate 西贝餐厅和预制菜
transcript:
大家好，欢迎回来 MaoMi Chinese!

今天的这一集要谢谢Maayot Chinese的支持！ 这个学习中文的网站和app很有用！可以读，可以听，也可以背单词。如果你在准备HSK的考试，用这个来练习阅读和背单词，可以让你记住更多！去试试看吧！

今天我们要聊一个最近在中国很火的话题：西贝餐厅和预制菜。

西贝是中国一家很有名的餐厅。他们的食物是中国西北菜，有牛肉羊肉，有大饼，也有很多面条。西贝一般开在商场里，很多中国人很喜欢吃西贝，很多爸爸妈妈喜欢带着孩子去西贝吃饭。

可是最近，很多人都在骂西贝。为什么呢？因为有人说，西贝的很多菜不是新鲜做的，而是“预制菜”。“预制菜”是什么意思？就是餐厅不是马上做菜，而是先在工厂里做好，然后冷冻，送到餐厅。客人点菜的时候，只要加热，就可以上桌。这样做很快，味道也差不多。

听起来很方便，对吗？但是，很多顾客不高兴。为什么？因为他们觉得，去餐厅，就是要吃新鲜的菜，要有厨师做菜。有人说，预制菜没有“烟火气”。“烟火气”就是家的感觉，很生活，很温暖，很热闹。比如我们说：这个小吃店很有烟火气，让我觉得很舒服。

不过，也有网友觉得，预制菜也不是坏事。他们说，现在很多快餐，很多外卖，本来就是预制菜。如果干净，如果安全，那就没问题。

那为什么大家生气呢？有的网友说：“我可以接受预制菜，但是我不能接受预制菜卖很贵的价钱。”他们觉得花很多钱，却只吃到预制菜，就是“不值”。“不值”的意思是 not worth it。比如：花一百块吃一份预制菜，我觉得不值。

西贝也做了回应。“回应”就是respond。西贝回应说，不是所有的菜都是预制菜，而且用预制菜，可以让全国西贝餐厅的味道一样。你去北京的西贝，或者去上海的西贝，味道都差不多。但是，这个回应没有让所有人满意。现在，在中国社交媒体上，大家还在讨论。有的人支持，有的人反对。

我们先来说说今天学的词吧：

那你觉得呢？你喜欢新鲜的菜，还是觉得预制菜也可以？你觉得，预制菜卖很贵，公不公平呢？下次去餐厅的时候，你也可以想一想，你吃的菜，是不是预制菜呢？
translation:
Hello everyone, and welcome back to MaoMi Chinese.

This episode is kindly supported by Maayot Chinese! Their website and app for learning Chinese are really useful. You can read, listen, and learn vocabulary. If you’re preparing for the HSK exam, using it to practise reading and vocabulary can really help you remember more.

Today we’re going to talk about a topic that has been very popular in China recently: XiBei restaurants and pre-made food.

XiBei is a very famous restaurant in China. Their food is northwestern cuisine – beef and lamb, big flatbreads, and many different kinds of noodles. XiBei usually opens inside shopping centres. Lots of Chinese people enjoy eating there, and many parents like to take their children to XiBei for a meal.

But recently, many people have been criticising XiBei. Why? Because some say that many of their dishes are not freshly made, but are instead “pre-made food”. What does “pre-made food” mean? It means the food isn’t cooked straight away in the restaurant, but is prepared in a factory in advance, then frozen and delivered. When customers order, the dish just needs to be heated before serving. It’s quick, and the taste is more or less the same.

Sounds convenient, right? But many customers are unhappy. Why? Because they feel that going to a restaurant should mean eating freshly cooked food, with chefs cooking on the spot. Some people say pre-made food has no “yan huo qi”. This phrase means the warm, lively atmosphere of home and daily life. For example, we might say: “This little eatery has lots of yan huo qi, it makes me feel comfortable.”

However, some people online feel that pre-made food isn’t such a bad thing. They point out that a lot of fast food and takeaway meals are already pre-made. If it’s clean and safe, then it’s not really a problem.

So why are people angry? Some say: “I can accept pre-made food, but I can’t accept pre-made food being sold at such high prices.” They feel that paying a lot of money only to be served pre-made dishes is simply “not worth it”. For example: “Spending 100 yuan on a pre-made meal – it’s not worth it.”

XiBei has also given a response. They said not all their dishes are pre-made, and using pre-made food helps them ensure consistency across the country. Whether you go to XiBei in Beijing or in Shanghai, the taste will be very similar. But this response hasn’t convinced everyone. On Chinese social media, people are still debating – some support it, others are against it.

Let’s quickly review the new words from today:

title: #230 Young People in China Becoming Rat? 老鼠人
transcript:
大家好！欢迎回来MaoMi Chinese！

今天的MaoMi Chinese也要谢谢Maayot Chinese的支持！我们学了新的词以后，怎么样才知道我们懂了呢？Maayot Chinese有很多的小测试，学了新的词以后，我们就可以做测试，让我们学得更好一点！

以前，我们说过“躺平”。“躺平”就是不想努力，不想和别人比赛，过一种很简单的生活。比如，不想买房，不想买车，不想结婚，不想生孩子，就是过得很轻松。这就是“躺平”。

那“老鼠人”是什么意思呢？在网上，有一些年轻人把自己叫做“老鼠人”。他们不是真的老鼠，只是因为他们的生活习惯有点像老鼠。老鼠白天都躲在洞里，不出来。到了晚上才出来找东西吃。很多年轻人也是这样：白天不出门，不见朋友，也不和人说话。到了晚上，他们才开始活动，比如玩游戏，刷手机，看视频。

老鼠人喜欢躺平，也不喜欢社交。“社交”，就是和别人一起活动、聊天、见面。老鼠人不喜欢社交，他们不想和别人有太多联系。

有的老鼠人拍视频，记录他们的生活。比如：他们中午十二点才起床，点了外卖，躺在床上玩游戏，看电视剧，睡午觉，睡到晚上，吃晚饭。晚上继续玩手机，到两三点才睡。第二天，又是一样的一天。

为什么现在有那么多年轻人变成“老鼠人”呢？我觉得，有这些原因：

第一，一些年轻人生活压力很大。房租很贵，房价也很高，工作也很辛苦。

第二，很多人觉得，就算努力，也不一定能改变。努力工作，可能还是买不起房子。所以他们觉得努力没有用。

第三，社交让人觉得很累。面对面和别人说话，让他们觉得没有力气。但是，在手机上，发几句话就可以了。所以他们更喜欢在家里。

“老鼠人”这个词，就像年轻人的一种心情。变成老鼠人，对他们来说，其实是保护自己，不让自己太累。可是如果一直这样，他们可能会更孤单，对他们身体健康不好，心理健康也不好。

好啦，我们先来看看今天聊的词吧！

躺平”就是不想努力，不想和别人比赛，过一种很简单的生活。比如，工作太累了，我只想躺平。

老鼠人，像老鼠一样，白天睡觉，晚上才活动的人。

社交，就是和别人一起活动，见面，聊天。老鼠人都不喜欢社交。

你怎么看呢？你觉得做“老鼠人”是一个好事，还是一个坏事？欢迎给我们留言，和我们分享哦！
translation:
Hello everyone! Welcome back to MaoMi Chinese!

Today’s episode of MaoMi Chinese is kindly supported by Maayot Chinese! When we learn new words, how do we know if we really understand them? Maayot Chinese has lots of little quizzes. After we learn new words, we can take a quiz to check ourselves and help us learn even better!

In the past, we’ve talked about “tǎng píng”, or “lying flat”. “Lying flat” means not wanting to work hard, not wanting to compete with others, and living a very simple life. For example, not wanting to buy a house, not wanting to buy a car, not wanting to get married, not wanting to have children – just living in a relaxed way. That’s what “lying flat” means.

So, what does “lǎoshǔ rén” – “rat people” – mean? On the internet, some young people call themselves “rat people”. They are not really rats! It’s just that their way of living is a bit like a rat’s. Rats hide in their holes during the day and don’t come out. At night, they come out to look for food. Many young people are like this too: during the day they don’t go out, don’t meet friends, and don’t talk to anyone. At night, they become active – playing games, scrolling on their phones, watching videos.

Rat people like lying flat, and they don’t like socialising. “Socialising” means doing activities with others, chatting, meeting face to face. Rat people don’t enjoy this. They don’t want too much contact with other people.

Some rat people even make videos to record their lives. For example: they get up at midday, order takeaway, lie in bed playing games, watch dramas, take a nap, wake up in the evening, eat dinner. At night, they continue on their phones until two or three in the morning. The next day, it’s the same again.

Why are so many young people becoming rat people nowadays? I think there are a few reasons.

First, some young people feel a lot of pressure in life. Rent is expensive, house prices are high, work is tiring.

Second, many people feel that even if they work hard, it might not change anything. Even with a job, they still can’t afford a house. So, they think working hard is pointless.

Third, socialising feels exhausting. Talking face to face with others takes a lot of energy. But on a phone, you can just send a few messages. So, they prefer to stay at home.

“Rat people” is really a reflection of how young people are feeling. Becoming a rat person is, in a way, a way of protecting themselves, so they don’t feel too tired. But if it goes on for too long, they may feel more lonely, and it’s not good for their physical or mental health.

Okay, let’s first take a look at the words we’re talking about today!

“躺平” means not wanting to work hard, not wanting to compete with others, and just living a very simple life. For example: work is too tiring, I just want to “lie flat.”

“老鼠人” are people who live like mice – they sleep during the day and only come out at night.

“社交” means socializing: doing activities with other people, meeting up, chatting. “老鼠人” don’t like socializing.

What do you think? Do you think being a “rat person” is a good thing? Leave us a message and share your thoughts!

title: #231 From Chicken Cutlets to Fame 鸡排哥的故事
transcript:
大家好，欢迎回来 MaoMi Chinese！

谢谢Maayot Chinese对这集播客的支持。你可以用这个app来读中文，听中文，看新闻，也能记单词。如果你在准备HSK的考试，那你还能在这里看到HSK1到HSK6的单词。如果你感兴趣，试试看吧！

今天我们来聊一聊最近在中国很火的人，景德镇的鸡排哥。

鸡排哥的名字很简单。“鸡排”就是炸鸡肉的意思，英文是 chicken cutlet，“哥”是哥哥。在中文里，人们喜欢用“什么什么哥”“什么什么姐”来叫一个人，比如酱油哥，泡面姐，等等。鸡排哥就是卖鸡排的男人。

鸡排哥的名字叫李俊永。他是中国江西人，在景德镇生活了很多年。平时他在学校附近摆摊，卖鸡排。摆摊，意思是卖东西，但是不开店。我们可以推着小推车去摆摊。因为鸡排哥总是笑着和客人聊天，很热情，就有人拍了他的视频放到网上。人们发现他的鸡排又好吃又便宜，而且他说话也很有意思，很多网友看了他的视频以后都觉得很开心。

慢慢地，鸡排哥在网上火了起来。现在，很多人坐很久的高铁或者飞机，从别的地方来到景德镇，排队四五个小时，只为了买他做的鸡排。后来，排队的人越来越多，来景德镇旅游的人越来越多，鸡排哥就成了景德镇的一个小景点。

有时候排队的人很多，鸡排哥太忙了，但他也会说很多有意思的话，我们来听一听：

“做你的，做完你的我做你的，做完你的做你的。对对对对对，我来了我来了。我知道我知道我知道，我心里有数我心里有数。这种场面我还是在控制。”

因为客人太多了，他要快点做鸡排，所以他说话也很快。他说，做完一个客人的鸡排，就做下一个客人的鸡排。他让客人不用着急，因为他心里有数。心里有数，也就是我们知道自己在做什么。他还说，这种场面他还是在控制，意思是，虽然现在很忙，但是他还是可以控制的，他还是可以做好的。后来，人们也开始学鸡排哥说话：“这种场面我还是在控制的。”

以前，人们去景德镇是看瓷器，买瓷器。现在，很多人还会说：“我想先去找鸡排哥。”因为他的热情和真诚，让更多人注意到这个城市，也让景德镇变得热闹了。

鸡排哥自己说，他只是一个普通人，卖鸡排是为了生活。他希望大家喜欢他的家乡，也希望每个人都能开心地过好每一天。

好啦，我们先来说说今天的词语吧：

好啦，今天的MaoMi Chinese就先到这里。我们下次再见吧！
translation:
Hello everyone, welcome back to MaoMi Chinese!

Thank you to Maayot Chinese for supporting this episode. You can use this app to read Chinese, listen to Chinese, and read the news. You can also learn new words. If you’re preparing for the HSK exam, you can find vocabulary from HSK 1 to HSK 6 there. If you’re interested, give it a try!

Today we’re going to talk about someone who has become very popular in China recently — the Chicken Cutlet Brother from Jingdezhen.

His name is quite simple. “鸡排” means fried chicken, or chicken cutlet in English. “哥” means “older brother”. In Chinese, people often call someone “something哥” or “something姐”, such as “Soy Sauce Brother” or “Instant Noodles Sister”. So, “Chicken Cutlet Brother” simply means the man who sells chicken cutlets.

His real name is Li Junyong. He’s from Jiangxi Province and has lived in Jingdezhen for many years. Usually, he sets up a street stall near a school to sell chicken cutlets. The phrase 摆摊 means to sell things without opening a shop. You can push a small cart and set up a stall.

Because Chicken Cutlet Brother always smiles and chats warmly with his customers, someone filmed him and uploaded the video online. People found that his chicken cutlets were delicious and cheap, and that he was also very funny. Many viewers said his videos made them feel happy.

Gradually, Chicken Cutlet Brother became famous on the internet. Now, many people take long train or plane journeys from other cities to Jingdezhen, queueing for four or five hours just to buy his chicken cutlets. As more and more people came, Jingdezhen’s tourism also grew. Chicken Cutlet Brother became a small tourist attraction in the city.

Sometimes there are so many people in line that he gets extremely busy, but he still says some funny things. Let’s listen:

“Doing yours, after yours I’ll do yours, after yours I’ll do yours. Yes yes yes yes yes, I’m coming, I’m coming. I know, I know, I know, I’ve got it in my head, I’ve got it in my head. I’m still in control of this situation.”

Because there are so many customers, he has to work quickly, so he speaks very fast. He means that after he finishes one customer’s order, he will do the next one. He tells customers not to worry because he knows what he’s doing. The phrase “心里有数” means to know what you’re doing. He also says he’s “still in control of this situation”, which means that even though it’s very busy, he can still handle it well. Later, people started imitating him, saying: “I’m still in control of this situation.”

In the past, people went to Jingdezhen to see and buy porcelain. Now, many people say, “I want to visit Chicken Cutlet Brother first.” His warmth and sincerity have brought more attention to the city and made Jingdezhen even livelier.

Chicken Cutlet Brother says he’s just an ordinary person, selling chicken cutlets to make a living. He hopes people will like his hometown and that everyone can live happily every day.

Alright, let’s go over the words we learned today.

Alright, that’s all for today’s MaoMi Chinese. See you next time!

title: #232 China Golden Week Tent Trend 黄金周睡帐篷
transcript:
大家好！欢迎回来 MaoMi Chinese！

今天的播客也要谢谢Maayot Chinese的支持！这是一个学中文的app，可以记单词，读新闻，看一些中文的文章，随时随地在手机上学中文。以后学中文，就更方便了！如果你感兴趣，就去试试看吧！

上个星期是中国的黄金周。什么是黄金周呢？十月一号是中国的国庆节。每年这一天，中国都会放假，很多人都有七天假期，所以我们叫它“黄金周”。因为时间长，又在秋天，天气舒服，很多人都会出去旅游。

但是，这几年国庆节的时候，中国很多地方的酒店都非常贵。平时两三百块一晚的房间，黄金周可能要一千多块，两千多块。有的地方，酒店早早就订满了。订满了，意思是酒店没有房间了，火车没有票了，等等。于是，很多年轻人想出了一个新办法。他们黄金周旅游的时候，会带上帐篷。

你可能会想，他们是不是去露营？其实不是。他们不是去山里露营，而是在城市、景区外面、有时候在火车站旁边睡帐篷。在社交媒体上，你可以看到很多照片：有人在停车场睡帐篷，有人在草地上，还有人就在景区门口睡帐篷。白天玩，晚上就在帐篷里休息。

有些人看到这些照片，觉得有点辛苦。但是年轻人觉得没关系，他们觉得这样反而很有趣，也很自由。不用担心酒店太贵，也不用担心房间订满。带上帐篷，在哪里都睡觉。

有网友说：“我宁愿睡帐篷，也不想被酒店坑。”被坑，意思是被别人骗。 还有人说：“住帐篷虽然累一点，但是挺好玩的，晚上大家聊天、吃泡面、看星星，很有意思。”

也有人说，现在的年轻人想省钱，他们宁愿睡在不太舒服的帐篷，也不要被酒店坑，花很多钱。他们觉得，旅行的意义不是“住得好”，而是“玩得开心”。

好啦，我们来看看今天说的词吧：

“黄金周”是中国很重要的假期，因为假期长，人很多，生意也很好。

“订满”是说房间、票都没有了，比如：酒店订满了，火车票也订满了。

“被坑”意思是被别人骗了钱，比如酒店太贵了，就可以说：“我被酒店坑了。”

你怎么看呢？如果酒店太贵，你会选择住帐篷吗？欢迎给我们留言，说说你的看法。
translation:
Hello everyone! Welcome back to MaoMi Chinese!

Today’s episode is also supported by Maayot Chinese! It’s a Chinese learning app where you can memorise vocabulary, read news and articles, and study Chinese anytime, anywhere on your phone. If you’re interested, go and give it a try!

Last week was China’s Golden Week. So, what is “Golden Week”?

The first of October is China’s National Day. Every year on this day, the whole country has a public holiday, and many people get seven days off work. That’s why we call it “Golden Week”. Because it’s a long break, and it’s in autumn when the weather is pleasant, lots of people choose to travel.

However, in recent years, hotels across China have become extremely expensive during National Day. Rooms that normally cost two or three hundred yuan per night can go up to over one or even two thousand yuan during Golden Week. In some places, hotels are fully booked very early on. “Fully booked” means that there are no rooms left, no train tickets left, and so on.

So, many young people have come up with a new idea. When they travel during Golden Week, they bring their own tents.

You might think they’re going camping, but actually, they’re not. They’re not camping in the mountains — they’re pitching tents in cities, just outside tourist attractions, and sometimes even near train stations. On social media, you can see lots of photos: some people sleeping in car parks, some on grassy areas, and some right by the entrance of scenic spots. They go sightseeing during the day and rest in their tents at night.

Some people who see these photos think it looks a bit tough, but young people don’t seem to mind. They actually find it quite fun and feel a sense of freedom. They don’t need to worry about expensive hotels or rooms being fully booked. With a tent, they can sleep anywhere.

One person online said, “I’d rather sleep in a tent than be ripped off by a hotel.” The phrase “be ripped off” means to be cheated or overcharged. Another said, “Sleeping in a tent might be a bit tiring, but it’s really good fun. At night, we chat, eat instant noodles, and look at the stars — it’s lovely.”

Some people also say that young people nowadays want to save money. They’d rather sleep in an uncomfortable tent than spend a fortune on hotels. They believe that the point of travelling isn’t to stay somewhere luxurious, but to enjoy yourself and have a good time.

Alright, let’s take a look at some of today’s words:

“Golden Week” is a very important holiday in China — because it’s long, crowded, and great for business.

“Fully booked” means that all rooms or tickets are sold out. For example: “The hotel is fully booked,” or “The train tickets are fully booked.”

“To be ripped off” means to be overcharged or cheated, for example: “The hotel was so expensive, I felt I was ripped off.”

What do you think? If hotel prices were too high, would you choose to sleep in a tent? Leave us a message and share your thoughts!

title: #233 The First Full 24 Hours in a Hotel in China 24小时退房酒店
transcript:
大家好，欢迎回来MaoMi Chinese！

今天的播客也要谢谢Maayot Chinese的支持！用Maayot Chinese，我们可以随时随地记单词，看中文的文章。如果有正在准备HSK考试的朋友，这个app就更方便了。感兴趣的话，赶快试一试吧！

最近，我去了日本旅游。旅游的时候，我常常住酒店，一般下午三点入住，第二天11点退房。算起来，其实还没有二十四个小时。在中国住酒店，我们一般下午两点入住，第二天中午11点或者12点退房，也没有二十四个小时。如果退房晚了，我们就需要多付钱。

上个月，在中国的一个城市，武汉，有一家酒店做了一个新的尝试。他们开始了“二十四小时退房制”。意思是，我们什么时候入住，就可以在第二天什么时候退房，可以住二十四个小时。比如，我们晚上九点入住，第二天晚上九点再退房，也可以。你觉得这个二十四小时退房制怎么样？

酒店的老板说，很多客人都觉得很方便，他们不用早早起床退房，可以慢慢收拾东西。在社交媒体上，网友们看到新闻后也有讨论。有的人说，“太好了，这才是真正为客人着想！”也有人说，“如果所有酒店都这样，打扫房间的员工会很辛苦吧。”也有人觉得，这样虽然好，但是也可能让下一个客人等很久。一些酒店的老板说，他们也可以用24小时退房制，但是客人要付更多钱，因为打扫更麻烦了。

但是，总的来说，很多人都希望更多酒店能这样做。他们都觉得，我们住酒店是为了工作或者旅游，如果能多休息一会儿，就多一点幸福。

你觉得呢？如果下次你住酒店，你愿不愿意多花一点钱，住24小时退房制的酒店？你觉得这样是对的吗？欢迎给我们留言，和我们分享！
translation:
Hello everyone, and welcome back to MaoMi Chinese!

Today’s episode is also supported by Maayot Chinese! With Maayot Chinese, you can learn new words and read Chinese articles anytime, anywhere. If you’re preparing for the HSK exam, this app is even more useful. If you’re interested, give it a try!

Recently, I went travelling in Japan. When I travel, I often stay in hotels. Usually, I can check in at 3 p.m. and have to check out at 11 a.m. the next day. So actually, I don’t even stay for a full 24 hours. In China, it’s quite similar — we usually check in at 2 p.m. and check out at 11 or 12 the next day, still not a full 24 hours. If we check out late, we have to pay extra.

Last month, in Wuhan, a city in China, one hotel tried something new. They introduced a “24-hour check-out policy”. This means that no matter when you check in, you can stay for a full 24 hours. For example, if you check in at 9 p.m., you can check out at 9 p.m. the next day. What do you think about this idea?

The hotel owner said that many guests found it very convenient. They didn’t have to get up early to check out and could take their time packing. On social media, many people were also discussing this news. Some said, “That’s great! This really shows care for the guests!” Others said, “If all hotels do this, it’ll be really tiring for the cleaning staff.” Some also thought that although the idea is good, it might make the next guest wait longer. Some hotel owners said they could also offer the 24-hour check-out system, but guests would need to pay more, as cleaning and room turnover would take more time.

Overall, though, many people hope more hotels will try this system. They said that when we stay in hotels, it’s usually for work or travel, and if we can rest a bit longer, we’ll feel a bit happier.

What do you think? If you stay in a hotel next time, would you be willing to pay a bit more for a 24-hour stay? Do you think that’s fair? Leave us a comment and share your thoughts!

title: #234 Burning Corn: Creativity or Waste? 玉米燃料是浪费吗？
transcript:
大家好，欢迎回来 MaoMi Chinese！

今天也要谢谢Maayot Chinese的支持！如果你也喜欢一边读中文的文章一边学很多词语，你就可以试试Maayot Chinese的网站或者app。这里有很多的中文文章，每一天读一点，进步就会更快。如果你感兴趣，去试试看吧！

你喜欢吃烤肉吗？中国人很喜欢吃烤肉，在中国也有很多烤肉店。最近，有一家烤肉店，因为他们用玉米做燃料，被很多网友骂了。燃料，也就是用来燃烧的材料，比如木头，炭，等等。这家店用的燃料是玉米。

这家店在网上发了一个视频，视频里可以看到，烤肉的火下面放的不是木头，也不是炭，而是一根根黄色的玉米。火在烧，玉米“噼里啪啦”地响，看起来很特别。

店家说，他们这样做是因为玉米烧得更干净。用玉米烤肉，肉会有一点甜味，更香。他们还说，用的玉米不是人吃的那种，而是 “陈化粮”，也就是放久了、不能很好吃的玉米。他们觉得这样做既环保又有特色。

但是，很多网友不同意。有人觉得，这样做是在浪费粮食。现在大家都在说要节约粮食，你们却拿玉米来烧火，这样看起来不太好。还有人说，农民种玉米很辛苦，玉米是粮食，不应该拿来当燃料。不过，也有人支持这家店。他们说，这不一定是浪费。可能他们还帮了很多农民，买了他们的玉米。

很多人都在社交媒体上讨论这个事。有人说要节约粮食，有人说他们帮助了农民。烤肉店后来也说，他们没有浪费粮食，只是用了不能吃的玉米。

这件事让我们也想一想：什么是浪费？在生活里，我们是不是有时候也太快去批评别人了？你怎么看呢？欢迎给我们留言，和我们分享哦！
translation:
Hello everyone, and welcome back to MaoMi Chinese!

Today, we’d like to say a big thank you to Maayot Chinese for supporting this episode! If you enjoy learning new words while reading Chinese stories, you should definitely check out Maayot’s website or app. There are lots of short Chinese articles there — if you read a little every day, your Chinese will improve much faster. If you’re interested, give it a try!

Do you like barbecue? Chinese people love eating barbecue, and there are many barbecue restaurants across the country. Recently, one of these restaurants has become very controversial online because they used corn as fuel. Fuel means material that’s used for burning — for example, wood or charcoal. But this restaurant used corn instead.

They posted a video on social media showing their cooking fire. Under the grill, you could see not wood or charcoal, but rows of yellow corn cobs. The fire was burning, and the corn was crackling — it looked quite special.

The restaurant owner said they used corn because it burns more cleanly. They also said that meat grilled over corn fire has a light sweetness and a better aroma. According to them, the corn they used wasn’t for eating — it was old stock corn, which means it had been stored for a long time and was no longer suitable for food. They believed this method was both environmentally friendly and unique.

However, many people online disagreed. Some said it was a waste of food. Nowadays, people often talk about saving food, yet this restaurant was using corn as fuel — which didn’t seem right. Others pointed out that farmers work very hard to grow corn, and as it’s an important food crop, it shouldn’t be burned as fuel.

But some people supported the restaurant. They argued that it wasn’t necessarily wasteful — maybe the restaurant even helped local farmers by buying their old corn.

The debate spread quickly across social media. Some said we must save food, while others thought the restaurant’s practice actually supported farmers. Later, the restaurant responded, saying they hadn’t wasted any food — they had only used corn that wasn’t suitable for eating.

This story also makes us think: what does it really mean to waste something? And in our daily lives, do we sometimes criticise others too quickly before understanding the full story? What do you think? Feel free to leave us a comment and share your thoughts!

title: #235 Where Do Chinese People Like to Immigrate To?中国人移民喜欢去哪儿？
transcript:
大家好，欢迎回来 MaoMi Chinese！

今天的播客也要谢谢Maayot Chinese的支持！ 在Maayot Chinese的app，我们可以记单词，读文章，听文章，了解中国的社会和文化。在手机上下载就可以用。如果你感兴趣，就去试试看吧！

你的国家有很多移民吗？移民，就是从别的国家来的人。移民不是游客，他们是从别的国家来，但是到这个国家生活的人。很多国家都有中国人的移民。中国人都移民去了哪里？今天，我们就来聊一聊吧！

第一名当然是美国，大约有三分之一的中国移民去了那里。为什么呢？因为美国大学多，很多中国人去美国上大学，上完大学就留下来工作。也有一些人觉得，美国的机会多、生活自由，所以在那里生活。

第二名是韩国，有百分之十一点六的中国移民去了韩国。韩国离中国很近，文化也比较像。在中国也有一些人是朝鲜族，朝鲜语和韩语一样，所以他们去韩国上学、工作、做生意、生活，非常方便。

第三名是日本，有百分之十一点二。日本的生活很安全，环境干净，教育也不错。很多中国学生喜欢去日本留学，也有人去工作，比如做IT、做翻译、或者开餐馆。

接下来是加拿大和澳大利亚，加拿大有百分之十点一，澳大利亚有百分之九点四。这两个国家空气好，环境美，社会也比较安全。很多中国家庭为了更好的生活，会选择去那边生活。

在亚洲，还有一个很受欢迎的地方，那就是新加坡。新加坡华人多，说中文很方便，生活水平高，社会也很安全。

在欧洲，中国移民去得比较多的国家是意大利、英国、西班牙、法国和德国。虽然人数没有那么多，但也有很多中国人开餐馆、做生意、或者上学。

那你觉得，中国人为什么喜欢移民呢？有人是为了孩子的教育，有人是为了生活环境，还有人只是想去看看不同的世界。其实不管去哪里，我们都带着中国文化，带着家的味道。所以在纽约、东京、悉尼，你都能看到中国餐馆、中文学校，还有春节的红灯笼。

这就是中国人，走到哪里，家就在哪里。

你想移民去别的国家吗？你想去哪儿呢？欢迎给我们留言，和我们分享哦！
translation:
Hello everyone, and welcome back to MaoMi Chinese!

Today’s episode is once again sponsored by Maayot Chinese! On the Maayot Chinese app, you can learn new words, read articles, listen to stories, and discover more about Chinese society and culture. You can simply download the app on your phone and start using it. If you’re interested, go and give it a try!

Does your country have many immigrants? Immigrants are people who come from another country to live in your country. They’re not tourists — they don’t just visit for a short time, but move to live there. Many countries around the world have Chinese immigrants. So, where have Chinese people moved to? Let’s talk about that today!

The top destination, of course, is the United States, where about one-third of Chinese immigrants have gone. Why? Because there are many universities in America. Many Chinese people go there to study, and after graduation, they stay to work. Some also think that the U.S. offers more opportunities and freedom, so they choose to live there.

In second place is South Korea, with 11.6% of Chinese immigrants. Korea is very close to China, and the culture is quite similar. There are also ethnic Koreans in China, whose language is the same as Korean, so for them, studying, working, doing business, or living in South Korea is very convenient.

Third is Japan, with 11.2%. Life in Japan is safe, the environment is clean, and the education system is good. Many Chinese students like to study there. Some also go for work — for example, in IT, translation, or running restaurants.

Next are Canada and Australia. Canada has 10.1%, and Australia 9.4% of Chinese immigrants. Both countries have clean air, beautiful environments, and relatively safe societies. Many Chinese families move there for a better life, or for their children’s education.

In Asia, there’s another very popular destination — Singapore. There are many Chinese people in Singapore, so speaking Chinese is easy. The standard of living is high, and the society is safe and well organised.

In Europe, the countries with the most Chinese immigrants are Italy, the UK, Spain, France, and Germany. The numbers aren’t as high as in other regions, but many Chinese people there run restaurants, do business, or study.

So, why do Chinese people like to immigrate? Some do it for their children’s education, some for a better living environment, and others simply want to see more of the world. But no matter where we go, we always bring our culture with us — the feeling of home never disappears. That’s why, whether you’re in New York, Tokyo, or Sydney, you can always find Chinese restaurants, Chinese schools, and red lanterns during Spring Festival.

That’s what Chinese people are like — wherever we go, home goes with us.

Would you like to move to another country one day? Where would you like to go? Leave us a message and share your thoughts!

title: #236 Why Everyone in China Knows this Tibetan man? 藏族男孩丁真
transcript:
大家好，欢迎回来 MaoMi Chinese！

今天的podcast也要谢谢Maayot Chinese的支持！ 这是一个可以看和可以听的中文学习app，上面还有一些老师会给你feedback。如果你正在准备考试，或者想提高中文，那你可以试试这个app！

今天我们来聊一个中国很特别的人,他的名字叫丁真。你可能听过他的名字。他不是明星，也不是歌手，但是他因为一张笑脸，在全中国都很有名。

丁真是中国四川省一个藏族男孩，他住在一个叫理塘的小地方。藏族是一个少数民族，藏族人说藏语，所以，那时候的丁真还不太会说汉语。理塘有很高的山，很蓝的天，还有很多牦牛。几年前，有工作人员在理塘拍视频，他们拍到了一个骑马的男孩，他笑得很干净、很自然。这个男孩就是丁真。视频发到网上以后，很多人看到后都因为他的笑容很感动。大家都说，这个笑容太真、太美了！

很快，丁真变成了网络红人。他的名字上了热搜，理塘这个小地方也因为他变得很有名了。后来，理塘政府邀请他工作，让他做“旅游形象代言人”，也就是代表理塘，拍视频、宣传家乡。因为他，很多人去理塘旅游，理塘的经济也越来越好。

但是，过了一段时间，人们开始讨论丁真。有的人开始不喜欢他。他们觉得丁真其实没有做什么特别的事情，只是因为长得帅就出名。有的人说，他说汉语也说得不好，不知道为什么这么多人喜欢他。当然，也有很多人喜欢他。他们说，丁真只是一个普通的年轻人，他没有做错什么。他只是笑了，然后他的生活就不一样了。

在网络上红了以后，丁真开始学汉语，他的汉语也越来越好了。我们来听一听他的一个采访吧：

A：那么现在活得怎么样呢？好不好？

丁真：现在活得……现在我理解了人生，我也觉得活到自己想要的那种样子。因为我觉得人不能活在别人指挥的那种……

A：就是这个道理。

丁真：对然后就我想活到……活成我自己，可以指挥我自己的人生。

有人问丁真，现在活得怎么样，也就是现在的生活好不好，丁真说，他理解了人生，可以活成自己想要的样子，不用听别人的指挥，也就是不用管别人说的话，可以做他自己。

其实，丁真今年只有24岁，他在网上火了的时候只有19岁。只有5年，他的人生完全不一样了。我觉得，他可以说出这样的话，非常了不起。

你呢？如果有一天你突然在网上火了，你会喜欢这样的生活吗？欢迎给我们留言，说说你的想法！
translation:
Hello everyone, and welcome back to MaoMi Chinese!

Today’s episode is kindly supported by Maayot Chinese — an app where you can both read and listen to Chinese stories. There are even teachers who give you personalised feedback! If you’re preparing for an exam or just want to improve your Chinese, you might want to give this app a try.

Today, we’re going to talk about a very special person in China. His name is Ding Zhen. You might have heard of him. He’s not a celebrity or a singer, but he became famous all across China — simply because of one smile.

Ding Zhen is a Tibetan boy from Sichuan Province in China. He lives in a small place called Litang. Tibetans are one of China’s ethnic minorities, and they speak the Tibetan language, so at that time, Ding Zhen couldn’t speak much Chinese yet. Litang is surrounded by tall mountains, blue skies, and many yaks.

A few years ago, some staff were filming a video in Litang when they came across a young boy on horseback. He had a clean, natural smile — that boy was Ding Zhen. After the video was uploaded online, many people were deeply moved by his smile. Everyone said, “This smile is so pure, so beautiful!”

Soon, Ding Zhen became an internet sensation. His name appeared on the trending lists, and the small town of Litang became famous because of him. Later, the local government invited him to work as a tourism ambassador, representing Litang by filming videos and promoting his hometown. Thanks to him, many people started visiting Litang, and its local economy grew stronger.

But after some time, people began to talk more critically about Ding Zhen. Some started to dislike him. They felt he hadn’t done anything particularly special — that he became famous just because of his looks. Others said his Chinese wasn’t very good, and they didn’t understand why so many people liked him. Of course, there were still plenty of people who supported him. They said Ding Zhen was just an ordinary young man who hadn’t done anything wrong. He simply smiled, and his life completely changed.

After becoming famous online, Ding Zhen started learning Chinese, and his Chinese improved a lot. Let’s listen to a short clip from one of his interviews:

A: So, how is life now? Is it good?

Ding Zhen: Now I understand life. I think I’m living the way I want to. I don’t think people should live under other people’s control…

A: That’s right.

Ding Zhen: Yes, I want to live as myself, and be the one in charge of my own life.

Someone asked Ding Zhen how his life is now — whether he’s happy. Ding Zhen said that he now understands life and can live the way he wants, without following what others tell him to do. In other words, he’s learned to be himself.

Actually, Ding Zhen is only 24 years old. When he became famous online, he was just 19. In only five years, his life has completely changed. I think it’s really impressive that he can now speak about life in such a thoughtful way.

And what about you? If one day you suddenly became famous online, would you enjoy that kind of life? Feel free to leave us a comment and share your thoughts!

title: #237 Leftovers for 120 Cats 剩菜养活120只流浪猫
transcript:
大家好！欢迎回来 MaoMi Chinese！

首先我们再一次谢谢Maayot Chinese的支持。他们的网站能看，能听，能说，能写，是一个学习中文的好工具，也非常方便。如果你感兴趣，赶快去试试吧！

今天我想跟大家聊一个最近中国很火的故事。故事的主角叫“宣宣”。她有一点“社恐”，意思是不太敢跟陌生人说话，会紧张。但是为了家里的小动物，她做了一件很勇敢的事情。

三年前的冬天，“宣宣”在外面看到一只很瘦的小“流浪猫”，就是没有家、在外面生活的猫。她觉得很可怜，就把它带回家。后来，她又捡到了第二只、第三只……慢慢地，从一两只变成很多很多只。现在，她家里已经有一百二十多只流浪猫了。她的家变成了猫咪的家。

每天养这么多猫，需要很多钱。每天光是食物就要三百多块。“宣宣”做兼职，还拍视频，但是压力还是很大。

有一天，她去参加“婚宴”，就是新人的结婚晚宴。她发现桌子上的菜很多都没有吃，但是很快就被收走了。她突然想到：“这些剩菜可以带回去吗？”“剩菜”就是别人没吃完但还很干净的饭菜。

于是她鼓起勇气，走到新郎和新娘面前，小声地说：“你好，我能不能把剩菜打包一下？我要带回家喂流浪猫。”这句话，她现在已经说了快一百次了。大部分新人听到以后都很支持她。有的人还请她一起坐下来吃饭。但是她一般都会很礼貌地说不，她只会给一百元，说：“这是小猫交的饭钱。”

网友看到以后很感动，说：“小猫也是被请的小客人呀。”

“宣宣”大概每十天会去一次婚宴。最多的时候，她可以带回六七十斤干净的鸡肉、鱼、虾。她回家以后，会把这些菜洗一下，去油、去盐，让猫可以安全地吃。这样不仅减少了食物浪费，也帮她省钱。

后来，她把这些经历拍成视频，放到网上。没想到，非常火。有一条视频有五千万播放，一百五十多万点赞。很多网友请她来参加自己的婚礼。

三年时间，一个害羞的女孩，变成了勇敢的猫妈妈。她希望更多人可以关心身边的流浪动物，也希望大家在养宠物之前一定要想清楚，要负责任。因为每一只猫、每一只狗，都是很重要的生命。

好啦，我们先来听听今天聊的词吧：

社恐：意思是害怕社交，不敢跟陌生人说话。

流浪猫：意思是没有家、在外面生活的猫。

剩菜：意思是别人没吃完、但还很干净的饭菜。

婚宴：意思是新人的结婚晚宴。

今天的MaoMi Chinese就先到这里。你怎么看宣宣的故事呢？欢迎给我们留言，和我们分享！
translation:
Hello everyone! Welcome back to MaoMi Chinese!

First of all, we’d like to thank Maayot Chinese once again for their support. On their website you can read, listen, speak and write — it’s a really useful and convenient tool for learning Chinese. If you’re interested, go and give it a try!

Today I want to share with you a story that has recently become very popular in China. The main character is a young woman called “Xuanxuan”. She has a bit of “social anxiety”, meaning she gets nervous and finds it difficult to talk to strangers. But for the sake of the animals in her home, she did something incredibly brave.

Three winters ago, Xuanxuan saw a very thin little stray cat outside — a cat with no home, living on the streets. She felt sorry for it and took it home. Later, she found another one, then a third… and slowly, one or two cats became many, many more. Now, she has more than 120 stray cats living in her home, and her house has basically turned into a big cat shelter.

Feeding so many cats every day costs a lot of money. Food alone costs over 300 yuan a day. Xuanxuan does part-time work and makes videos, but the pressure is still huge.

One day, she went to a wedding banquet — the dinner party at a wedding. She noticed that a lot of the food on the tables hadn’t really been touched, but was quickly taken away. Suddenly she thought, “Can I take these leftovers home?” Leftovers means food that people didn’t finish, but is still clean and safe to eat.

So she gathered her courage, walked up to the bride and groom, and quietly said, “Hello, would it be alright if I packed up the leftovers? I’d like to take them home to feed my stray cats.” She has now said this sentence nearly a hundred times. Most newlyweds are very supportive when they hear her story. Some even invite her to sit down and eat with them. But she usually politely declines. She simply gives 100 yuan and says, “This is the cats’ meal money.”

Many people online were really touched when they saw this. Some said, “The cats are also little guests invited to the wedding!”

Xuanxuan now goes to a wedding banquet roughly once every ten days. On the busiest days, she can take home 30 to 35 kilograms of clean chicken, fish and prawns. After returning home, she washes everything, removes the oil and salt, and prepares it so the cats can eat safely. This not only reduces food waste but also helps her save a significant amount of money.

Later, she filmed her experiences and posted them online. She didn’t expect them to go viral — but they did. One video has 50 million views and more than 1.5 million likes. Many people even invite her to their weddings on purpose.

In three years, a shy girl has become a brave “cat mum”. She hopes that more people will pay attention to stray animals around them, and that anyone who wants to keep a pet will think carefully and take responsibility. Because every cat and every dog is a life that matters.

Alright, let’s now listen to today’s key words:

社恐 (shèkǒng): social anxiety; being afraid of social situations or talking to strangers.

流浪猫 (liúlàng māo): stray cat; a cat with no home.

剩菜 (shèngcài): leftovers; food that wasn’t finished but is still clean.

婚宴 (hūnyàn): wedding banquet; the meal at a wedding.

This is all about MaoMi Chinese today! What’s your thought on this story? Leave us a comment, and share with us!

title: #238 Why Are Blind Boxes So Popular in China? 为什么盲盒这么受欢迎？
transcript:
大家好，欢迎回来MaoMi Chinese！

今天我们聊一个很有趣的东西：盲盒。你知道什么是盲盒吗？盲盒就是你买的时候不知道里面是什么的盒子。可能是一只玩偶，也可能是小玩具，就是买的时候看不到买了什么。最近，盲盒在中国很受欢迎，这是为什么呢？今天我们一起来聊聊吧！

第一个原因是惊喜，也就是不知道会发生什么，很开心。你不知道里面是什么，每次开盒子都有小小的期待和开心。就像拆礼物一样，很好玩。第二个原因是可以收藏，也就是把喜欢的东西收起来，用来看或者玩。很多盲盒有一套不同的东西，有的人想收集全套，有的人只收集自己喜欢的东西。第三个原因是社交，也就是和别人一起玩或者聊天。开盲盒的时候，大家会互相分享，还可以交换，这样可以认识新朋友，很开心。

说到盲盒，中国有很多有名的盲盒。最有名的是泡泡玛特盲盒，它的玩偶很可爱，每次开盒子都很惊喜。也有一些特别有趣的盲盒，比如“剩菜盲盒”，有点像“Too Good To Go”。有一些餐厅卖不完饭菜，就会做成剩菜盲盒。剩菜盲盒比较便宜，但是买的人不知道里面有什么样的剩菜。

有的人开盲盒会很高兴，也有人开了很多次还是没有得到自己想要的，有点小失望，这也是盲盒的乐趣。不过盲盒也有问题。有人会花太多钱，只为了收集玩偶，有些玩偶很快就不值钱。所以买盲盒的时候，要管好自己的钱包。

总的来说，盲盒是惊喜、收藏和社交，现在在中国很多年轻人都喜欢买盲盒。好啦，我们来说说今天学了什么词语吧：

盲盒，就是一个盒子，但是我们买的时候不知道里面是什么。

惊喜，就是不知道会发生什么，但是很开心。

收藏，也就是把我们喜欢的东西收起来，用来看或者玩。

你喜欢买盲盒吗？你觉得买盲盒是一种乐趣，还是浪费钱呢？欢迎给我们留言，说说你的看法！
translation:
Hello everyone and welcome back to MaoMi Chinese!

Today we’re talking about something very interesting: blind boxes. Do you know what a blind box is? A blind box is a box where you don’t know what’s inside when you buy it. It might be a little figurine, or a small toy — you simply can’t see what you’re buying until you open it. Recently, blind boxes have become very popular in China. Why is that? Let’s talk about it today!

The first reason is the surprise — meaning you don’t know what’s going to happen, and that makes you happy. You don’t know what’s inside, so every time you open a box, you feel a bit of excitement and joy. It’s like opening a present — it’s great fun. The second reason is collecting — meaning you keep the things you like so you can look at them or play with them. Many blind boxes come in a whole series. Some people want to collect the entire set, while others only want the ones they personally like. The third reason is socialising — meaning you play or chat with other people. When people open blind boxes, they often share what they got, and they can even trade with each other. It’s a good way to meet new friends, and it’s enjoyable too.

Speaking of blind boxes, there are many famous ones in China. The most popular is the Pop Mart blind box — the figurines are very cute, and opening one always feels exciting. There are also some very interesting blind boxes, such as “leftover food blind boxes”, which are a bit like “Too Good To Go”. Some restaurants turn food they didn’t manage to sell into a leftover-food blind box. These boxes are cheaper, but you still don’t know what kind of leftover food you’ll get.

Some people feel very happy when they open blind boxes, while others open many and still don’t get the one they want, so they feel a bit disappointed. But that’s also part of the fun.

However, blind boxes also have problems. Some people spend too much money just to collect figurines, and some figurines lose their value very quickly. So when you buy blind boxes, you need to look after your wallet.

Overall, blind boxes bring surprise, collecting, and socialising, and many young people in China really enjoy buying them.

Alright, let’s look at the new words we learned today:

盲盒Blind box – a box where you don’t know what’s inside when you buy it.

惊喜Surprise – not knowing what will happen, but feeling happy.

收藏Collecting – keeping things you like so you can look at them or play with them.

Do you like buying blind boxes? Do you think they’re fun, or do you think they’re a waste of money? Feel free to leave us a message and tell us what you think!

title: #239 A Brit in China’s Kitchen 做中国菜的英国人
transcript:
大家好，欢迎回来 MaoMi Chinese！

今天我想跟大家介绍一个非常特别的人，她的中文名字叫扶霞，英文名字是 Fuchsia Dunlop。她是一个英国人，但是很多中国人都说，她可能比中国人更了解中国菜。为什么呢？她的故事真的很有意思。

扶霞在英国长大。她小时候，不太了解中国。大学的时候，她第一次来到中国，那是1990年代的事情了。那个时候的中国和现在不一样，生活简单，外国人也不多。但是在那一次旅行，她爱上了中国菜，她觉得中国菜实在是太好吃了、太丰富了、太神奇了。她吃到了以前从来没吃过的味道，也看到了完全不同的做饭的方式。她一下子就爱上了。

后来，她决定不只是吃，还要真正了解中国菜。于是，她做了一件非常勇敢的事：她去了中国四川成都，进了一个厨师学校。她是这个学校里第一个外国学生。每天她都和中国厨师，和中国学生一起学习做中国菜。她每天都努力练习，比如切很细很细的丝，用很重的锅炒菜，等等。她说，中国的厨房让她感觉像进了一个新的世界。

扶霞不仅会做中国菜，她还写了很多本书，介绍她看到的、学到的、吃到的东西。她的书不仅介绍中国菜，也介绍中国的文化和人。这些书在西方非常有名，也帮很多外国人第一次真正了解中国菜和中国文化。

很多中国人说，她是“中国菜最好的外国朋友”。她尊重中国的传统，尊重中国厨师的智慧，也努力让全世界看到，中国菜不是“外卖店里的炒饭和炒面”，而是一个非常有历史的文化。

我特别喜欢她的一句话：“如果你想了解一个国家，你一定要了解它的食物。”

希望你们也喜欢今天的故事。你最喜欢的中国菜是什么？欢迎给我们留言，和我们分享！
translation:
Hello everyone, welcome back to MaoMi Chinese!

Today I want to introduce someone very special. Her Chinese name is Fuxia, and her English name is Fuchsia Dunlop. She’s British, but many Chinese people say she might understand Chinese cuisine even better than we do. Why? Her story is truly fascinating.

Fuchsia grew up in the UK. When she was young, she didn’t know much about China. It was only when she was at university that she came to China for the first time, back in the 1990s. China then was very different from today — life was simple, and there weren’t many foreigners. But during that trip, she completely fell in love with Chinese food. She thought Chinese cuisine was unbelievably delicious, incredibly rich, and full of surprises. She tried flavours she had never tasted before, and she saw cooking techniques that were completely new to her. She fell in love instantly.

Later, she decided she didn’t just want to eat Chinese food — she wanted to understand it properly. So she did something very brave: she went to Chengdu in Sichuan, China, and enrolled in a professional chef school. She was the first foreign student in the entire school. Every day, she learned Chinese cooking alongside Chinese chefs and Chinese students. She practised hard every day — cutting vegetables into extremely thin shreds, stir-frying with heavy woks, and so on. She said that being in a Chinese kitchen felt like entering a whole new world.

Fuchsia can cook Chinese food very well, but she also writes books about what she has seen, learned, and tasted. Her books don’t just talk about Chinese dishes, but also about Chinese culture and the people she met. These books are very famous in the West and have helped many foreigners truly understand Chinese cuisine and Chinese culture for the first time.

Many Chinese people say she is “the best foreign friend of Chinese cuisine”. She respects Chinese traditions, respects the wisdom of Chinese chefs, and works hard to show the world that Chinese cuisine is not just “fried rice and chow mein from takeaway shops”, but a culture with deep history and meaning.

There’s one sentence of hers that I especially like:“If you want to understand a country, you must understand its food.”

I hope you enjoyed today’s story as well. What’s your favourite Chinese dish? Feel free to leave a comment and share it with us!

title: #240 The Chinese Dubbing of Zootopia 2 Caused Debate 中文配音引争议
transcript:
大家好，欢迎回来 MaoMi Chinese！

最近很多人都在电影院看Zootopia 2，中文名叫《疯狂动物城2》在中国，也有非常多的人喜欢这部电影。可是，很多人说他们不喜欢这部电影的中文配音。配音，也就是给电影或者电视剧加上声音。今天我们来聊一聊《疯狂动物城2》的中文配音。为什么大家会这样说呢？

在电影里，有一些角色是明星配音。很多网友一听，就觉得不对劲。“不对劲”，也就是听起来怪怪的。有人说自己“出戏”，也就是你在看电影，但是你脑子里想到的不是角色，而是那个明星。比如，你明明看到的是一只动物，但是一听声音，你想到的是明星上节目、拍广告的样子。这样大家就很难专心看电影。

为什么大家不喜欢明星配音呢？第一，很多明星的声音太有名了。也就是他们一开口，你马上就知道是谁。大家就会想：“哦，这是那个明星”，而不是“这是电影里的角色”。这样，我们看电影的时候会出戏。

第二，很多网友觉得明星的配音不自然。“不自然”，也就是听起来不像真的在说话，更像在读书本上的句子。专业的配音演员会用声音表现开心、生气、害怕这些感觉。但是明星可能没有训练过，所以他们的声音听起来平平的，没有特别的感觉。

第三，现在中国观众对动画电影越来越认真。他们希望角色听起来像角色本身，而不是像一个明星。如果角色是一个活泼的小动物，声音就应该活泼一点。如果角色是一个冷静的大角色，声音要冷静一点。但是有时候明星的声音和角色差很远，所以网友就会觉得“不合适。”

每次有电影用明星配音，网友都会讨论。有人说明星可以让更多人来看电影。但也有很多网友说：“配音应该请真正会配音的人。”

好啦，我们来复习一下今天学的词：

配音，也就是给电影或者电视剧加上声音。

不对劲，也就是听起来怪怪的。

出戏，也就是你看到角色，但是想到的是别的东西。

不自然，也就是听起来不像真的在说话。

不合适，也就是和角色不一样。

你有没有看过一部动画片，一听到声音就觉得怪怪的？你也可以在网站给我们留言！
translation:
Hello everyone, welcome back to MaoMi Chinese!

Recently, lots of people have been watching Zootopia 2 in the cinema. In China, the film is called 《疯狂动物城2》, and many people really like it. However, quite a few people say they don’t like the Chinese dubbing of the film. Dubbing means adding voices to a film or TV show. Today, we’re going to talk about the Chinese dubbing of Zootopia 2. Why are people saying this?

In the film, some of the characters are voiced by celebrities. Many internet users say that as soon as they hear the voices, something feels “not right”, meaning it sounds a bit strange. Some people say they feel “taken out of the story”, meaning that when they watch the film, they don’t think about the character—they think about the celebrity. For example, you’re clearly looking at an animal on screen, but when you hear the voice, you think of the celebrity on TV shows or in adverts. This makes it hard for people to concentrate on the film.

Why don’t people like celebrities doing voice acting? Firstly, many celebrities’ voices are too well-known. That means the moment they start speaking, you instantly know who it is. People think, “Oh, that’s that celebrity,” instead of “This is the character in the film.” And that takes the audience out of the story.

Secondly, many internet users feel that the celebrities’ voice acting doesn’t sound natural. “Not natural” means it doesn’t sound like real speech—it sounds more like reading words from a book. Professional voice actors use their voices to show emotions such as happiness, anger or fear. But celebrities might not have had this kind of training, so their voices can sound flat, without any special feeling.

Thirdly, Chinese audiences are taking animated films more and more seriously. They want characters to sound like the characters themselves, not like a famous person. If the character is a lively little animal, the voice should sound lively. If the character is calm and serious, the voice should sound calm. But sometimes the celebrity’s voice is very different from the character, so people feel it’s “not suitable”.

Whenever a film uses celebrities for dubbing, people start discussing it. Some say celebrities can attract more viewers to the film. But many others say, “Dubbing should be done by people who are truly skilled at it.”

Right, let’s review the new words from today:

不对劲 – this means something sounds strange or not quite right.
