title: #241 The Rise of Eating Alone in China 一人食
transcript:
大家好，欢迎回来 MaoMi Chinese！

今天我想和你聊一个最近在中国很流行的词，叫“一人食”。

一人食，其实意思很简单，就是一个人吃饭。一人食可以是一个人去餐厅，一个人点菜，一个人坐下来，慢慢吃。一人食也可以是一个人买了很多菜，在家里做很好吃的菜，在家慢慢吃。

在以前的中国，吃饭通常是很多人一起的。一家人一起吃，朋友一起吃，同事一起吃。吃饭是一件很热闹的事情。如果一个人去餐厅吃饭，有些人可能会觉得有点奇怪，甚至会想，这个人是不是很孤单，是不是没有人陪。

但是现在，情况慢慢变了。一人食在中国越来越常见，特别是在年轻人中。

原因有很多。一个很重要的原因是，大家的生活变得很快。工作很忙，下班时间也不一样，有时候真的很难找到时间和别人一起吃饭。那一人食，反而更简单。

还有一个原因是，很多人开始发现，一个人吃饭其实也很舒服。不用聊天，不用考虑别人想吃什么，也不用吃得很快。想吃什么就点什么，想吃多久就吃多久。

慢慢地，大家对“一个人”的看法也变了。一个人，不一定等于孤单。有时候，一个人只是想安静一下。

我在中国的时候，看到越来越多一人食的餐厅。有单人的座位，小小的桌子，不需要和别人拼桌。拼桌，也就是要和其他客人一起坐一个桌子。有些拉面店、火锅店，甚至一开始就是为了一人食设计的。

以前说到火锅、烧烤，很多人都会觉得，一定要一群人一起吃才有气氛。但现在，一个人吃火锅已经很正常了。一人一个小锅，不用分享，不用等别人，也不用想别人要吃什么。对很多人来说，这是一种自由。

所以，一人食并不是不喜欢别人，也不是没有朋友。很多时候，它只是一种选择。今天，我想一个人吃饭，就是这样。有时候，一人食也是一种和自己相处的方式。一天很忙，很多声音，很多人，说很多话。吃饭的时候，一个人安静下来，也是一种休息。

那你呢？你喜欢一个人吃饭吗？还是更喜欢和朋友一起？欢迎给我们留言，和我们分享哦！
translation:
Hello everyone, welcome back to MaoMi Chinese!

Today I’d like to talk to you about a word that has become very popular in China recently. It’s called “yī rén shí”, which means eating alone.

The idea of yī rén shí is actually very simple. It means one person eating a meal. It can be going to a restaurant on your own, ordering your own food, sitting down and eating slowly. It can also be buying lots of ingredients, cooking a nice meal at home, and enjoying it slowly by yourself.

In the past, in China, people usually ate together. Families ate together, friends ate together, colleagues ate together. Eating was a very lively, social activity. If someone went to a restaurant alone, some people might find it a bit strange, and even wonder whether that person was lonely or had no one to eat with.

But now, things are slowly changing. Eating alone is becoming more and more common in China, especially among young people.

There are many reasons for this. One very important reason is that life has become much faster. People are very busy at work, and everyone finishes work at different times. Sometimes it’s really hard to find time to eat with other people. In that case, eating alone actually becomes easier.

Another reason is that many people have started to realise that eating alone can be very comfortable. You don’t need to make conversation, you don’t need to think about what other people want to eat, and you don’t need to eat quickly. You can order whatever you want and take as long as you like.

Gradually, people’s views about being alone have also changed. Being alone doesn’t necessarily mean being lonely. Sometimes, being alone just means wanting a bit of quiet time.

When I was in China, I saw more and more restaurants that are friendly to people who eat alone. They have single seats and small tables, and you don’t need to share a table with strangers. Sharing a table means sitting at the same table as other customers. Some noodle shops and hotpot restaurants are even designed especially for people eating alone.

In the past, when people talked about hotpot or barbecues, many would say that you need a group of people for it to feel lively. But now, eating hotpot on your own has become very normal. One person, one small pot. You don’t need to share, you don’t need to wait for others, and you don’t need to think about what other people want to eat. For many people, this feels like freedom.

So eating alone doesn’t mean you don’t like other people, and it doesn’t mean you don’t have friends. Very often, it’s simply a choice. Today, I want to eat by myself — that’s all. Sometimes, eating alone is also a way of spending time with yourself. The day can be busy, with lots of noise, lots of people, and lots of talking. Sitting down to eat quietly on your own can actually be a kind of rest.

What about you? Do you like eating alone, or do you prefer eating with friends? Feel free to leave us a message and share your thoughts with us!

title: #242 Why Chinese old people love tour group? 为什么大爷大妈喜欢旅游团？
transcript:
大家好，欢迎回来 MaoMi Chinese！

你有没有见过中国的旅游团？很多时候，你会看见，中国旅游团里的人，大多是老人。我们也叫这些老人大爷大妈。他们很有活力，很有热情，但是他们就是喜欢在一个旅游团里，一共三十个人，四十个人，甚至五十个人一起旅游。旅游以前，他们都不认识。我们说这种是跟团旅游。为什么中国的大爷大妈喜欢跟团游呢？今天，我们一起来聊一聊吧！

第一个原因，其实是时间。很多年轻人要上班，要请假，时间不自由。老人退休了，也有退休金，时间比较多，什么时候想出去旅游都可以。但是，一个人去旅游太孤单了，对他们来说，跟团旅游很方便。

第二个原因是语言。很多老人不会说外语。他们想去旅游，但是又不敢一个人去旅游。一个人出国旅游，也会觉得很害怕。跟着中国旅游团，有导游，说中文，遇到问题也有人帮忙，心里会更放心。

还有一个原因是习惯。很多老人习惯有人安排好一切。吃什么，住哪里，去哪儿玩，都不用自己想。每天跟着计划走，对他们来说很轻松。

还有安全的问题。很多年轻人喜欢自由行。自由行，意思是不跟团旅游，自己想去哪儿就去哪儿，很自由，但是也有点麻烦。一些老人觉得，自由行很累，也会害怕迷路、生病或者不安全。旅游团人多，有导游，有很多中国人，他们会觉得更安全。

那为什么年轻人比较少跟团呢？因为很多年轻人更喜欢自由。他们会自己订机票、订酒店，想去哪儿就去哪儿，不想每天赶时间。赶时间，也就是做了一个事，去了一个地方，马上就要做下一个事，去下一个地方，非常忙。

你呢？你更喜欢跟团旅行，还是自由行？欢迎给我们留言，和我们分享哦！
translation:
Hello everyone, welcome back to MaoMi Chinese!

Have you ever seen a Chinese tour group? Very often, you’ll notice that most people in Chinese tour groups are older. In Chinese, we often call them dà yé and dà mā — uncles and aunties. They are full of energy and enthusiasm, and they really enjoy travelling in a tour group, sometimes with thirty, forty, or even fifty people. Before the trip, they don’t know each other at all. We call this kind of travel travelling with a tour group. So why do these Chinese uncles and aunties like group tours so much? Today, let’s talk about it together.

The first reason is actually time. Many young people have to work and need to take leave, so their time isn’t very flexible. Older people are retired, and they also receive a pension, so they have much more free time. They can travel whenever they want. But travelling alone can feel lonely, and for them, going with a tour group is very convenient.

The second reason is language. Many older people don’t speak foreign languages. They want to travel, but they don’t dare to travel on their own. Travelling abroad alone can also feel quite scary. When they join a Chinese tour group, there is a guide who speaks Chinese, and if there are any problems, someone is there to help. This makes them feel much more at ease.

Another reason is habit. Many older people are used to having everything arranged for them. What to eat, where to stay, and where to go are all planned, so they don’t need to think about it themselves. Following a daily schedule like this feels very easy for them.

There is also the issue of safety. Many young people like independent travel. Independent travel means not joining a tour group and going wherever you want, which feels very free, but can also be a bit troublesome. Some older people feel that independent travel is tiring, and they worry about getting lost, falling ill, or safety issues. In a tour group, there are many people, a guide, and lots of other Chinese travellers, so they feel safer.

So why do younger people join tour groups less often? Because many young people prefer freedom. They book their own flights and hotels, go wherever they want, and don’t like rushing every day. Rushing means finishing one thing, going to one place, and then immediately moving on to the next — always very busy.

What about you? Do you prefer travelling with a tour group, or travelling on your own? Feel free to leave us a message and share your thoughts with us!

title: #243 Walking the Line on Chinese Social Media擦边
transcript:
大家好，欢迎回来 MaoMi Chinese！

2025快要结束了。今年，有很多流行的中文词。今天，我想介绍一个最流行的词之一：擦边。

现在，社交媒体上的短视频越来越多。如果你会看中国的短视频，或者用微博、小红书，你可能见过这个词。什么是擦边呢？擦边是什么意思呢？

“擦”是轻轻碰一下，“边”是边界，也是规则。所以“擦边”就是碰到边界，但没有真的过边界。很多时候，我们说的 “擦边”，意思是：差一点坏了规则，但是还在规则里。

中国的社交媒体有很多规则。比如，不可以有色情的东西。在一些视频里，有人穿很少的衣服，跳很性感的舞。这些视频还是规则里，但是人们会说：这些是擦边视频。

有一个中国的前体操运动员在社交媒体抖音上发一些视频，视频里，她穿性感的裙子跳舞，有些网友喜欢她的视频，就会给她钱。后来，抖音关了她的账号，她再也不能赚钱了。很多人讨论这个事情，有人说：她只是擦边，没有破坏规则，不应该关她的账号。也有人说：擦边视频一样不好，应该关她的账号。总而言之，“擦边”不是完全对，也不是真的错，但是擦边非常接近规则和边界，有点危险。可是，也有很多人喜欢看擦边的东西。

中国的社交媒体对这些擦边的视频很严格。今年，抖音和小红书关了很多账号，这些账号都发过一些擦边的视频。有人说，这也是一个好事，因为很多孩子们也用社交媒体，不应该让孩子们看这些擦边的视频。也有人说，这样做太严格了，少了很多自由。

你怎么看呢？你觉得我们应该怎么看擦边视频呢？欢迎给我们留言，和我们分享！
translation:
Hello everyone, welcome back to MaoMi Chinese!

2025 is coming to an end. This year, there have been many popular Chinese words. Today, I’d like to introduce one of the most popular ones: “擦边”.

Nowadays, there are more and more short videos on social media. If you watch Chinese short videos, or use Weibo or Xiaohongshu, you may have seen this word before. So what is 擦边? What does it mean?

“擦” means to touch lightly, and “边” means a boundary, or a rule. So “擦边” means touching the boundary, but not really crossing it. Most of the time, when we say “擦边”, we mean: almost breaking the rules, but still staying within them.

There are many rules on Chinese social media. For example, sexual content is not allowed. In some videos, people wear very little clothing and dance in a very sexy way. These videos are still technically within the rules, but people will say: these are “擦边” videos.

There was a former Chinese gymnast who posted videos on Douyin. In her videos, she wore sexy dresses and danced. Some viewers liked her videos and even gave her money. Later, Douyin shut down her account, and she could no longer make money. Many people discussed this. Some said: she was only “擦边”, she didn’t break the rules, so her account shouldn’t have been closed. Others said: “擦边” videos are still bad, and her account should have been shut down. In short, “擦边” is not completely right, but it’s not completely wrong either. It is very close to the rules and the boundary, and it can be a bit risky. However, many people still enjoy watching “擦边” content.

Chinese social media platforms are quite strict about this kind of content. This year, Douyin and Xiaohongshu shut down many accounts that had posted “擦边” videos. Some people think this is a good thing, because many children use social media, and they shouldn’t be exposed to this kind of content. Others think this is too strict and takes away too much freedom.

What do you think? How do you think we should view “擦边” videos? Feel free to leave us a comment and share your thoughts!

title: #244 Why New Year Resolution fail 新年计划总失败?
transcript:
大家好！欢迎回来MaoMi Chinese！

首先祝大家新年快乐！我们结束了2025年，开始了2026年。我们的人生少了一年的时间，但是多了一年的故事。很多人都喜欢做新年计划，也就是New Year Resolution。去年的这个时候，你也做了新年计划吗？你的新年计划是什么？这些新年计划你都做到了吗？我去年做了一些新年计划，有些成功了，有些失败了。今天，我们就一起来聊聊新年计划吧！

我们在做新年计划的时候，总是有很多雄心壮志。雄心壮志是一个成语，意思是一些伟大的目标，也就是英文里的ambition。虽然做新年计划的时候，有很多雄心壮志，但是，真的做事情的时候，我们又常常觉得很难。后来，我们就不做了，新年计划也失败了。

比如，2025年1月1日，我的一个新年计划是：为了更健康，我要自己做饭，不吃外卖。我以为这个计划很简单，但是其实太难了。因为我每天在学校工作很忙，也很累，回家以后，我一点儿力气也没有，也不想做饭。我现在住在泰国曼谷，曼谷有非常多的餐厅，叫外卖太方便了，而且也不贵。所以，我在做这个计划的两个月以后，就失败了。

我开始想，应该怎么样做新年计划呢？我觉得，第一，做新年计划应该要具体，也就是很清楚地知道自己要做什么。比如，我今年的一个新年计划，是每个星期在家做饭至少两次。第二，做新年计划也要现实一点。比如，我知道自己工作很忙，每天都做饭不太现实，每天都去健身房也不太现实。所以，我今年的计划是：每个星期在家做饭至少两次，每个星期至少去健身房三次，每次锻炼三十分钟就可以了。第三，做新年计划也可以灵活，也就是有时候不做，也可以。比如，我今天去了骑自行车，那么我这个星期，如果太累了，就可以少去一次健身房。

你怎么看新年计划呢？你会做新年计划吗？你觉得我们应该怎么做新年计划呢？欢迎给我们留言，和我们分享哦！
translation:
Hello everyone! Welcome back to MaoMi Chinese!

First of all, I’d like to wish you all a Happy New Year! We have finished 2025 and started 2026. We have one year less of time in our lives, but one more year of stories. Many people like to make New Year’s resolutions. At this time last year, did you make any New Year’s resolutions? What were they? And did you manage to keep them? I made some New Year’s resolutions last year — some were successful, and some failed. Today, let’s talk about New Year’s resolutions together.

When we make New Year’s resolutions, we often have lots of big ambitions. “雄心壮志” is a Chinese idiom, meaning great goals — in English, ambition. Although we have many ambitions when we make plans, when it comes to actually doing them, we often feel that it’s very difficult. After a while, we give up, and our New Year’s resolutions fail.

For example, on 1 January 2025, one of my New Year’s resolutions was: to be healthier, I would cook for myself and not order takeaway. I thought this plan would be very easy, but in fact it was too hard. I work very busy days at school, and I’m very tired. When I get home, I have no energy at all and don’t want to cook. I live in Bangkok, Thailand, and there are so many restaurants here. Ordering takeaway is extremely convenient and not expensive. So after two months, I failed at this plan.

I then started to think: how should we make New Year’s resolutions? I think, first, our resolutions should be specific — we should clearly know what we want to do. For example, one of my resolutions this year is to cook at home at least twice a week. Second, our resolutions should be realistic. I know I’m very busy at work, so cooking every day isn’t realistic, and going to the gym every day isn’t realistic either. So this year, my plan is to cook at home at least twice a week, go to the gym at least three times a week, and exercise for thirty minutes each time. Third, our resolutions can be flexible — it’s OK not to follow them perfectly every time. For example, if I go cycling today, then if I feel too tired later in the week, I can go to the gym one less time.

What do you think about New Year’s resolutions? Do you make them? How do you think we should make New Year’s resolutions? Feel free to leave us a comment and share your thoughts!

title: #245 The Fastest Nurse in China and Debate about her最快护士和她的争议
transcript:
大家好，欢迎回来 MaoMi Chinese！

你不工作的时候会做什么？会做运动吗？你会参加一些运动比赛，比如马拉松吗？在中国，有一个护士，她叫张水华，她也是一名马拉松选手。人们叫她“最快护士”，因为她跑得很快。但是，这位“最快护士”被她工作的医院批评了，她说的很多话也让人们讨论。今天，我们一起来聊一聊吧！

张水华在中国福建的一个医院工作。不工作的时候，她喜欢跑步，也参加了很多马拉松比赛。人们都叫她“最快护士”。2025 年 8 月，她参加了哈尔滨马拉松比赛。她跑得非常快，拿到了女子组第一名。

比赛以后，有人去采访她，她在采访里说：希望医院的领导让她调休跑马拉松。调，意思是调整，也就是去改一些东西。休，也就是休息。调休，意思是改变一下她休息的时间。她的意思是，不是想多休息，只是希望换一下休息的时间，这样，她就有时间多去比赛。她说了这句话以后，很多人讨论。

很多人支持她，觉得她一边工作，一边跑马拉松，很不容易，也很努力。很多人觉得，普通人也应该有自己的爱好和梦想。

但也有一些人不同意。有的人觉得，护士的工作很重要，不能因为个人的爱好经常调休。如果她经常调休，她的同事也要跟着她调休。她的同事们也有自己的生活，经常调休对她的同事们不公平。

后来，她的医院认为，她有一些问题，经常用不真实的理由调休，还有，她自己接了广告，医院不同意。所以，医院批评了她。

张水华现在还在医院工作，但是她也继续在跑马拉松。2026年1月1日，她又拿了一个马拉松比赛的第一名。

这件事情让很多人开始思考一个问题：工作和个人爱好应该怎么平衡？当你的梦想影响到别人时，我们应该怎么做？

你怎么看张水华这件事呢？欢迎给我们留言，分享你的看法。
translation:
Hello everyone, welcome back to MaoMi Chinese!

What do you do when you’re not working? Do you exercise? Do you take part in sports competitions, such as marathons? In China, there is a nurse called Zhang Shuihua, who is also a marathon runner. People call her “the fastest nurse” because she runs very fast. However, this “fastest nurse” was criticised by the hospital where she works, and many of the things she said have caused a lot of discussion. Today, let’s talk about it together.

Zhang Shuihua works at a hospital in Fujian, China. When she is not working, she likes running and has taken part in many marathon races. People often call her “the fastest nurse”. In August 2025, she ran in the Harbin Marathon. She ran very fast and won first place in the women’s category.

After the race, someone interviewed her. In the interview, she said that she hoped the hospital leaders would allow her to adjust her rest days so she could run marathons. “Adjust” means to change something, and “rest” means time off. So “adjusting rest days” means changing when she takes her time off. What she meant was that she did not want more time off, but wanted to swap her rest days so that she could have more time to compete. After she said this, many people began to discuss it.

Many people supported her. They felt that it is not easy to work and run marathons at the same time, and that she works very hard. Many people also believe that ordinary people should have their own hobbies and dreams.

However, some people did not agree. They felt that a nurse’s job is very important and that she should not frequently change her rest days because of personal hobbies. If she often changes her shifts, her colleagues also have to change theirs. Her colleagues have their own lives too, and frequent schedule changes are unfair to them.

Later, her hospital believed that she had some problems. She often used untrue reasons to change her shifts, and she also accepted advertising work without the hospital’s approval. Because of this, the hospital criticised her.

Zhang Shuihua is still working at the hospital, and she continues to run marathons. On 1 January 2026, she won first place in another marathon race.

This situation has made many people think about an important question: how should we balance work and personal hobbies? When your dreams affect other people, what should we do?

What do you think about Zhang Shuihua’s story? Leave us a comment and share your thoughts with us.

title: #246 Chinese Government Started to Manage People’s Weight? 中国开始管理人们体重了？
transcript:
大家好，欢迎回来 MaoMi Chinese！

我们2026年的新年计划里，有没有“减肥”呢？这几年在中国，胖的人也越来越多了。中国的一个城市，杭州，开始管理居民体重。居民，意思是住在这个地方，在这个地方生活的人们。杭州居民，也就是在杭州生活的人们。

杭州是中国的一个大城市。最近，杭州通过了一条新的规定，也就是新的法律。这个法律和健康有关，名字叫《全民健康促进条例》。“条例”，也就是政府定的一些规则。

这个条例里，有一个内容让很多人注意到，那就是体重管理。“体重管理”，也就是注意自己的体重，不要太胖，要健康一点。

为什么要管理体重呢？因为现在很多人超重。“超重”，也就是体重太高，对身体不好。体重太高，可能会有一些问题，比如心脏不好，血糖不正常，身体容易累。

这个条例告诉大家两句话：管住嘴，迈开腿。“管住嘴”，也就是少吃太油、太甜、太咸的东西，多吃健康的食物。杭州说，以后在学校，医院，这些地方，都要有营养师。在很多地方，人们不能吸烟，也要少喝酒。“迈开腿”，也就是多运动，比如走路、跑步、骑自行车。

杭州说，以后会有更多运动的地方，比如公园、运动场，让大家更方便运动。比如，杭州会有更多的公园，让大家运动。一些大学有操场和运动场，学生放假的时候，居民也可以来这里做运动。这不是说每个人一定要减肥，而是希望大家更健康。

杭州还说，医院和学校也会鼓励人们和孩子们多做运动。杭州也会做一个居民健康的数据库。有了数据库，他们会鼓励老人和年轻人，男人和女人，病人和健康的人，做不同的运动。

很多人在讨论这个事情。有的人觉得很好，因为健康真的很重要；也有人觉得很不舒服，觉得体重是自己的事情，不想被管理。

你怎么看杭州管理体重这件事呢？欢迎给我们留言，和我们分享你的看法。
translation:
Hello everyone, welcome back to MaoMi Chinese!

In our plans for 2026, is “losing weight” on your list? In recent years, more and more people in China have become overweight. In one Chinese city, Hangzhou, the local government has started to manage residents’ body weight. “Residents” means people who live in a place. So Hangzhou residents are people who live and work in Hangzhou.

Hangzhou is a large city in China. Recently, Hangzhou passed a new regulation, in other words, a new law. This law is related to health and is called the “Public Health Promotion Regulation”. A “regulation” means a set of rules made by the government.

In this regulation, one part has caught a lot of attention, and that is weight management. “Weight management” means paying attention to your body weight, not being too overweight, and staying healthier.

Why manage weight? Because many people are now overweight. “Overweight” means having too much body weight, which is not good for your health. Being overweight can cause problems such as heart issues, abnormal blood sugar levels, and feeling tired easily.

This regulation tells everyone two simple ideas: watch what you eat and get moving. “Watch what you eat” means eating less food that is too oily, too sweet, or too salty, and eating more healthy food. Hangzhou says that in the future, places like schools and hospitals will all have nutritionists. In many places, people will not be allowed to smoke and will also need to drink less alcohol. “Get moving” means doing more exercise, such as walking, running, or cycling.

Hangzhou has also said that there will be more places for exercise in the future, such as parks and sports grounds, to make it easier for people to work out. For example, Hangzhou will have more parks for exercise. Some universities have sports fields and playgrounds, and when students are on holiday, local residents can also use these places to exercise. This does not mean that everyone must lose weight; the aim is to help people become healthier.

Hangzhou has also said that hospitals and schools will encourage people and children to exercise more. The city will also create a health database for residents. With this database, they will encourage different groups — older people and younger people, men and women, people who are ill and people who are healthy — to do different kinds of exercise.

Many people are discussing this policy. Some people think it is a good thing, because health is very important. Others feel uncomfortable and believe that body weight is a personal matter and should not be managed by others.

What do you think about Hangzhou managing residents’ body weight? Leave us a comment and share your views with us.

title: #247 Love You, My Old self. See You Tomorrow.” 爱你老己，明天见
transcript:
大家好，欢迎回来 MaoMi Chinese+！

最近有一句话，中国年轻人非常喜欢，这句话也在网上也很火。这句话就是：爱你老己，明天见。今天，我们一起来聊一聊吧！

这句话什么意思呢？爱你老己，意思是爱你自己。这里不用“自己”，而用“老己”。老己，也就是把自己当成一个老朋友。有时候，我们也会用“老”来叫一个很亲近的人。比如“老妈”，“老爸”。如果你的一个好朋友姓“张”，你也可以叫他“老张”。听起来很亲切。

那这句话是怎么火的呢？网上有一个短视频。视频里的人看起来很累，生活压力很大。视频最后，她说了一句安慰自己的话：爱你老己，明天见。安慰，也就是在别人不开心的时候，说一些温柔的话，让他感觉好一点。很多年轻人看到以后，觉得这句话很像在说自己，于是也开始用这句话。

为什么年轻人喜欢这句话？因为现在很多年轻人真的很累。工作很忙，压力很大，有时候还会觉得很失败。这个时候，他们不想听大道理，也不想听别人说“你要加油”。他们只要一点点安慰。

“爱你老几”，这句话不要我们马上变好，也不要我们成功。它只是告诉我们：你今天已经很辛苦了，先对自己好一点。 现在，很多人会在视频里说这句话。比如，下班很晚，很累，就说一句：爱你老己，明天见。也有人把这句话写在笔记里，提醒自己，要爱自己，要对自己好一点。

这句话能火，还有一个原因。它很简单，很真实。真实，也就是不假，很像普通人的生活。它不教我们怎么成功，只是安慰我们。

那你呢？你会对自己说这句话吗？在什么时候你最需要听到这句话？欢迎给我们留言，和我们分享。
translation:
Hello everyone, welcome back to MaoMi Chinese+!

Recently, there’s a sentence that many young people in China really like, and it has become very popular online. The sentence is: “Love you, old self. See you tomorrow.” Today, let’s talk about it together.

What does this sentence mean? “Love you, old self” means love yourself. Here, people don’t use the word “yourself”, but use “old self”. “Old” here means someone very close to you, like a friend you know well. In Chinese, we often use “old” for people we feel close to. For example, “mum” can be called “old mum”, “dad” can be “old dad”. If your good friend’s surname is Zhang, you might call him “Old Zhang”. It sounds friendly and warm.

So how did this sentence become popular? There was a short video online. The person in the video looked very tired and under a lot of life pressure. At the end of the video, she said one sentence to comfort herself: “Love you, old self. See you tomorrow.” “Comfort” means saying gentle words when someone feels unhappy, to help them feel a bit better. Many young people saw the video and felt the sentence was talking about them, so they started using it too.

Why do young people like this sentence so much? Because many young people today are really tired. Work is busy, pressure is high, and sometimes they feel like they are failing. At times like this, they don’t want big speeches or people telling them, “You must try harder.” They just want a little comfort.

This sentence doesn’t ask you to become better straight away, and it doesn’t ask you to be successful. It only tells you: you’ve already worked very hard today, so be a bit kinder to yourself. Now, many people say this sentence in videos. For example, after a long and tiring day at work, they say, “Love you, old self. See you tomorrow.” Some people also write it in their notebooks, to remind themselves to love themselves and treat themselves more gently.

Another reason this sentence became popular is that it is simple and real. “Real” means not fake, very close to ordinary people’s lives. It doesn’t teach us how to succeed, it just comforts us.

What about you? Would you say this sentence to yourself? When do you most need to hear it? Leave us a message and share your thoughts with us.

title: #248 When a Story Doesn’t End 章莹颖案
transcript:
大家好，欢迎回来 MaoMi Chinese。

今天的话题有一点严肃，但是我觉得很重要。我们要聊一个很多中国人都知道的名字：章莹颖。

章莹颖是一位中国女生。2017 年，她去美国学习。在美国的一天，她在路上遇到了一个陌生男人。这个男人骗了她，说可以帮她。后来，她被带走，再也没有回来。

后来，美国的警察抓到了这个男人，法院也判了他有罪。但是，到现在为止，章莹颖的遗体一直没有被找到。遗体，也就是人死了以后的身体。

事情发生以后，很多中国人一直关心章莹颖，也很关心她的父母。章莹颖的父母是普通人。他们只有一个女儿。女儿出事以后，他们去了美国，希望找到女儿，也希望把女儿带回家。

但是，这件事非常难。在美国找人、找证据、打官司，都要很多钱，也要很长时间。章莹颖的父母不会英文，也不懂美国的法律。他们很多时候只能等，只能相信别人。

这些年，他们一直没有放弃。

现在，章莹颖的父母开始在网上直播卖东西。直播，也就是livestream。她的父母现在在直播，也就是在网上和大家说话，也卖一些东西。他们这样做，不是为了过更好的生活，而是为了赚钱，再去美国，继续找女儿的遗体。

我看了他们的直播以后，心里很难受。失去女儿的父母，到了这个年纪，还要站在镜头前，一件一件卖东西，只是为了见到女儿最后一面。

这件事情让很多人开始想：如果一个普通家庭遇到这样的事情，他们可以依靠谁？一个失去孩子的父母，要怎么继续生活？我们可以怎么样帮助他们？

今天这一期，我不是想让你难过，而是想让我们记住：在一个新闻后面，有真实的人。在一个案件后面，有一对一直没有放弃的父母。

希望有一天，他们可以把女儿带回家。
translation:
Hello everyone, welcome back to MaoMi Chinese.

Today’s topic is a little serious, but I think it is very important. We are going to talk about a name that many Chinese people know: Zhang Yingying.

Zhang Yingying was a young Chinese woman. In 2017, she went to the United States to study. One day in the US, she met a strange man on the street. This man lied to her and said he could help her. Later, she was taken away and never came back.

Later, the American police arrested this man, and the court found him guilty. However, up to now, Zhang Yingying’s body has still not been found. 遗体，means corpse.

After this happened, many Chinese people continued to care about Zhang Yingying, and also about her parents. Zhang Yingying’s parents are ordinary people. They had only one daughter. After their daughter disappeared, they went to the United States, hoping to find her and hoping to bring her home.

But this has been very difficult. In the United States, looking for a person, finding evidence, and going to court all cost a lot of money and take a very long time. Zhang Yingying’s parents do not speak English and do not understand American law. Many times, they could only wait and trust other people.

Over these years, they have never given up.

Now, Zhang Yingying’s parents have started selling products through online livestreams. Livestream means selling things and talking to people online. Her parents now do livestreams, talking to viewers and selling products. They are not doing this to live a better life, but to earn money so they can go back to the United States and continue looking for their daughter’s body.

After watching their livestreams, I felt very sad. Parents who lost their daughter, at this age, still have to stand in front of a camera and sell things one by one, just to see their daughter one last time.

This story has made many people think: if an ordinary family faces something like this, who can they rely on? How can parents who lose a child continue living? How can we help them?

In this episode, I am not trying to make you feel sad. I just want us to remember this: behind a piece of news, there are real people. Behind a case, there is a pair of parents who have never given up.

I hope that one day, they will be able to bring their daughter home.

title: #249  All In, Then All Out上头和下头
transcript:
大家好，欢迎回来 MaoMi Chinese!

今天我们来聊两个中国年轻人天天在用、但是很多中文学习者都会觉得有点奇怪的词：上头和下头。

先说上头。上头的意思很简单，就是：情绪来了，没有理智了。我们也知道在做什么，但就是停不下来。

有时候喝酒，很多中国人会说： 我喝两杯就上头了。意思是，我一喝酒就容易上头，开始乱说话。这里的上头，不只是醉，也是没有理智的意思。

打游戏和玩手机的时候，我们也很容易上头。比如： 我本来只想玩十分钟，结果一玩就上头了。 刚刚用手机看短视频，上头了，两个小时就过去了。意思就是：太沉迷了，完全停不下来。看电视剧，也特别容易上头。你会听到很多人说： 这部剧真的太上头了。这里的上头，有一点“上瘾”的感觉。

上头还可以用来说情绪，比如我们生气或者太激动的时候。比如，我们和人吵架， 有点上头，说话太难听了。吵架的时候一上头，什么话都说得出来。

如果我们很喜欢一个人，也可以说上头。比如，我们觉得一个人长得很好看，我们很喜欢，很上头，想天天都和这个人在一起。后来，发现他只是长得好看，性格不好，就不喜欢了，下头了。

下头是什么意思呢？就是感觉突然没了。可能只是因为一句话、一个动作，或者一件小事。比如说一个人， 他一开口我就有点下头。 本来觉得他还行，结果越聊越下头。意思就是：本来还可以，现在不行了。

上头和下头，经常一起出现。可能昨天我们对一个人很上头，很喜欢他。但是今天他说了一句奇怪的话，我们就下头了，不喜欢了。

你对什么上头？又因为什么下头？欢迎给我们留言，说说你的故事吧！
translation:
Hello everyone, welcome back to MaoMi Chinese!

Today we’re going to talk about two words that Chinese young people really use every single day, but that confuse a lot of Chinese learners when they hear them: shàngtóu and xiàtóu.

Let’s start with shàngtóu.

The meaning of shàngtóu is actually very simple: the emotion has kicked in, and rational thinking has gone. We know what we’re doing, but we just can’t stop ourselves.

When it comes to drinking, a lot of Chinese people will say:

“I had just two drinks and I was already shàngtóu.”

This means: as soon as I drink alcohol, I easily get shàngtóu and start talking nonsense. Here, shàngtóu doesn’t just mean being drunk — it also means losing rational control.

When we play games or use our phones, it’s also very easy to get shàngtóu. For example:

“I originally only wanted to play for ten minutes, but once I started, I got shàngtóu.”

“I was just watching short videos on my phone, got shàngtóu, and two hours passed.”

The meaning is: you’re too absorbed and completely unable to stop. Watching TV dramas is especially likely to make people shàngtóu as well. You’ll often hear people say:

“This drama is really too shàngtóu.”

Here, shàngtóu has a bit of an “addictive” feeling.

Shàngtóu can also be used to talk about emotions, especially when we’re angry or overly excited. For example, when we argue with someone:

“I got a bit shàngtóu and spoke too harshly.”

Once you get shàngtóu during an argument, you can say absolutely anything.

If we really like someone, we can also say shàngtóu. For example, we think someone is very good-looking, we really like them, we’re very shàngtóu, and we want to be with them every day. Later on, we realise that they’re just good-looking but have a bad personality, so we stop liking them — and then we’re xiàtóu.

So what does xiàtóu mean?

It means that the feeling suddenly disappears. It might be because of just one sentence, one action, or one small thing. For example, talking about a person:

“As soon as he opened his mouth, I felt a bit xiàtóu.”

“At first I thought he was alright, but the more we talked, the more xiàtóu I felt.”

The meaning is: before, it was okay — now it’s not.

Shàngtóu and xiàtóu often appear together. Yesterday, we might have been very shàngtóu about someone and really liked them. But today, they say something strange, and suddenly we’re xiàtóu and no longer like them.

So what do you get shàngtóu about? And what makes you xiàtóu? Leave us a comment and share your story!

title: #250 Year of the Horse… or Year of Malfoy?马年和马尔福
transcript:
大家好，欢迎回来 MaoMi Chinese！

马上就要过年了，今年是马年。我先祝大家新年快乐，马年大吉！

最近在网上，很多年轻人说，今年的“吉祥物”除了马，还有马尔福。吉祥物，意思就是可以给我们好运的人或者东西。马尔福是谁呢？他是《哈利·波特》里的一个角色(Draco Malfoy)，那个金色头发、有点骄傲的男生。为什么大家会选他呢？原因很简单，因为他的名字里有一个字——马。马尔福，第一个字就是“马”。所以很多网友开玩笑说，既然是马年，那就让马尔福来做吉祥物，给我们好运吧！

马尔福里的马，刚刚好是马年的马，这叫“谐音”。谐音，意思就是两个词听起来一样，或者很像。比如“马年”和“马尔福”，都有“马”。虽然一个是年份，一个是小说的角色，本来没有关系，但是因为发音一样，大家就把它们连在一起。这就是谐音。

然后网上就有了很多好玩的图片。有人把马尔福做成红色背景的年画。年画就是过年时贴在墙上的传统图片。有人给他加上“马到成功”这样的祝福。还有人说：“今年考试就靠你了，马尔福！”这些内容在中文里常常叫“梗”。梗，意思就是在网上流行的笑话，很多人都会用，也都明白。马尔福的演员也知道了这个事，他在他的社交媒体Instagram上也发了这个事，他觉得中国人用他做吉祥物，真的非常好玩，他也很开心。

当然，没有人真的相信马尔福可以带来好运，这只是年轻人过年的幽默。以前龙年的时候，有人会用名字里有“龙”的明星，比如成龙。猴年的时候，人们会想到孙悟空。现在马年，就是马尔福了。你可以看到，现在的春节文化不只是传统文化，也会加入电影、小说和流行文化。传统和现代放在一起，就变得更有趣了。

好啦，我们再来说说今天聊的词语吧。

吉祥物，就是可以给我们好运的人或者东西。比如，MaoMi Chinese的吉祥物是我的猫六一。

谐音，意思是两个词听起来一样，或者很像，比如马尔福和马年。

梗，意思是网上流行的笑话。比如，马尔福变成了中国年轻人新年的梗。

所以，如果你今年看到很多马尔福的图片，不要觉得奇怪。这只是中文里的谐音游戏，也是中国年轻人的幽默。今年是马尔福年，那明年又会是谁呢？如果是你的生肖年，你会选谁做你的吉祥物呢？欢迎给我们留言，分享你的想法！
translation:
Hello everyone, welcome back to MaoMi Chinese!

The New Year is just around the corner, and this year is the Year of the Horse. First of all, I’d like to wish you all a Happy New Year – and good luck in the Year of the Horse!

Recently, many young people online have been saying that this year’s “mascot” is not only the horse, but also Malfoy. A mascot is a person or thing that brings us good luck. So, who is Malfoy? He is a character from Harry Potter, the blond-haired, slightly arrogant boy. Why have people chosen him? The reason is very simple: there is a “马” (horse) in his Chinese name. 马尔福 (Malfoy) – the first character is “马”, which means horse. So many internet users joke that since it’s the Year of the Horse, we might as well let Malfoy be our mascot and bring us good luck!

The “马” in Malfoy happens to be the same “马” as in the Year of the Horse. This is called a “homophone”. A homophone means two words that sound the same, or very similar. For example, “马年” (Year of the Horse) and “马尔福” (Malfoy) both contain the sound “马”. One is a year in the lunar calendar, and the other is a character from a novel. Originally, they have nothing to do with each other. But because they sound the same, people connect them together. That’s what a homophone is.

Then lots of funny pictures appeared online. Some people turned Malfoy into a traditional New Year picture with a red background. A New Year picture is a traditional decoration people put on the wall during Spring Festival. Others added blessings such as “马到成功”, which means “may you achieve success immediately” – it also contains the word “horse”. Some people even said, “Malfoy, I’m counting on you for my exams this year!” In Chinese, this kind of popular online joke is often called a “meme” or “梗”. A “梗” means a joke or idea that becomes popular on the internet and that many people understand and use. The actor who played Malfoy also found out about this. He even posted about it on his Instagram, saying he thought it was great fun that Chinese people were using him as a New Year mascot, and he felt very happy about it.

Of course, no one truly believes that Malfoy can bring good luck. This is simply a bit of humour for the New Year. In previous Year of the Dragon, people used celebrities whose names include “龙” (dragon), such as Jackie Chan. In the Year of the Monkey, people think of the Monkey King. Now in the Year of the Horse, it’s Malfoy’s turn. You can see that Spring Festival culture today is not only traditional; it also includes films, novels and pop culture. When tradition and modern culture come together, it becomes even more interesting.

Right, let’s quickly go over today’s key words.

A mascot is a person or thing that brings good luck. For example, the mascot of MaoMi Chinese is my cat, Liu Yi.

A homophone means two words that sound the same or very similar, like Malfoy and the Year of the Horse.

A meme, or “梗”, is a popular internet joke. For example, Malfoy has become a New Year meme among young Chinese people.

So, if you see lots of pictures of Malfoy this year, don’t be surprised. It’s just a homophone joke in Chinese, and a bit of humour from young people in China. This year may feel like the Year of Malfoy – but who will it be next year? If it were your zodiac year, who would you choose as your mascot? Leave us a comment and share your ideas!

title: #251 Kung Fu Robots on Spring Festival Gala 中国春晚的机器人
transcript:
大家好，欢迎回来 MaoMi Chinese。今天我们来聊一聊春晚，还有今年很多人看的机器人武术表演。

春晚，也就是“春节联欢晚会”，是很多中国人每年除夕晚上看的一个电视节目。很多中国家庭一边吃年夜饭，一边看春晚。对很多中国人来说，这是一种过年的习惯。

今年春晚有一个节目特别火，就是机器人的武术表演。武术，就是中国传统的功夫。去年的春晚，有很多机器人跳舞。今年不一样，机器人开始表演武术动作，而且动作越来越难。很多机器人一起打功夫，看起来很震撼。震撼，就是让人觉得非常惊讶、很厉害。

在Youtube，也有很多网友看了这个节目。很多人觉得很震撼，很多人认为，中国的机器人和AI很厉害，只用了一年，机器人不仅可以跳舞，也可以打功夫了。有些人说，甚至有点害怕。

中国网友有一些不一样的看法。有些人觉得机器人和AI特别厉害，他们说：“去年机器人只能跳舞，今年已经可以表演武术了，进步太快了！”他们为中国机器人和AI的发展感到自豪。自豪，就是觉得骄傲。

但是，也有很多人觉得，春晚的机器人太多了。他们说，机器人应该去做辛苦、危险或者无聊的工作，而不是代替人类去表演。代替，就是取代原来的人。他们担心，如果连舞台表演都让机器人来做，那人类艺术家怎么办？

所以，同一个节目，不同的人会有不同的感觉。每一年的春晚都会有很多讨论。今年的机器人武术表演，不只是一个节目，也是一种信号。它让我们看到科技在进步，也让我们问一个问题：科技应该怎么和人一起发展？

那你怎么看今年的机器人武术表演呢？你觉得震撼，还是有一点担心？欢迎给我们留言，说说你的看法！
translation:
Hello everyone, welcome back to MaoMi Chinese. Today we’re going to talk about the Spring Festival Gala, and the robot martial arts performance that many people watched this year.

The Spring Festival Gala, also called the “Spring Festival Evening Gala”, is a television programme that many Chinese people watch on Lunar New Year’s Eve. Lots of families eat their New Year’s Eve dinner while watching the show. For many people in China, it’s a New Year tradition.

This year, one performance in particular became very popular: the robots performing martial arts. Martial arts means traditional Chinese kung fu. In last year’s Gala, many robots performed dance routines. This year was different. The robots began performing martial arts movements, and the moves became more and more difficult. Many robots performed kung fu together on stage, and it looked very impressive. Impressive means something that makes you feel surprised and amazed.

On YouTube, many viewers also watched this performance. A lot of people said they were amazed. Many felt that Chinese robots and AI are very advanced. In just one year, robots not only learned to dance, but also to perform martial arts. Some people even said they felt a little bit afraid.

Chinese viewers had slightly different opinions. Some people thought the robots and AI were extremely impressive. They said, “Last year robots could only dance. This year they can already perform martial arts. The progress is so fast!” They felt proud of the development of Chinese robotics and AI. Proud means feeling a sense of achievement and honour.

However, many others felt that there were too many robots in the Gala. They said robots should be used to do hard, dangerous, or boring jobs, rather than replacing humans on stage. Replace means to take the place of someone. They worry that if even stage performances are done by robots, what will happen to human artists?

So, with the same programme, different people have different feelings. Every year, the Spring Festival Gala brings a lot of discussion. This year’s robot martial arts performance was not just a show, but also a kind of signal. It shows us that technology is progressing, and it also makes us ask an important question: how should technology develop together with human beings?

What do you think about this year’s robot martial arts performance? Did you find it impressive, or are you a little concerned? Leave us a comment and share your thoughts!

title: #252 Uncle Hanzi 汉字叔叔
transcript:
大家好，欢迎回来 MaoMi Chinese！

今天我想跟大家介绍一个人，这个人叫“汉字叔叔”，他是一个美国人，名字叫Richard Sears，中国网友叫他汉字叔叔，因为他非常喜欢汉字，一直研究汉字。

理查德年轻的时候，学的是物理和计算机，还在美国做IT工作，可是他真正喜欢的是汉字。他22岁第一次去台湾，自己练习中文，不上课，只通过跟当地人聊天，慢慢学会了说中文。

后来他的人生有了大变化，有一次心脏病让他重新思考人生，他决定做一件别人很少做的事情，那就是把中国最早分析汉字的书《说文解字》数字化。数字化，也就是把一个东西变成电脑或者手机就可以看的东西。数字化以后，大家可以用电脑看见汉字的变化，于是他做了一个叫汉字源（Chinese Etymology）的网站。

这个网站有十几万万古代汉字和它们的历史，比如甲骨文、金文、小篆等，你只要输入一个汉字，就可以看到它从几千年前的样子慢慢变到今天的样子。很多中国网友第一次看到这些汉字的“以前样子”都觉得很新奇，还发在微博上，这样Richard的名字和他的网站突然在中国火了起来。

虽然很多人叫他网红，但他的网站一直是免费的，他自己也没有收入。有一次，因为没钱做网站，网站就要关了，很多网友给他捐钱。捐钱，也就是给他很多钱，不用他还钱。还有人叫他“汉字叔叔”，这个名字让他很开心。

后来他来到中国，住过天津、北京和很多地方。现在他的网站有超过十万个古代汉字，每个汉字背后都有故事。我们在网站上看一个汉字，就会知道这个字怎么来、怎么变、为什么这样写。

我觉得这个故事很有意思，因为他不是中国人，却花了这么多年，用电脑和网络把汉字的故事带给全世界。汉字叔叔太伟大了！
translation:
Hello everyone, welcome back to MaoMi Chinese!

Today I’d like to introduce someone to you. He’s known as “Uncle Hanzi”. He’s an American man called Richard Sears. Chinese netizens call him “Uncle Hanzi” because he absolutely loves Chinese characters and has spent many years studying them.

When Richard was young, he studied physics and computer science, and he worked in IT in the United States. But what he truly loved was Chinese characters. When he was 22, he went to Taiwan for the first time. He practised Chinese on his own. He didn’t attend classes; he simply chatted with local people and gradually learned how to speak Chinese.

Later, his life changed in a big way. After suffering a heart attack, he began to rethink his life. He decided to do something very few people had done — to digitise Shuowen Jiezi, the earliest Chinese book that systematically analyses Chinese characters. “Digitise” means turning something into a form that can be viewed on a computer or a mobile phone. Once it was digitised, people could use a computer to see how Chinese characters have changed over time. So he created a website called Hanziyuan (Chinese Etymology).

This website contains tens of thousands of ancient Chinese characters and their historical forms, such as oracle bone script, bronze inscriptions, and small seal script. You simply type in a character, and you can see how it has gradually changed from thousands of years ago to the form we use today. When many Chinese netizens first saw the “old versions” of these characters, they found them fascinating and shared them on Weibo. That’s how Richard and his website suddenly became popular in China.

Although many people call him an internet celebrity, his website has always been free, and he himself has had no income from it. At one point, because he didn’t have enough money to maintain the site, it was about to close. Many netizens donated money to him. Donating means giving him money without expecting it to be repaid. People continued to call him “Uncle Hanzi”, and that name made him very happy.

Later, he came to China and lived in Tianjin, Beijing and other places. Now his website includes more than 100,000 ancient Chinese characters, and behind each character there is a story. When we look up a character on the website, we can learn where it came from, how it changed, and why it is written the way it is.

I think this story is very moving. He isn’t Chinese, yet he has spent so many years using computers and the internet to share the story of Chinese characters with the world. Uncle Hanzi is truly remarkable.

title: #253 The Hidden Workers of the City 我在北京送快递
transcript:
大家好，欢迎回来 MaoMi Chinese！

如果有一天，你在网上买了一件衣服，又买了一本书。过了两天，有人按门铃，把一个快递送到你家门口。快递，就是你在网上买东西以后，公司把东西送到你家。你拿到快递，说一声“谢谢”，然后关上门。事情好像就这样结束了。

但是你有没有想过，这个把快递送到你家的人，他的一天是怎么过的？

今天我想跟大家聊一本书，名字叫《我在北京送快递》。这本书在中国最近很受欢迎，因为它讲的是一个很多人每天都会看到，但很少真的了解的职业：快递员。快递员，就是每天给大家送快递的人。

这本书的作者叫胡安焉。他不是一个作家，而是一个普通人。他年轻的时候做过很多工作，比如服务员、保安、工厂工人，还有快递员。后来，他把自己这些年的工作经历写成了一本书。经历，就是一个人以前做过的事情和生活。

在中国，网购非常普遍。网购的意思是在网上买东西。很多人几乎每天都会网购，比如买衣服、买手机、买零食，甚至买水果。所以每天都有非常多的快递，需要有人把它们送到不同的地方。在很多城市里，你都可以看到骑着电动车送快递的人。

作者在书里说，送快递是一个非常辛苦的工作。很多快递员每天工作很长时间，常常是早上很早就开始，一直工作到晚上十点或者十一点。北京的夏天非常热，可能三十多度，冬天又非常冷，有时候会到零下十度。但是不管天气怎么样，快递还是要送。

在送快递的时候，作者每天都会遇到很多不同的人。有的人对快递员非常友好，比如会说一声“辛苦了”或者“谢谢”。有时候还有人会给快递员一瓶水。但是也有一些人态度不太好，如果快递晚了一点，就会很生气，或者让快递员在楼下等很久。

作者在书里写了一句话，让很多人感动。他说，一个城市每天都在运转。运转的意思是一直在工作、一直在运行。但是在这个城市里，有很多人其实是看不见的。比如送快递的人、送外卖的人，还有清洁工人。如果没有这些人，城市的生活很难正常继续，但是很多人平时很少注意到他们。

《我在北京送快递》这本书其实讲的不是一个特别大的故事，而是一个普通人的生活。但是因为这样，它让很多人开始思考，城市里那些看起来普通、但是其实非常重要的工作。

好啦，最后我们复习一下今天学的词：

1快递。快递就是公司把东西很快送到你家的服务。

2 快递员。快递员就是每天给大家送快递的人。

3 网购。网购就是在网上买东西。

4 经历。经历就是一个人以前做过的事情和生活。

5 运转。运转就是一直在运行、一直在工作，比如我们可以说，一个城市每天都在运转。

你了解快递员的生活吗？在你的国家，快递员的生活怎么样？在下一期MaoMi Chinese+，我们会聊一聊中国快递员的生活，他们的工资，他们工作会有什么困难。
translation:
Hello everyone, welcome back to MaoMi Chinese!

Imagine one day you buy a piece of clothing online and also order a book. Two days later, someone rings your doorbell and delivers a parcel to your door. A delivery, or “kuaidi”, is the service where a company sends the things you bought online to your home. You take the parcel, say “thank you”, and close the door. It feels like the story ends there.

But have you ever thought about the person who brings that parcel to your home? What does a day in their life look like?

Today I’d like to talk about a book called I Deliver Parcels in Beijing. This book has recently become very popular in China because it talks about a job that many people see every day but rarely truly understand: the parcel delivery worker. A delivery worker is the person who brings parcels to people every day.

The author of the book is called Hu Anyan. He isn’t a writer but an ordinary person. When he was younger, he did many different jobs, such as being a waiter, a security guard, a factory worker, and a delivery worker. Later, he wrote about his work experiences over the years and turned them into a book. “Experience” here means the things a person has done and the life they have lived in the past.

In China, online shopping is extremely common. Online shopping means buying things on the internet. Many people shop online almost every day. They buy clothes, mobile phones, snacks, and even fruit. Because of this, there are a huge number of parcels every day that need to be delivered to different places. In many cities, you can often see people riding electric scooters to deliver parcels.

In the book, the author says that delivering parcels is actually a very hard job. Many delivery workers work very long hours. They often start early in the morning and keep working until ten or even eleven at night. Summers in Beijing are very hot, sometimes over thirty degrees, while winters are extremely cold and can drop to minus ten degrees. But no matter what the weather is like, the parcels still have to be delivered.

While delivering parcels, the author meets many different kinds of people every day. Some people are very friendly to delivery workers. For example, they might say “you’ve worked hard” or simply “thank you”. Sometimes people even give them a bottle of water. But there are also people who are not very kind. If a parcel arrives a little late, they may become angry or make the delivery worker wait downstairs for a long time.

In the book, the author writes a sentence that moved many readers. He says that a city is always running. “Running” here means that everything in the city is always working and operating. But in this city, there are many people who are almost invisible. For example, the people who deliver parcels, those who deliver takeaway food, and the street cleaners. Without these people, it would be very difficult for city life to continue normally, but many people rarely notice them.

I Deliver Parcels in Beijing is not a book about a grand or dramatic story. Instead, it tells the story of an ordinary person’s life. But because of this, it encourages many people to think again about the jobs in a city that may look ordinary but are actually very important.

Alright, before we finish, let’s review the words we learned today.

First, “kuaidi”, or delivery. This means the service where a company quickly sends the things you bought to your home.

Second, delivery worker. This is the person who delivers parcels to people every day.

Third, online shopping. This means buying things on the internet.

Fourth, experience. This refers to the things a person has done and the life they have lived before.

Fifth, running or operating. This means something is continuously working or functioning. For example, we can say that a city is running every day.

Do you know what the life of a delivery worker is like? In your country, what is the life of delivery workers like?

In the next episode of MaoMi Chinese, we will talk more about the lives of delivery workers in China — their salary and the difficulties they face in their work.

title: #254 All-Women Repair Team全女维修工
transcript:
大家好，欢迎回来 MaoMi Chinese！

如果家里的东西坏了，你会自己维修，还是叫师傅维修？维修，就是把坏的东西修好。在中国，我们叫维修工人师傅，因为他们会很多我们不会的东西。在中国，很多维修师傅都是男人。但是在中国成都，有一群维修工，都是女人。这就是强记女工。今天，我们一起来聊聊吧！

如果你第一次听到这个词，可能会觉得有一点奇怪。“强记女工”是什么意思呢？ “强记”是一个店名，也就是一个品牌名字。如果你在中国的路上走一走，也经常会看到这样的店名，比如“陈记烧烤”，“王记面条”等等。“女工”就是女工人。所以，“强记女工”其实是一个团队的名字。

这个团队在中国成都。她们做的工作叫上门维修。“上门”的意思是到客户家里去，“维修”就是修理坏了的东西。比如灯坏了,电器坏了，师傅就会到家里帮你修。在中国，这种工作以前大部分都是男性做的，比如电工（修电的人）或者维修师傅。所以很多人会觉得，这是一种体力工作。体力工作就是需要用很多力气的工作。

但是在成都，有一群女性开始做这样的工作。她们带着工具箱，到客户家里修灯、修电器、装灯具，有时候也会安装家具。这个团队成立的时间不长，但是已经给一千多个家庭提供过服务。“提供服务”的意思就是帮助别人解决问题。

很多客户第一次看到女师傅来修东西，会有一点吃惊，因为大家已经习惯看到男维修工。但是很多人用过她们的服务以后，都觉得她们做得很好，也很细心。“细心”的意思是注意很多小细节，做事很认真。

一开始的时候，也有人不太相信她们。有的人会问：女生真的会修电器吗？女生真的可以做这种工作吗？ 但是慢慢地，越来越多的人用过她们的服务，也开始改变想法。因为其实一个工作，不一定只适合男性，也不一定只适合女性。只要有技术，有耐心，谁都可以把工作做好。

所以，“强记女工”的故事告诉我们，很多人以前觉得有些工作女生不能做，但是现在大家发现，其实女生也可以做得很好。
translation:
Hello everyone, welcome back to MaoMi Chinese!

If something in your home breaks, do you repair it yourself, or do you call someone to fix it? “Repair” means fixing something that is broken. In China, we usually call repair workers shifu. Shifu means a skilled worker or master, because they can do many things that we cannot. In China, many repair workers are men. But in Chengdu, a city in China, there is a group of repair workers who are all women. They are called Qiangji Nügong. Today, let’s talk about them.

If this is the first time you have heard this term, you might think it sounds a little strange. What does “Qiangji Nügong” mean? “Qiangji” is actually a shop name, or a brand name. If you walk around in China, you will often see names like this, for example “Chenji Barbecue” or “Wangji Noodles”. “Nügong” simply means female workers. So “Qiangji Nügong” is the name of a team.

This team is based in Chengdu. Their work is called home repair services. “Home” means they go to the customer’s house, and “repair” means fixing things that are broken. For example, if a light is broken or an electrical appliance stops working, a repair worker will come to your home and fix it. In China, this kind of work used to be done mostly by men, such as electricians or repair technicians. So many people think it is manual work. Manual work means work that requires physical effort.

But in Chengdu, a group of women have started doing this kind of job. They carry their toolboxes and go to customers’ homes to repair lights, fix appliances, and install light fittings. Sometimes they also install furniture. This team has not existed for very long, but they have already provided services to more than one thousand families. “Providing services” simply means helping people solve problems.

When many customers first see a female repair worker arrive, they feel a little surprised, because they are used to seeing male repair workers. But after using their service, many people say they do a very good job and are very careful. “Careful” means paying attention to small details and doing things seriously.

At the beginning, some people did not really believe in them. Some people asked: can women really repair electrical appliances? Can women really do this kind of work? But slowly, more and more people used their service, and their ideas began to change. In fact, a job does not have to belong only to men or only to women. As long as you have the skills and the patience, anyone can do the job well.

So the story of Qiangji Nügong tells us something simple: in the past, many people thought some jobs were not suitable for women. But now people are beginning to see that women can also do these jobs very well.

title: #255 An Annual TV Show that Exposes Bad Products 315晚会
transcript:
大家好，欢迎回来 MaoMi Chinese！

今天我们来聊一个在中国每年都有的节目，叫做315晚会。“315”就是3月15日，这一天在中国叫做消费者权益日。消费者，意思是买东西的人；权益，意思是我们应该有的权利。消费者的权益是什么呢？那就是我们可以买到安全、真实的东西。简单来说，这一天就是保护大家买东西的安全。

那315晚会是什么呢？它是一个电视节目，在每一年的3月15日晚上播出，第一次播出是1991年，到现在已经36年了。这个节目会曝光一些不好的公司。曝光，意思是把不好的事情说出来，让大家知道。比如卖假东西的、食品不安全的，或者骗钱的公司。坏公司在这一天会很紧张，因为他们害怕被曝光。

为什么在中国，大家这么关注这个节目呢？因为如果公司被曝光，他们会有很严重的后果。他们的产品也可能不能再卖了，很多人也会不再相信这个公司了。所以很多公司在3月都会特别小心。

有一年，315晚会说有一些餐厅用不新鲜的肉做菜。不新鲜，就是已经不好了，但是他们还是卖给客人。315也会说一些餐厅的厨房不干净，很多人看到以后很害怕，因为这些店我们平时也可能会去。

但是，人们对这个节目也有不同的看法。有的人觉得315很好，为了消费者的权益，曝光那些骗人的公司。也有人觉得，为什么只有这一天才说这些问题，平时为什么不说？为什么一定要等到3月15日这一天呢？

那如果是你，你会想看这样的节目吗？你觉得它有用吗？下一次的MaoMi Chinese+，我们会聊一聊，今年的315晚会曝光了什么东西，这样我们都可以小心一点！
translation:
Hello everyone, welcome back to MaoMi Chinese!

Today we’re going to talk about a program that happens every year in China, called the 315 Gala. “315” means March 15th, which in China is called Consumer Rights Day. A consumer means someone who buys things; rights means the things we should be allowed to have. So what are consumers’ rights? It means we should be able to buy safe and real products. In short, this day is to protect people when they shop.

So what is the 315 Gala? It is a TV program that is broadcast every year on the evening of March 15th. The first show was in 1991, so now it has been on for 36 years. The program exposes bad companies. Expose means to tell everyone about something bad. For example, companies that sell fake products, unsafe food, or scam people. Bad companies get very nervous on this day because they are afraid of being exposed.

Why do people in China care so much about this show? Because if a company is exposed, the consequences can be serious. Their products might not be sold anymore, and many people may stop trusting the company. So every March, companies are especially careful.

One year, the 315 Gala said that some restaurants were using meat that was not fresh. Not fresh means it was already bad, but they still sold it to customers. The program also showed some kitchens that were not clean. Many people were very shocked because these are restaurants we might go to in real life.

But people have different opinions about the program. Some think the 315 Gala is very good because it protects consumers’ rights and exposes cheating companies. Others ask, why only on this day? Why not all the time? Why wait until March 15th?

What about you? Would you want to watch a program like this? Do you think it is useful? In the next MaoMi Chinese+ episode, we will talk about what this year’s 315 Gala exposed, so we can all be more careful!

title: #256 One Drop of Blood Solves a Case? The Story of Henry Lee 华人神探李昌钰
transcript:
大家好，欢迎回来 MaoMi Chinese！

3月27日，我看到了一个新闻，李昌钰博士去世了。很多人叫他“华人神探”。华人，就是有中国血统的人。神探，就是那种很快可以找到真相的人，比如夏洛克福尔摩斯。今天，我们来聊一聊李昌钰博士。

李昌钰是一位非常有名的法医专家。“法医”，意思是用科学的方法帮助警察破案的人。1938年，他出生在中国江苏。小时候，他爸爸是富商，他们家很有钱。后来，他爸爸突然去世了，家里也欠了很多钱，他们一家人突然变得很穷。后来他们去了台湾生活，再后来，他一个人去了美国读书。

大家可以想一想，一个年轻人去美国，要用英语学习，还要开始新的生活。这真的很不容易，对吧？一开始，他的英语不好，生活也不容易，但是他没有放弃。后来，他开始做法医的工作，用科学的方法来找证据。“证据”，意思是可以证明事情是真的东西，比如血、头发、指纹。

他做过很多非常有名的案件。比如说，有一个案件，现场只有一点点血。“现场”，意思是事情发生的地方。很多人觉得，这一点点血没有用，但是李昌钰用这滴血，得到很多信息，最后帮警察找到了重要的线索。“线索”，意思是帮助我们找到答案的小信息。

还有一次，一个案子看起来像是“意外”。“意外”，意思是不是故意发生的事情，比如在路上遇到撞车的意外。但是李昌钰仔细检查，发现其实不是意外，而是有人做的，这也帮警察找到了凶手。

他常常会非常仔细地看每一个小细节。“细节”，意思是很小、很小的地方。别人看不到的，他可以看到，所以大家都叫他“神探”。后来，他变得非常有名，也去了很多国家工作，还教很多学生。他也常常鼓励年轻人，不要怕困难，要坚持做自己喜欢的事情。

李昌钰博士是一个伟大的人，也是一个非常厉害的神探和法医学家。他一生都在非常努力地工作，现在他终于可以休息了。
translation:
Hello everyone, welcome back to MaoMi Chinese!

On 27 March, I saw some news: Dr Henry Lee had passed away. Many people called him the “Chinese Sherlock Holmes”. “Chinese” means someone with Chinese heritage. “Sherlock Holmes” or “神探” means a detective who can find the truth very quickly. Today, let’s talk about Dr Henry Lee.

Henry Lee was a very famous forensic scientist. “Forensic scientist” means someone who uses science to help the police solve crimes. He was born in 1938 in Jiangsu, China. When he was young, his father was a wealthy businessman and the family was rich. Later, his father suddenly passed away, and the family owed a lot of money. Suddenly, they became very poor. They moved to Taiwan, and later Henry went to the United States to study on his own.

Think about it: a young man, going to America, learning in English, and starting a completely new life. That must have been really difficult, right? At first, his English was poor and life was not easy, but he did not give up. Later, he started working in forensic science, using scientific methods to find evidence. “Evidence” means something that can prove the truth, like blood, hair, or fingerprints.

He worked on many very famous cases. For example, in one case, there was only a tiny drop of blood at the scene. “Scene” means the place where something happened. Many people thought such a small drop of blood was useless, but Henry Lee used it to get important information and helped the police find key clues. “Clues” are small pieces of information that help us find the answer.

In another case, it looked like an “accident”. “Accident” means something that was not done on purpose, like a car crash on the road. But Henry Lee checked carefully and found it was not an accident—it was done by someone. This helped the police catch the criminal.

He always looked very carefully at every tiny detail. “Detail” means something very small. He could see things that others could not, which is why people called him a “Chinese Sherlock Holmes”. Later, he became very famous, worked in many countries, and taught many students. He often encouraged young people not to be afraid of difficulties and to keep pursuing what they love.

Dr Henry Lee was a great man, a remarkable detective, and a brilliant forensic scientist. He worked very hard all his life, and now he can finally rest.

title: #257 ‘Sudden Death’ of a Chinese Celebrity 张雪峰猝死
transcript:
大家好，欢迎回来 MaoMi Chinese！

今天我们来聊一个最近在中国很火的人，张雪峰。最近有一个让人很难过的消息，那就是张雪峰“猝死了”。“猝死”的意思是，一个人本来好好的，没有生病，但是突然去世了。所以很多人一看到这个消息，都非常震惊，因为张雪峰看起来身体很好，还跑过很多次马拉松，怎么会猝死呢？今天，我们一起来聊一聊吧。

张雪峰是谁？为什么这么多人关心他？

张雪峰是一个做教育的人，他不是在普通学校上课的老师，而是帮助学生和家长了解大学，专业，还有未来工作的人。在中国，有一个很重要的考试，叫高考。很多学生考完以后，不知道应该去什么大学，选什么专业，这时候张雪峰就会给他们建议。

他为什么这么有名呢？因为他说话很直接，也很真实，有时候还有一点“毒舌”。“毒舌”的意思是，说话很直接，有点不客气，甚至有一点伤人，但很多时候他说的是实话。比如他说，有些专业看起来很好听，但是其实不好找工作，有些学校名字很好，但是不一定真的好。很多人听了以后觉得他说的就是现实，所以越来越多人关注他。

后来，他开始做视频、做直播，也开公司，卖课程，慢慢变成了一个很成功的商人。但是，他的工作也非常累。他每天要录视频、直播、回答很多问题，还要管理公司，工作时间很长，几乎没有什么事件休息。而且因为他说话很直接，也会被很多人批评，所以他的压力也很大。

当人们知道他“猝死”的时候，大家都很难过，因为他帮助了很多学生和家长。他还有一个12岁的女儿，他也才41岁，太年轻了。但是，这件事情还是让很多人开始思考一个问题：现在很多人都在拼命工作，想赚钱，想成功，可是如果一直这么累，身体会不会出问题？张雪峰的故事让我们看到，成功不一定等于健康，也不一定等于快乐。

所以我们也可以问问自己： 我们每天这么忙，有没有好好休息？我们的生活，是不是太累了？

你觉得，如果是你，你会选择多赚钱但是很累，还是赚少一点，但是生活轻松一点？欢迎给我们留言，说说你的想法！
translation:
Hello everyone, welcome back to MaoMi Chinese!

Today we are going to talk about a person who has recently been very popular in China: 张雪峰. Recently, there was some very sad news saying that he had “died suddenly”. The meaning of “died suddenly” is when a person seems completely fine, not obviously ill, but passes away unexpectedly. So when many people saw this news, they were very shocked, because Zhang Xuefeng looked very healthy and had even run many marathons. So how could he die suddenly? Today, let’s talk about it together.

Who is Zhang Xuefeng, and why do so many people care about him?

Zhang Xuefeng works in education. He is not a normal school teacher. Instead, he helps students and parents understand universities, university subjects, and future careers. In China, there is a very important exam called 高考. After this exam, many students do not know which university to choose or which subject to study, and this is when Zhang Xuefeng gives advice.

Why is he so famous? Because he speaks in a very direct and very honest way, and sometimes he is even “sharp-tongued”. “Sharp-tongued” means a person speaks very directly, sometimes not very politely, and it can even sound a bit hurtful, but often what they say is actually true. For example, he might say that some subjects sound impressive, but are actually hard to find jobs. Or some universities have nice names, but are not necessarily very good. Many people feel that he is simply telling the truth about reality, so more and more people started following him.

Later, he began making videos, doing live streams, and also started his own company selling courses. Slowly, he became a very successful businessman. But his work was also extremely tiring. Every day he had to record videos, do live streams, answer many questions, and manage his company. He worked very long hours and had almost no rest. Because he also spoke very directly, he often received criticism online, so his stress was also very high.

When people heard the news that he had “died suddenly”, many were very sad, because he had helped so many students and parents. He also had a 12-year-old daughter, and he was only 41 years old, which feels far too young. However, this situation also made many people start thinking about an important question: nowadays, many people are working extremely hard to earn money and achieve success, but if life is always this stressful and exhausting, could it affect our health? Zhang Xuefeng’s story reminds us that success does not always mean good health, and it does not always mean happiness.

So we can also ask ourselves: in our busy daily lives, are we getting enough rest? Is our lifestyle too exhausting?

What do you think? If it were you, would you choose to earn more money but live a very tiring life, or earn a bit less but have a more relaxed and balanced life? Feel free to leave a comment and share your thoughts!

title: #258 Work Buddies in China 上班搭子
transcript:
大家好，欢迎回来 MaoMi Chinese。

今天我们聊一个很新的词：上班搭子。先说“搭子”是什么意思。“搭子”就是一起做一件事的人。“搭”有“一起”的意思。所以，如果你每天和一个人一起吃饭，他就是你的吃饭搭子。如果你和一个人一起运动，他就是你的运动搭子。总而言之，就是一起做一件事。

那“上班搭子”呢？就是在公司里，和你一起上班的人。你们可能会一起吃午饭，一起买咖啡，一起聊天。有时候也会一起吐槽老板。“吐槽”就是轻松地说一说不开心的事，比如说工作太多、很累，但是不是很认真地生气，就是说一说而已。

但是，上班搭子不一定是你的好朋友。你们可能只是在上班的时候在一起，下班以后就不联系了。所以很多人会说：我们只是上班搭子，不是朋友。

为什么现在很多人喜欢“搭子”呢？因为现在大家都很忙，也有压力。“压力”就是让你觉得很累，紧张的事情。大家不想一个人，但是也不想太累地去维持很深的关系。“维持关系”就是要花时间聊天、见面、关心对方。所以，“搭子”就很好：有人陪你，但是不用太多时间，也不用有太多责任。

现在还有很多“搭子”。比如饭搭子，一起吃饭的人；学习搭子，一起学习的人；旅游搭子，一起旅行的人；还有游戏搭子，一起玩游戏的人。有的人还会找减肥搭子，一起运动，一起少吃一点，互相帮助。

那“搭子”和“朋友”有什么不一样呢？朋友的关系比较深，你们会关心对方，也会一起做很多事情。但是“搭子”的关系比较简单，只是在一个地方，一起做一件事，比如在公司一起吃饭，这是上班搭子，饭搭子。

好啦，我们来复习一下今天说的词吧：

搭子，就是一起做一个事情的人。比如，上班搭子，饭搭子，学习搭子，等等。 吐槽，就是说一说一些不开心的事。比如，他们是上班搭子，经常一起吐槽老板。 维持关系，意思是花时间去做很多事情，来保护关系，比如维持朋友关系，维持夫妻关系，等等。

那么，你有没有自己的“搭子”？你想要什么样的搭子？欢迎给我们留言，和我们分享吧！
translation:
Hello everyone, welcome back to MaoMi Chinese.

Today we’re going to talk about a very new word: shàngbān dāzi (work buddy). First, what does dāzi mean? A dāzi is someone you do something with. The word dā means “together”. So, if you eat with the same person every day, they are your eating buddy. If you exercise with someone, they are your workout buddy. In short, it just means someone you do an activity with.

So what is a “work buddy”? It’s someone at work who goes through the day with you. You might have lunch together, grab a coffee together, or have a chat. Sometimes you might also complain about your boss together. “To complain” here means to talk lightly about things that make you unhappy, like having too much work or feeling tired. You’re not seriously angry, you’re just talking about it.

However, a work buddy is not necessarily a close friend. You might only spend time together at work, and not keep in touch after work. That’s why many people say: we are just work buddies, not friends.

Why do so many people like having a “dāzi” now? Because people are very busy and often feel stressed. “Stress” means things that make you feel tired or nervous. People don’t want to be alone, but they also don’t want to spend too much time and energy building deep relationships. “To maintain a relationship” means spending time chatting, meeting, and caring about the other person. So having a “dāzi” is ideal: you have someone with you, but it doesn’t take too much time or responsibility.

There are also many other types of “dāzi”. For example, an eating buddy is someone you have meals with; a study buddy is someone you study with; a travel buddy is someone you go on trips with; and a gaming buddy is someone you play games with. Some people even look for a dieting buddy, so they can exercise together, eat a bit less, and help each other.

So what’s the difference between a “dāzi” and a friend? A friendship is usually deeper. You care about each other and do many things together. But a “dāzi” relationship is simpler. It’s usually just in one place, doing one activity together. For example, eating together at work — that’s a work buddy or an eating buddy.

Right, let’s quickly review today’s key words. A dāzi is someone you do an activity with, for example a work buddy, eating buddy, or study buddy. “To complain” means to talk about things that make you unhappy. For example, they are work buddies and often complain about their boss together. “To maintain a relationship” means to spend time doing things to keep a relationship going, like maintaining a friendship or a marriage.

So, do you have your own “dāzi”? What kind of “dāzi” would you like to have? Feel free to leave us a message and share your thoughts!

title: #259 Will Our Digital Clone Replace Us? 数字人会取代我们吗?
transcript:
大家好，欢迎回来 MaoMi Chinese!

最近，在中国的社交媒体上，很多人都在讨论数字人。什么是数字人呢？简单说，就是用 AI 做出来的“人”。数字人不是真的人，是AI，但是可以像人一样工作，回答问题，解决问题。这是一个好事，还是一个可怕的事呢？今天，我们一起来聊一聊吧！

在中国，很多工作已经开始用数字人了。有AI演员，很多短视频都是AI做的，演员都是AI演员。很多广告里的人不是真的人，而是AI。有 AI 主播，有的电视台已经用数字人来报新闻了，他们可以一天工作 24 小时，不会累，也不会请假。还有一些公司，会把员工平时开会的录音、写的邮件、工作的习惯，都整理起来，做成一个“数字分身”。这样就算员工不在这里工作了，这个“数字人”也可以继续帮公司回答问题，做简单的工作。

社交媒体上，很多网友开始讨论了。有的人觉得很方便，有人说：“太好了，以后半夜也可以有人帮我解决问题。”还有做老板的人觉得，这样可以省很多钱，不用一直找新员工。但是，更多人觉得很可怕。有网友觉得，如果他们不在公司工作了，公司还用他们的数字人来工作，那这个还是他们吗？也有网友问：“公司用我的声音、我的脸，这合法的吗？”合法，也就是在法律上是对的。

最近在中国，有一家视频公司的老板说，他们以后要用AI演员，大家听了以后都很生气。大家都说，只要你们敢用AI演员，我们就再也不看你们的电视剧！一方面，大家觉得，AI电视剧没有“人味”，觉得AI做的东西没什么感情。另一方面，大家都很担心，如果越来越多工作可以被数字人代替，那真的人怎么办？是不是会有很多人失业？但是也有人觉得还好，他们觉得需要有人来做AI，所以会有新的工作。

如果有一天，你的公司想用你的数据做一个数字人，你会同意吗？欢迎给我们留言，分享你的看法！
translation:
Hello everyone, welcome back to MaoMi Chinese!

Recently, on Chinese social media, many people have been talking about digital humans. So, what are digital humans? Simply put, they are “people” created by AI. They are not real people, but AI that can work like humans, answer questions, and solve problems. Is this a good thing, or something a bit scary? Today, let’s talk about it together.

In China, many jobs have already started using digital humans. There are AI actors—many short videos are now made by AI, and the “actors” are not real people. In many adverts, the people you see are actually AI. There are also AI news presenters—some TV stations already use digital humans to deliver the news. They can work 24 hours a day, they don’t get tired, and they don’t need time off. Some companies even collect things like meeting recordings, emails, and working habits from their employees, and use this data to create a “digital clone”. So even if the employee is no longer working there, this “digital person” can still help the company answer questions and do simple tasks.

On social media, many people have started to discuss this. Some think it’s very convenient. One person said, “That’s great—now even in the middle of the night, someone can help me solve problems.” Some business owners think it can save a lot of money, because they don’t need to keep hiring new staff. However, more people feel that it’s quite scary. Some users say, “If I’m no longer working at the company, but they still use ‘me’ to work, is that still me?” Others ask, “If a company uses my voice and my face, is that legal?” “Legal” means whether it is allowed by law.

Recently in China, the boss of a video company said that they plan to use AI actors in the future. Many people were very angry when they heard this. They said, “If you use AI actors, we will stop watching your TV dramas!” On the one hand, people feel that AI shows have no “human feeling” and lack emotion. On the other hand, many people are worried that if more and more jobs can be replaced by digital humans, what will happen to real people? Will many people lose their jobs? But some people are not too worried. They think that AI still needs humans to create and manage it, so new jobs will appear.

So, what do you think? If one day your company wants to use your data to create a digital human, would you agree? Feel free to leave us a message and share your thoughts!

title: #260 特朗普在中国的“认真模式” Trump’s “Serious Mode” in China
transcript:
大家好！欢迎回来 MaoMi Chinese！

5月13号到5月15号，美国总统特朗普到北京了。这是他第二次访问中国。在全世界，很多人都在看这个新闻。中国人是怎么看这一次特朗普访问中国的呢？今天，我们一起来聊一聊吧！

在网上，很多人都说： “特朗普在中国的时候，太正经了。” “正经”就是很认真，不乱开玩笑。因为大家觉得，特朗普平时讲话很随便，比较自由，想说什么就说什么，而且动作很多，也很喜欢开玩笑。但是来到中国以后，他看起来突然变得特别安静，特别认真。中国人看到了不一样的他，觉得特别有意思。有人开玩笑说：“特朗普在美国像综艺节目主持人，在中国像来开家长会的爸爸。”家长会，就是家长去学校开会，这些会和他们的孩子有关。

很多人说，特朗普以前讲话的英文特别简单，很容易可以听懂。但是，这几天他在中国的讲话，说了很难的英文，说了很多很长的句子。大家都不太习惯这么严肃的特朗普总统。

还有一些中国网友觉得，其实特朗普很懂场合。“懂场合”就是知道现在是什么情况，知道应该怎么做。他知道什么时候可以随便一点，什么时候应该严肃一点。

很多中国网友看国际新闻的时候，常常有一种“吃瓜”的感觉。“吃瓜”是中国网络很常见的一个词，不是吃真的西瓜，意思只是看热闹。比如别人发生了什么事情，大家在旁边一边看，一边讨论，就叫“吃瓜”。

其实，不只是特朗普，很多外国明星或者名人来到中国参加严肃活动的时候，也会突然变得很安静，也比较严肃。有人说，这是因为中国的文化和美国不一样。人们在严肃的地方都很认真，比如开会的时候，说生意的时候。

你怎么看这一次特朗普总统访问中国呢？欢迎给我们留言，说说你的看法！
translation:
Hello everyone! Welcome back to MaoMi Chinese!

From the 13th to the 15th of May, US President Trump visited Beijing. This was his second visit to China. People all around the world have been following this news. So, how do Chinese people see Trump’s visit to China this time? Today, let’s talk about it together!

Online, many people have been saying: “Trump becomes very serious when he’s in China.” “Serious” here means acting formally and not joking around. This is because many people think that Trump usually speaks in a very casual way. He speaks quite freely, says whatever comes to mind, uses lots of gestures, and enjoys making jokes. But after arriving in China, he suddenly seemed much quieter and much more serious. Chinese people saw a different side of him, and they found it quite interesting. Some people joked: “In America, Trump is like a TV variety show host. In China, he’s like a dad attending a parents’ evening.” A parents’ evening is when parents go to school for meetings about their children.

Many people also said that Trump’s English used to be very simple and easy to understand. But during these few days in China, his speeches sounded much more formal. He used more difficult English and much longer sentences. People were not very used to seeing such a serious President Trump.

Some Chinese internet users also think that Trump actually understands different situations very well. “Understanding the situation” means knowing what kind of environment you are in and knowing how you should behave. He knows when he can be more relaxed and when he should act more seriously.

When many Chinese people follow international news, they often have a feeling called “chi gua”. “Chi gua” is a very common Chinese internet expression. It does not mean actually eating watermelon. It means watching drama or gossip from the side. For example, when something happens and everyone watches and discusses it online, that is called “chi gua”.

Actually, it’s not only Trump. When many foreign celebrities or famous people come to China to attend formal events, they also suddenly become quieter and more serious. Some people say this is because Chinese culture is different from American culture. In formal situations, such as meetings or business discussions, people are usually very serious.

So, what do you think about President Trump’s visit to China this time? Feel free to leave us a comment and share your thoughts!

title: #261 中国和毒品 Drugs in China
transcript:
大家好，欢迎回来 MaoMi Chinese。

今天，我们来聊一个中国和其他国家很不一样的东西：毒品。如果你真的在中国生活过，你会发现，在中国，你几乎不可能看见毒品。

很多普通中国人，一辈子可能都没有见过毒品。毒品，就是 drugs。比如大麻，海洛因，等等，这些都叫毒品。很多中国人第一次知道“大麻”是什么，可能还是因为看外国电影或者外国新闻。大麻，就是 cannabis。有些国家的大麻已经合法了。合法，就是 legal，不犯法。

可是在中国，大部分人一听到“毒品”这个词，就会马上觉得很危险。很多人会想到警察、犯罪、坐牢。坐牢，就是 go to prison。为什么中国人这么怕毒品呢？其实和中国历史有关。

以前，中国发生过一个很有名的历史事件，叫“鸦片战争”。鸦片是一种以前很多人会吸的毒品。那个时候，很多中国人吸鸦片，人们的身体越来越差，国家也越来越弱。所以现在很多中国学生小时候都会在学校学这个历史。老师也常常会说一句话：“远离毒品。” 远离，就是不要靠近， stay away from。

所以，对很多中国人来说，毒品是非常危险的东西。中国法律对毒品非常严格。比如在一些国家，有的人觉得“抽一点大麻是合法的，没关系”。但是在中国，如果有人吸毒、卖毒品、带毒品，他们会坐牢，也可能是死刑。死刑，就是sentence to death。中国人会觉得：“为什么有人要吸毒？”

这里还有一个文化的不同。在一些西方国家，人们可能会觉得：“这是个人自由。” 可是在中国，很多人认为社会的安全更重要。中国人觉得，如果毒品太自由，社会就不安全了。 在中国，大家都认为，一定要禁毒。禁毒，意思是禁止吸毒。很多警察因为禁毒的工作牺牲。牺牲，意思是因为很伟大的事情死了。可以说，中国人不是不喜欢毒品，而是恨毒品。如果一个演员或者歌手吸毒，人们就再也不会听他的歌，也不会看他的电视剧。

对一些人来说，中国禁毒，可能是不自由。但是对于中国人来说，因为禁毒，中国是最安全的国家之一。

你怎么看呢？在你的国家，人们可以用毒品吗？欢迎给我们留言，说说你的看法！
translation:
Hello everyone, welcome back to MaoMi Chinese.

Today, we’re going to talk about something that is very different in China compared with many other countries: drugs. If you have really lived in China, you will notice that it is almost impossible to see drugs in everyday life.

Many ordinary Chinese people may never see drugs in their whole life. “毒品” means drugs. For example, cannabis, heroin, and so on — these are all called drugs. Many Chinese people first learned what cannabis was from foreign films or foreign news. “合法” means legal — not against the law. In some countries, cannabis is already legal.

But in China, when most people hear the word “drugs”, they immediately think of danger. People think about the police, crime, and prison. “坐牢” means to go to prison. Why are Chinese people so afraid of drugs? Actually, it is connected to Chinese history.

A long time ago, China had a very famous historical event called the Opium War. Opium was a kind of drug that many people used in the past. At that time, many Chinese people smoked opium, people became less healthy, and the country also became weaker. Because of this, many Chinese students learn about this history at school when they are young. Teachers also often say: “远离毒品” — stay away from drugs. “远离” means do not go near something.

So, for many Chinese people, drugs are extremely dangerous. Chinese law is also very strict about drugs. For example, in some countries, people may think: “Smoking a little cannabis is legal, so it’s fine.” But in China, if someone takes drugs, sells drugs, or carries drugs, they may go to prison, and in some cases they may even receive the death penalty. “死刑” means sentence to death. Many Chinese people will think: “Why would anyone want to take drugs?”

There is also a cultural difference here. In some Western countries, people may think: “This is personal freedom.” But in China, many people believe that public safety is more important. Chinese people think that if drugs become too free and common, society will become unsafe. In China, most people believe that drugs must be banned. “禁毒” means stopping and banning drugs. Many police officers have died while doing anti-drug work. “牺牲” means to die for an important or great cause. You could say that Chinese people do not simply dislike drugs — they hate them. If an actor or singer takes drugs, many people will never listen to their songs or watch their TV dramas again.

For some people, China’s anti-drug policy may seem less free. But for many Chinese people, because of these strict anti-drug laws, China is one of the safest countries in the world.

What do you think? In your country, can people use drugs? Leave us a comment and tell us your opinion!

title: #262 China's Electric Car Boom 中国电车
transcript:
大家好，欢迎回来 MaoMi Chinese。今天，我们来聊一个这几年在中国特别火的东西，那就是电车。

如果你已经很多年没有去过中国了，那么你回中国的时候，可能会发现：路上的电车怎么这么多？

以前，中国的马路上大部分都是汽油车。汽油车，就是需要加汽油的车。但是现在，不管是在北京，上海这样的大城市，还是在很多小城市，你都会看到越来越多的电车。

那么，为什么中国有这么多电车呢？

其实，十多年前，中国的电车不多。那个时候，很多人不喜欢电车。因为电车有几个问题。第一个问题是贵，要花很多钱。第二个问题是充电不方便。那个时候，充电站很少，所以很多人担心车没有电。第三个问题是续航。续航，就是车充满一次电以后，可以开多远。如果续航太短，人们就会担心开到一半没有电了。

后来，中国政府开始支持新能源车的发展。新能源车，就是使用电力或者其他新能源的汽车。政府给买车的人补贴。补贴，就是政府帮你付一些钱。这样，买电车就便宜了。中国也开始建越来越多的充电站。现在，在很多中国城市，你都能看到很多电车的充电站。

除了政府的支持，中国公司自己也发展得很快。他们花了很多时间和钱去研究电池技术。电池越来越好，越来越便宜，续航也越来越长。以前，很多电车开两三百公里就需要充电。现在，有些电车充电一次可以开五六百公里。

那么，中国人为什么这么喜欢买电车呢？

最重要的原因之一，就是省钱，也就是花更少的钱。一般来说，电费比汽油便宜，所以每天开车的人会发现，开电车的钱比开汽油车少。给汽油车加油一次要几百元，给电车充电一次只要几十元。

第二个原因是安静。因为电车用的是电池，所以比汽油车更安静。

第三个原因是科技。现在很多中国电车都有很大的屏幕。有些车可以帮我们停车，也可以帮助我们开车。

如果你下次去中国，可以看一看马路上的汽车。你可能会看见，十辆车里面，有一半都是电车。

你坐过中国的电车吗？你喜欢电车还是汽油车呢？欢迎告诉给我们留言，说说你的想法！
translation:
Hello everyone, welcome back to MaoMi Chinese. Today, we're going to talk about something that has become extremely popular in China over the past few years: electric cars.

If you haven't been to China for many years, you might notice something surprising when you go back: why are there so many electric cars on the roads?

In the past, most vehicles on Chinese roads were petrol cars. A petrol car is a car that runs on petrol. But nowadays, whether you're in a large city like Beijing or Shanghai, or in a smaller city, you'll see more and more electric cars everywhere.

So, why are there so many electric cars in China?

Actually, just over ten years ago, electric cars were not very common in China. At that time, many people didn't like them because they had several problems. The first problem was that they were expensive. The second problem was that charging wasn't convenient. There were very few charging stations, so many people worried that their car would run out of power. The third problem was driving range. Driving range means how far a car can travel on a full charge. If the range was too short, people worried that the battery would run out before they reached their destination.

Later, the Chinese government began supporting the development of new energy vehicles. New energy vehicles are cars powered by electricity or other alternative energy sources. The government provided subsidies to people who bought these cars. A subsidy means the government pays part of the cost for you. As a result, electric cars became more affordable. China also started building more and more charging stations. Today, in many Chinese cities, you can see charging stations almost everywhere.

Besides government support, Chinese companies also developed very quickly. They invested a lot of time and money into battery technology. Batteries became better, cheaper, and able to travel longer distances. In the past, many electric cars needed charging after only 200 or 300 kilometres. Today, some electric cars can travel 500 or 600 kilometres on a single charge. So why do Chinese people like buying electric cars so much?

One of the most important reasons is that they save money. In other words, they cost less to run. Generally speaking, electricity is cheaper than petrol, so people who drive every day find that using an electric car costs less than driving a petrol car. Filling up a petrol car can cost several hundred yuan, while charging an electric car may cost only a few dozen yuan.

The second reason is that they're quiet. Because electric cars run on batteries, they produce much less noise than petrol cars.

The third reason is technology. Many Chinese electric cars now come with large screens. Some can help you park, and some can even assist with driving.

If you visit China next time, take a look at the cars on the roads. You might find that out of every ten cars, five are electric.

Have you ever ridden in an electric car in China? Do you prefer electric cars or petrol cars? Leave us a comment and let us know what you think!
