title: #263 The Goose Leg Auntie Scandal 鹅腿阿姨
transcript:
大家好，欢迎回来 MaoMi Chinese。

最近，中国有一个很火的人，她叫“鹅腿阿姨”。如果你看中国新闻，或者刷小红书，你可能已经知道她的故事。

鹅腿阿姨是一位在北京卖烤鹅腿的阿姨。很多年来，她经常在北京大学和清华大学附近卖烤鹅腿。因为她卖的鹅腿很好吃，而且人也很热情，所以很多大学生都喜欢她。后来，越来越多学生在网上分享她的故事。大家觉得她很努力，也很亲切。慢慢地，她变成了一个网红。网红，就是 internet celebrity，意思是在网上很有名的人。

前几年，鹅腿阿姨还上过很多新闻。因为她卖的鹅腿很好吃，但是想买的人太多了，经常不够。北京大学和清华大学的学生都想买她的鹅腿。网上甚至有人开玩笑说，两所中国最好的大学终于开始“比赛”了，不过他们比的不是学习成绩，而是比谁可以买到鹅腿。

但是最近，事情突然有了变化。前不久，有人在网上说，鹅腿阿姨卖的不是鹅腿，是更便宜的鸭腿。很多网友听到以后都很惊讶。后来，鹅腿阿姨解释说，很多年前她卖的的确是鹅腿。但是后来很难买到鹅腿，所以她改成了鸭腿。不过，她一直没有改名字，所以大家还是叫她鹅腿阿姨。

现在，中国很多网友都在讨论这件事情。有些人觉得，如果卖的是鸭腿，就应该告诉顾客。因为鹅腿和鸭腿不一样，价格也不一样。 也有一些人说，他们以前吃鹅腿阿姨卖的鹅腿以后，拉肚子了，生病了，所以鹅腿阿姨的东西可能不太干净。有些人说，虽然鹅腿阿姨说自己赚的钱不多，但是她每天都能卖很多鸭腿，每个鸭腿卖16元，她每天能赚两万多元。也有人说，中国的大学生还是太单纯了，让鹅腿阿姨骗了那么久。单纯，意思是人很简单，太善良，很容易相信别人。

一个普通卖烤腿的阿姨，因为大学生喜欢她，后来变成网红。现在，又因为鸭腿和鹅腿的问题，又让大家开始讨论食品安全的问题。现在，鹅腿阿姨很可能会因为这个事情被惩罚。

你怎么看这个事呢？你觉得鹅腿阿姨错了吗？欢迎给我们留言，说说你的看法。
translation:
Hello everyone, welcome back to MaoMi Chinese.

Recently, there has been a very popular person in China called “Goose Leg Auntie” (Étuǐ Āyí). If you follow Chinese news or browse Xiaohongshu, you may already know her story.

Goose Leg Auntie is a woman who sells roasted goose legs in Beijing. For many years, she regularly sold them near Peking University and Tsinghua University. Because her goose legs were delicious and she was very friendly, many university students liked her. Later, more and more students shared her story online. People thought she was hardworking and approachable. Gradually, she became an internet celebrity. An internet celebrity is someone who becomes famous online.

A few years ago, Goose Leg Auntie appeared in the news many times. Because her goose legs were so popular, there were often more people wanting to buy them than there were goose legs available. Students from both Peking University and Tsinghua University wanted to buy her food. People online even joked that the two best universities in China had finally started “competing” with each other. However, they were not competing over academic results, but over who could buy her goose legs.

But recently, things suddenly changed. Not long ago, someone posted online that what Goose Leg Auntie was selling was not actually goose legs, but the cheaper duck legs. Many people were shocked when they heard this. Later, Goose Leg Auntie explained that she had originally sold goose legs many years ago. However, it later became difficult to buy goose legs, so she switched to duck legs. Nevertheless, she never changed her name, so people continued to call her Goose Leg Auntie.

Now, many Chinese internet users are discussing this issue. Some people believe that if she was selling duck legs, she should have told her customers, because goose legs and duck legs are different and their prices are different as well. Others say that after eating the duck legs she sold, they had diarrhoea or became ill, suggesting that her food might not have been very hygienic. Some people point out that although Goose Leg Auntie said she did not earn much money, she sold a large number of duck legs every day. Each duck leg sold for 16 yuan, and some people estimate that she could earn tens of thousands of yuan per day. Others argue that Chinese university students were simply too trusting and allowed themselves to be misled for so long. Trusting means being simple, kind-hearted and easily willing to believe others.

An ordinary woman selling roasted legs became an internet influencer because university students liked her. Now, because of the issue of duck legs and goose legs, people have once again started discussing food safety. Goose Leg Auntie may face punishment because of this incident.

What do you think about this story? Do you think Goose Leg Auntie was wrong? Feel free to leave us a comment and share your thoughts.

title: #264 让人又爱又恨的中国足球 The Chinese Football Team: Loved and Hated
transcript:
大家好，欢迎回到 MaoMi Chinese！

最近，世界上很多人都在看足球世界杯。说到足球，你可能会想到巴西、阿根廷、英国、德国。但是，你会想到中国吗？ 很多人会问：中国有这么多人，为什么足球踢得不好？中国人喜欢足球吗？中国人怎么看自己的国家队？今天，我们一起来聊一聊中国的足球吧！

其实，中国人很喜欢足球。在中国，足球是最受欢迎的运动之一。很多人从小就踢足球。每到世界杯，很多中国球迷都会熬夜。球迷，意思是喜欢看足球比赛的人。熬夜，意思是很晚睡觉，或者不睡觉。

中国有很多足球迷。有的人喜欢阿根廷队，有的人喜欢巴西队，也有很多人喜欢英国的球队。但是有一个有趣的问题：中国人喜欢足球，可是不一定喜欢中国男足，意思是中国男子国家足球队。

为什么呢？因为中国男足的成绩一直不好。 中国男足只参加过一次世界杯，那是在2002年。从那以后，中国队一直没能参加世界杯的比赛。

这些年，中国足球花了很多钱。中国请过外国教练，也买过很多外国球员。大家本来希望中国足球越来越好，但是其实，中国足球的成绩没有更好。

那么，中国男足为什么这么差呢？很多中国人有不同的看法，意思是不同的想法。有的人觉得，中国的小朋友学习太忙，没有太多时间运动。和很多国家相比，中国孩子踢球的机会比较少。

还有人觉得，中国足球的管理有问题。过去几年，中国足球有过很多腐败，一些官员、教练和球员违反法律。这也影响了中国足球的发展。当然，也有人觉得，中国足球的问题没有那么简单。足球是需要很多年发展的运动。好的球员、好的教练、好的比赛，少一个都不行。

中国的网友这样开玩笑：当你觉得生活很难的时候，看看中国足球，你就觉得不难了。意思是，中国的足球队已经是最糟糕的了！

虽然一次又一次失望，但是很多球迷还是希望有一天，中国队能够再次进入世界杯。也许，这就是足球的魅力。魅力，意思是让人喜欢它的原因。
translation:
Hello everyone, and welcome back to MaoMi Chinese!

Recently, people all over the world have been watching the FIFA World Cup. When you think of football, you might think of Brazil, Argentina, England or Germany. But do you think of China?Many people ask: China has such a large population, so why isn't the national football team very good? Do Chinese people like football? And what do they think of their own national team? Today let’s talk about football in China!

The truth is, Chinese people really do love football. In China, football is one of the most popular sports. Many people start playing when they're children. Whenever the World Cup comes around, lots of Chinese football fans stay up late to watch the matches. Football fan means someone who enjoys watching football matches. To stay up late means to go to bed very late, or not sleep at all.

There are many football fans in China. Some support Argentina, some support Brazil, and many also support English clubs. But here's an interesting question: Chinese people love football, but that doesn't always mean they love the Chinese men's national team. The Chinese men's national team refers to China's national football team for men.

Why is that?

Because the team hasn't had good results for a long time. In fact, China has only qualified for the FIFA World Cup once, back in 2002. Since then, the team hasn't managed to qualify again.

Over the years, China has spent a lot of money on football. The country has hired foreign coaches and brought in many foreign players. People hoped Chinese football would keep improving, but in reality, the results haven't got any better.

So why is the Chinese men's national team so weak?

Many Chinese people have different opinions. Opinion means what someone thinks. Some people believe that Chinese children spend too much time studying and don't have enough time for sport. Compared with many other countries, Chinese children have fewer opportunities to play football.

Others think the problem is the way Chinese football is managed. Over the past few years, there have been many corruption scandals in Chinese football. Some officials, coaches and players broke the law. This has also affected the development of football in China.

Of course, some people believe the problem is more complicated than that. Football is a sport that takes many years to develop. You need good players, good coaches and a strong league. If even one of these is missing, it's very difficult to succeed.

Chinese internet users often joke like this: "When life feels difficult, just look at Chinese football, and suddenly life doesn't seem so difficult anymore."

In other words, they're joking that the Chinese national team is already the worst!

Even though they've been disappointed again and again, many Chinese fans still hope that one day China will qualify for the World Cup again.

Perhaps that's the magic of football. Magic means the special quality that makes people love it.

title: #265 Would You Date an AI Robot? 你想和AI机器人谈恋爱吗？
transcript:
大家好，欢迎回到 MaoMi Chinese！

最近，中国网上有一个新闻，让很多人讨论。一家中国公司发明了AI 机器人伴侣。伴侣，也就是我们的另一半，比如男朋友，女朋友，丈夫，妻子。AI机器人伴侣真的可能吗？将来，人们会真的有机器人伴侣吗？中国人是怎么看这个AI机器人伴侣的？今天，我们一起来聊一聊吧！

这个中国公司的机器人，最便宜的十多万人民币，最贵的99万人民币，有男的机器人，也有女的机器人，但是只有成年人才可以买。成年人，也就是超过了18岁的人，不是小孩子的人。这个机器人可以和你聊天，记住你的习惯，也会关心你的心情，和你谈恋爱。大家是怎么看这个机器人伴侣的呢？

有一些人觉得，这样还不错。现在很多中国年轻人工作很忙，生活压力也很大。每天工作，下班以后已经没有什么时间认识新朋友，也不太想谈恋爱。有些人觉得，恋爱虽然很好，但是也很累。两个人要花很多时间在一起，也可能会吵架，会分手。可是机器人不会生气，也不会离开。还有人说，如果机器人真的和人一样聪明，他们可能更想和机器人伴侣一起生活。

但是，也有很多人觉得，这是一个很可怕的事情。因为机器人说"我喜欢你"，只是电脑程序，它不会真的开心，也不会真的伤心。真正的人和人之间，会有不同的想法，会有误会，也会吵架，但是也因为这样，我们才会互相了解，一起成长。如果有一天，越来越多人选择和 AI 在一起，那么我们会不会变得越来越孤独？我们还会成长吗？我们还会进步吗？

大家都知道，现在中国结婚的人越来越少，出生率也越来越低。很多年轻人不是不想结婚，而是觉得房子太贵，养孩子太贵，生活压力太大。

我觉得，这个新闻最有意思的地方，是它让我们看到，现在很多人需要的，或许不是一个完美的机器人，而是有人愿意听自己说话，有人愿意和自己在一起。是 AI 变得越来越像人了，还是人与人相处变得越来越困难了？这是一个很有意思的问题。你怎么看呢？如果未来真的有一天，AI 机器人已经和真人没有什么区别，你会愿意和它谈恋爱，甚至一起生活吗？欢迎给我们留言，说说你的看法！
translation:
Hello everyone, welcome back to MaoMi Chinese!

Recently, there has been a piece of news in China that has caused a lot of discussion online. A Chinese company has created an AI robot companion. A companion means the person we are close to, such as a boyfriend, girlfriend, husband or wife. Is an AI robot companion really possible? In the future, will people actually have robot partners? And what do Chinese people think about AI robot companions? Today, let’s talk about it together!

The robots made by this Chinese company are not cheap. The cheapest one costs more than 100,000 RMB, while the most expensive one costs 990,000 RMB. There are both male and female versions, but only adults can buy them. Adults means people who are over 18 years old, not children. These robots can chat with you, remember your habits, care about your feelings, and even have a romantic relationship with you. So, what do people think about these robot companions?

Some people think this is actually not a bad idea. Nowadays, many young people in China are very busy with work, and they also have a lot of pressure in their lives. After working every day, they do not have much time to meet new people, and some of them do not really want to date. Some people think that although love and relationships can be wonderful, they can also be tiring. Two people need to spend a lot of time together, and they may argue or even break up. However, a robot will not get angry, and it will not leave you. Some people even say that if robots really become as intelligent as humans, they might prefer living with an AI partner.

However, many people also think this is quite a worrying thing. This is because when a robot says "I love you", it is only following a computer programme. It does not truly feel happy, and it does not truly feel sad. Between real people, we have different opinions, misunderstandings, and arguments. But because of these experiences, we learn to understand each other and grow together. If one day more and more people choose to be with AI instead of real people, will we become lonelier? Will we still grow? Will we still improve ourselves?

Everyone knows that in China, fewer people are getting married, and the birth rate is also falling. Many young people do not avoid marriage because they do not want love or family. Instead, they feel that houses are too expensive, raising children is too expensive, and life pressure is too high.

I think the most interesting thing about this news is that it shows us that what many people really need may not be a perfect robot, but someone who is willing to listen to them and someone who wants to be with them. Is AI becoming more and more like humans, or is it becoming harder and harder for humans to build relationships with each other? This is a really interesting question.

What do you think? If one day AI robots become almost impossible to tell apart from real people, would you be willing to date one, or even live with one? Leave us a comment and share your thoughts!

title: #266 China’s New Maths Stars 中国的数学新星
transcript:
大家好，欢迎回来 MaoMi Chinese！

最近，在中国，很多人都在讨论两位中国数学家——王虹和邓煜。他们获得了数学界最高的奖之一：菲尔兹奖。大家讨论他们获奖，也讨论一个很有意思的问题。为什么他们都是中国最好的大学，北京大学的学生，但只有在国外做研究以后，才有了这么大的成功？今天，我们就来聊聊这个新闻，也聊一聊一些和学习有关的词语。

首先，我们来说说菲尔兹奖。很多人都叫它”数学的诺贝尔奖”。菲尔兹奖每四年一次，获奖的时候，数学家不能超过四十岁。所以拿到这个奖，真的非常不容易。今年，两位获奖者，王虹和邓煜，都出生在中国，也都曾经在北京大学学习数学。北京大学是中国最好的大学之一，也就是说，王虹和邓煜，在高考，都有非常好的成绩。后来，他们都去了国外继续学习、做研究，最后有了很厉害的研究成果，也获得了菲尔兹奖。

很多中国人看到这个消息，都觉得非常骄傲。骄傲，就是为他们感到高兴和自豪，也因为他们是中国人高兴。很多人觉得，他们都是中国培养的人才。培养，就是帮助一个人成长、学习、进步。比如，学校培养学生，公司培养年轻员工，父母培养孩子的兴趣。虽然他们后来去了国外，但是很多网友觉得，他们年轻的时候在中国学了数学，所以中国的教育也给了他们很多好处。

但是，有人也有不同的看法。有网友说，为什么他们都是在国外成功？为什么不是在中国完成这些重要的研究？于是，很多人开始讨论，中国的大学，能不能支持年轻数学家的发展。支持，就是帮助别人，让别人更容易成功。比如，老师支持学生，父母支持孩子，学校支持老师做研究。研究，就是认真地学习一个问题，希望发现新的知识。比如，科学家做研究，医生做研究，数学家当然也做研究。很多人认为，要做好研究，要很多条件，比如时间、资金、优秀的老师和同学，还有一个可以自由讨论、自由思考的环境。如果这些条件都很好，年轻人就更容易做出新的发现。

这样的讨论，不只发生在中国。很多国家都会有同样的问题：优秀的人才应该留在自己的国家，还是应该去国外学习和工作？一个国家应该怎样培养年轻人才？一个国家的大学应该怎么样支持年轻人才做研究？这些问题，到今天都没有一个简单的答案，每个人都会有自己的看法。

最后，我们来复习今天的新词。 骄傲，就是因为别人的成功感到高兴和自豪，这个人常常和我们有关，比如我们的朋友，家人，或者同一个国家的人。 培养，就是帮助一个人成长、学习、进步。 支持，就是帮助别人，让别人更容易成功。 研究，就是认真地学习一个问题，希望发现新的知识。

那你怎么看呢？如果一个年轻人有机会去国外学习，你觉得是一件好事吗？你认为，一个国家应该怎样培养优秀的人才？欢迎给我们留言，说说你的看法！
translation:
Hello everyone, welcome back to MaoMi Chinese!

Recently, many people in China have been talking about two Chinese mathematicians, Wang Hong and Deng Yu. They won one of the highest honours in mathematics: the Fields Medal. People are not only talking about their award, but also discussing a very interesting question. They both studied at Peking University, one of the best universities in China. So why was it only after they went abroad to do research that they achieved such great success? Today, let’s talk about this news story and learn some useful words related to studying.

First, let’s talk about the Fields Medal. Many people call it the “Nobel Prize of Mathematics”. The Fields Medal is awarded once every four years, and winners must be under the age of forty. So receiving this award is really not easy. This year, both winners, Wang Hong and Deng Yu, were born in China and both studied mathematics at Peking University. Peking University is one of the best universities in China. In other words, they both achieved excellent results in the Gaokao, China’s university entrance examination. Later, they both went abroad to continue their studies and carry out research. In the end, they produced outstanding research and won the Fields Medal.

Many people in China felt very proud when they heard the news. Jiāo’ào, or “to feel proud”, means feeling happy and proud because of someone else’s success. In this case, people also felt proud because Wang Hong and Deng Yu are Chinese. Many people believe they are talented people who were trained in China. Here, let’s learn the word péiyǎng, “to nurture” or “to develop”. It means helping someone grow, learn and improve. For example, schools nurture students, companies develop young employees, and parents cultivate their children’s interests. Although Wang Hong and Deng Yu later went abroad, many people think they learnt mathematics in China when they were young, so the Chinese education system also played an important role in their success.

However, not everyone agrees. Some people asked, “Why did they become successful abroad? Why didn’t they complete this important research in China?” This led many people to discuss whether Chinese universities can support the development of young mathematicians. Zhīchí, “to support”, means helping someone so that they are more likely to succeed. For example, teachers support students, parents support their children, and universities support teachers in carrying out research. Another useful word is yánjiū, “research”. It means studying a question carefully in the hope of discovering new knowledge. Scientists do research, doctors do research, and of course mathematicians do research as well. Many people believe that good research needs many different conditions, such as enough time, enough funding, excellent teachers and classmates, and an environment where people can discuss ideas and think freely. If all these conditions are available, young researchers are much more likely to make new discoveries.

This kind of discussion doesn’t only happen in China. Many countries face the same questions. Should talented people stay in their own country, or should they go abroad to study and work? How should a country nurture young talent? How should universities support young researchers? Even today, there are no simple answers to these questions, and everyone has their own opinion.

Finally, let’s review today’s new words.

Jiāo’ào means feeling happy and proud because of someone else’s success. Usually, that person is connected to us, such as a friend, a family member, or someone from the same country.

Péiyǎng means helping someone grow, learn and improve.

Zhīchí means helping someone so that they are more likely to succeed.

Yánjiū means studying a question carefully in the hope of discovering new knowledge.

So, what do you think? If a young person has the opportunity to study abroad, do you think that’s a good thing? How do you think a country should nurture talented people? Leave us a comment and let us know your thoughts!

title: #267 “Pin” the Chinese Way to Save Money 拼多多
transcript:
大家好，欢迎回来 MaoMi Chinese！

今天我们来聊一个很多中国人都非常熟悉的东西——拼多多。如果你在中国生活过，或者经常看中国的新闻和短视频，你可能经常会听到这个名字。拼多多是中国一个非常大的购物网站和app，但是你有没有想过，为什么它叫“拼多多”？“拼”到底是什么意思？

“拼”有很多不同的意思，但是在拼多多里，它的意思是，是把不同的人、不同的东西放在一起，大家一起做一件事情。比如说，一个人买一件东西可能要100块钱，但是如果十个人一起买，商家可能就可以便宜一点。大家一起买，这就叫“拼”。

所以，拼多多里的“拼”，就是大家一起买东西。因为人多了，东西可能就更便宜。这个想法非常简单，但是在中国特别受欢迎。为什么？当然是因为便宜。

中国人买东西的时候，经常会说一个词，叫“性价比”。“性价比”简单来说，就是花比较少的钱，买到比较好的东西。所以，如果同样的东西，在一个地方卖100块钱，在另一个地方只卖70块钱，很多中国人当然会选择70块钱的。

所以拼多多就非常有性价比。它会让你觉得：“我自己买可能比较贵，但是如果我们一起买，就可以便宜一点。”而且在拼多多上，你不一定真的认识和你一起“拼”的人。拼多多会帮你找到其他想买同样东西的人。

除了拼多多，我们生活中也经常用“拼”这个意思。

比如“拼车”。如果两个人要去同一个地方，就可以一起坐车，一起付车费。比如本来一个人打车要100块钱，两个人一起拼车，每个人可能只需要50块钱。

还有“拼单”。比如你想买一件东西，但是发现买两件会更便宜，那么你就可以找朋友一起买。你买一件，他买一件，这就叫“拼单”。

还有现在外卖平台上很常见的“拼好饭”。简单来说，也是把不同的订单放在一起，让大家可以用更便宜的价格吃到饭。

所以“拼”其实就是一个非常有意思的东西，那就是，大家都要买一样的东西，一起买，然后大家都可以得到一点好处。一个人买不一定便宜，但是大家一起买，就可能便宜，有性价比。

你在中国用过拼多多吗？拼过车吗？欢迎给我们留言，和我们分享哦！
translation:
Hello everyone, and welcome back to MaoMi Chinese!

Today, we’re going to talk about something that is very familiar to many Chinese people — Pinduoduo. If you have lived in China, or often watch Chinese news and short videos, you may have heard this name many times. Pinduoduo is a very large online shopping platform and app in China. But have you ever wondered why it is called “Pinduoduo”? What does “拼” actually mean?

“拼” has several different meanings, but in Pinduoduo, it means putting different people or things together and doing something together. For example, one person might have to pay 100 yuan for something. But if ten people buy it together, the seller might be able to offer it at a lower price. Buying something together like this is called “拼”.

So, the “拼” in Pinduoduo means buying things together. When more people buy something, it may become cheaper. It’s a very simple idea, but it is particularly popular in China. Why? Of course, because it’s cheap!

When Chinese people buy things, they often use a word called “性价比”. Basically, “性价比” means getting something better while spending less money. So, if exactly the same thing costs 100 yuan in one place but only 70 yuan somewhere else, many Chinese people will naturally choose the one that costs 70 yuan.

So Pinduoduo offers very good value for money. It makes you think, “It might be more expensive if I buy it on my own, but if we buy it together, it could be cheaper.” And on Pinduoduo, you don’t necessarily know the people you are “拼” with. Pinduoduo can help you find other people who want to buy the same thing.

Apart from Pinduoduo, we also use “拼” in everyday life.

For example, “拼车”. If two people are going to the same place, they can travel together and share the cost. If taking a taxi on your own costs 100 yuan, for example, two people can “拼车”, and each person might only need to pay 50 yuan.

Another example is “拼单”. Let’s say you want to buy something, but you find that buying two is cheaper. You can ask a friend to buy it with you. You buy one, they buy one, and this is called “拼单”.

And there is also “拼好饭”, which you can often see on food delivery platforms in China. Basically, different orders are put together so that people can get their meals at a cheaper price.

So, “拼” is actually a very interesting idea. It means that people want to buy the same thing, so they buy it together, and everyone can get some benefit from it. Buying something on your own may not be cheaper, but buying it together can make it cheaper and give you better value for money.

Have you ever used Pinduoduo in China? Have you ever “拼车”? Leave us a comment and share your experience with us!

title: #268 Why Did a “Terrible Film” Become So Popular? 为什么人们看《牛来》？
transcript:
大家好，欢迎回来 MaoMi Chinese。今天我们来聊一部最近在中国网上很多人讨论的电影，叫《牛来》。你可能会觉得，这个名字很奇怪。“牛来”是什么意思？为什么一部电影会叫这个名字？更有意思的是，这部电影一开始没有多少人知道，但是后来突然有很多人去电影院看。为什么呢？我们今天就来聊一聊。

我们先说一下《牛来》的故事。这是一部动画片，主要讲一只小牛，叫“牛来”，它和它妈妈的故事。牛来小时候不会走路，后来慢慢长大，和妈妈一起生活，也遇到了一个小豹子。它们一起遇到了危险，还遇到了很多狼。最后，牛来和小豹子一起离开，而牛妈妈为了保护牛来，留下来面对狼。这是一个小牛成长和母亲的爱的故事。

但是，这部电影真正引起大家注意的，不是这个故事，而是它的制作。很多人看完以后觉得，这部电影做得很难看，动画很丑。慢慢地，很多人在网上吐槽这个电影。 “吐槽”，意思是发现一个东西有问题，然后说出来，经常是开玩笑地说。有人吐槽《牛来》，说：“这真的是电影吗？”

但是最有意思的事情来了。原本没有什么人看《牛来》，后来看了的人说这个电影很丑，很难看，却有越来越多人知道了《牛来》。然后，有些人开始想：“真的有这么不好看吗？我要自己去看看。”所以，很多人去电影院看《牛来》，其实原因很简单：他们想看看一部“烂片”到底有多烂。

“烂片”，意思就是很糟糕的电影。比如，故事不好，画面不好，演员的表演不好，都可以说是“烂片”。所以，有一些网友就觉得很有意思：如果大家都说《牛来》是一部烂片，那我就去看看，它到底有多烂。有一点像看一个很奇怪的东西。你明明知道它可能不好看，但是你还是想看看有多奇怪。

还有一个原因，我觉得可能更加有意思。有一些网友说，现在电影院里好看的电影越来越少了。如果没有特别想看的电影，那为什么不去看《牛来》呢？有些人不是因为觉得《牛来》很好看才买票，而是因为他们觉得，其他电影也没有特别好，不想去电影院花钱看。既然不知道看什么，那不如去看一部大家都在讨论的《牛来》。至少，看完了《牛来》，还能和朋友一起吐槽烂片。

你会不会为了“看看一部烂片到底有多烂”，花钱去电影院看一部电影？还是说，如果没有好看的电影，你宁愿待在家里也不去电影院？欢迎给我们留言，说说你的看法！
translation:
Hello everyone, and welcome back to MaoMi Chinese. Today, we’re going to talk about a film that a lot of people in China have been talking about online recently. It’s called Niulai. You might think the name sounds a bit strange. What does “Niulai” mean? And why would a film have this name? What’s even more interesting is that, at first, hardly anyone knew about this film. But later, suddenly, lots of people started going to the cinema to watch it. So why? That’s what we’re going to talk about today.

Let’s start with the story of Niulai. It’s an animated film about a little cow called Niulai and his mum. When Niulai is young, he can’t walk, but he slowly grows up and lives with his mum. He also meets a little leopard. Together, they face some dangers and meet a lot of wolves. In the end, Niulai and the little leopard leave together, while Niulai’s mum stays behind to protect him from the wolves. So basically, it’s a story about a little cow growing up and a mother’s love.

But what really got people talking about this film wasn’t the story. It was the way the film was made. After watching it, many people thought it looked really bad. They thought the animation looked ugly, too. Gradually, lots of people started talking about the film online. There’s a Chinese word, “吐槽”, which means pointing out something you think is wrong or funny, often in a joking way. So, for example, people were making fun of Niulai online. Some people even said, “Is this really a film?”

But here comes the most interesting part. At first, hardly anyone was watching Niulai. Then the people who did watch it started saying that it looked really bad. But strangely, more and more people began to hear about it. And then some people started thinking, “Is it really that bad? I want to see it for myself.” So, for many people, the reason for going to the cinema was actually quite simple: they wanted to see just how bad a “烂片” could be.

“烂片” means a really bad film, or a film that is considered to be very poor quality. For example, if the story is bad, the visuals are bad, or the acting is bad, people might call it a “烂片”. So some people online thought this was quite funny. If everyone was saying that Niulai was a terrible film, they thought, “Well, I’m going to see it and find out just how bad it really is.” It’s a bit like looking at something really strange. You already know you might not like it, but you still want to see just how strange it is.

There’s another reason that I think is even more interesting. Some people online said that there are fewer and fewer good films in cinemas these days. If there isn’t a film that you really want to see, then why not go and watch Niulai? Some people didn’t buy a ticket because they thought Niulai was going to be a great film. Instead, they felt that the other films weren’t particularly good either, so they didn’t really want to spend money going to the cinema to watch them. If you don’t know what to watch, you might as well watch the film that everyone is talking about. At least after watching Niulai, you can have a good laugh with your friends and complain about how bad the film was.

So, would you spend money to go to the cinema just to see how bad a terrible film really is? Or, if there aren’t any good films, would you rather stay at home and not go to the cinema at all? Let us know what you think!

title: #269 Why Chinese Young People Joining Senior’s Tours? 中国年轻人爱上老年旅行团
transcript:
大家好，欢迎回来 MaoMi Chinese！

你喜欢旅行吗？你喜欢一个人旅行，还是和朋友一起旅行，还是喜欢跟团旅行？跟团，就是跟着旅行团。旅行团，就是一起旅行的很多个人，他们可能认识，也可能不认识。

如果你去旅行，你会选择什么样的旅行团呢？今天，我们来聊聊一个有意思的事情：现在，越来越多的年轻人开始参加老年旅行团。

什么是老年旅行团呢？就是主要给老年人准备的旅行团。比如，旅行团里的大部分人可能是五十岁、六十岁，甚至七十多岁的老人。

以前，我们可能觉得，年轻人应该和年轻人一起旅行，老年人应该和老年人一起旅行。但是，现在有些年轻人开始选择和老年人一起旅行了。这是为什么呢？

首先，老年旅行团通常比较便宜。

很多年轻人刚开始工作，工资不高，但是又想出去玩。如果自己计划旅行，可能要花很多时间，也可能要花很多钱。但是，参加旅行团就简单多了。旅行团会安排好交通、酒店，还有每天去哪里玩。有时候，吃饭也不用自己安排。对一些年轻人来说，这样的旅行很方便，也很省钱。

其次，老年旅行团的老人们通常很热情。

他们可能会主动和年轻人聊天，也可能会关心年轻人有没有吃饱、累不累。有时候，他们还会和年轻人分享水果、零食，或者给年轻人介绍有意思的地方。

对一些年轻人来说，和这些热情的老人一起旅行，就像和自己的爷爷奶奶一起旅行一样，感觉很温暖，也很开心。

当然，老年旅行团也有一些坏处。

这些旅行团的行程通常很紧张，经常早上五六点就要起床，因为老年人通常很早就起床了。早上起来以后，大家还要马上坐车去下一个地方。而且，旅行团经常要坐很久的大巴车。有时候，一坐就是几个小时。对年轻人来说，这也可能有一点累。所以，如果你喜欢睡懒觉，或者喜欢自由地安排自己的时间，那么老年旅行团可能不太适合你。

但是，和老年人一起旅行，还是有很多有意思的地方。

因为大家的生活经验不一样，喜欢的东西也不一样。年轻人可能喜欢拍照、看手机、在网上分享自己的旅行。老年人可能更喜欢聊天，看风景，了解当地的文化。在旅行的过程中，年轻人可以听老人讲以前的故事，老人也可以了解年轻人的生活。有时候，大家虽然年龄差很多，但是很容易成为朋友。

如果你想省钱，也想认识一些热情的老年人，听听他们的故事，那么老年旅行团是一个不错的选择。

如果有机会，你愿意参加老年旅行团吗？你愿意和比自己大二三十岁的人一起旅行吗？

欢迎给我们留言，说说你的想法！
translation:
Hello, and welcome back to MaoMi Chinese!

Do you like travelling? Do you prefer travelling alone, travelling with friends, or joining a tour group? 跟团 means travelling with a tour group. A 旅行团 is a group of people travelling together. They may know each other, or they may not know each other at all.

If you go travelling, what kind of tour group would you choose? Today, we’re going to talk about something interesting: more and more young people are starting to join tour groups for older travellers.

What is a tour group for older travellers? It’s a tour group mainly designed for older people. For example, most of the people in the group might be in their fifties or sixties, or even in their seventies.

In the past, we might have thought that young people should travel with other young people, and older people should travel with other older people. But now, some young people are choosing to travel with older people. Why is that?

First of all, tours for older travellers are usually cheaper.

Many young people have only just started working. They don’t earn much yet, but they still want to go travelling. If they plan a trip themselves, it might take a lot of time and money. But joining a tour group makes things much easier. The tour group arranges transport, hotels and places to visit each day. Sometimes, meals are organised too. For some young people, this kind of trip is convenient and saves money.

Secondly, the older people on these tours are often very friendly and welcoming.

They might start conversations with younger travellers. They might also check whether they’ve had enough to eat or whether they’re tired. Sometimes, they share fruit and snacks with younger people, or recommend interesting places to visit.

For some young people, travelling with these friendly older people feels like travelling with their own grandparents. It makes them feel warm and happy.

Of course, there are some disadvantages to joining these tour groups too.

The schedule is often quite packed. You might have to get up at five or six in the morning because older people often get up early. As soon as everyone is up, they have to get on the coach and head straight to the next place. Tour groups also often spend a long time travelling by coach. Sometimes, you might be sitting on one for several hours. This can be tiring for young people too. So, if you like having a lie-in or prefer to organise your own time freely, a tour for older travellers might not be right for you.

However, there are still lots of interesting things about travelling with older people.

People have different life experiences, and they enjoy different things. Young people might like taking photos, looking at their phones and sharing their travels online. Older people might prefer chatting, enjoying the scenery and learning about local culture. During the trip, young people can listen to older people talk about their past, while older people can learn about the lives of younger people. Sometimes, even though there’s a big age gap, people can easily become friends.

If you want to save money, meet some friendly older people and listen to their stories, then joining a tour group for older travellers could be a good choice.

If you had the chance, would you join a tour group for older travellers? Would you be happy to travel with people who are twenty or thirty years older than you?

Feel free to leave us a comment and tell us what you think!

title: #270 One Bad Review, One Broken Life? 一条差评，一条生命
transcript:
大家好，欢迎回来 MaoMi Chinese！

今天，我想跟大家聊一个最近发生在中国的真实故事。故事的主人公叫胡二妹。她是一个小吃摊的老板娘。因为一条差评，她在网上受到了很多批评。三天后，她不幸去世了。这个故事让很多人感到难过，也让大家开始讨论网络暴力的问题。

胡二妹来自中国四川省的一个小镇。她的家很穷，所以她15岁的时候，就离开家乡去成都打工了。那时候，她还没有读完初中。后来，她做过餐厅服务员，也做过销售员。结婚以后，她有了两个孩子。后来，她回到了家乡，为了照顾家人，她和丈夫一起做小生意，在夜市卖小吃。

她没有店，只有夜市里的摊位。摊位，就是很小的一个位置。她的摊位主要卖炸土豆和炸串。炸串，就是把蔬菜或者其他食物放进油里炸熟，然后再加上调料。她的摊位不大，但是每天都要花很多时间准备。她既要赚钱养家，也要照顾两个孩子。生活非常辛苦，但是她一直努力工作。

那么，事情是怎么发生的呢？

2026年10月6日，一位顾客来到胡二妹的摊位买小吃。她买的是一种套餐，也就是顾客可以自己选择喜欢的菜，放进一个小篮子里，然后给胡二妹去炸。这个套餐里有二十多种菜。一般来说，如果顾客选的菜比较少，胡二妹就会再加一些土豆。但是，如果顾客已经选了很多菜，篮子里装满了，她就不会再加土豆了。

那天，这位顾客觉得胡二妹没有给她很多的土豆，所以她不太满意。后来，她在网上写了一条差评。她觉得胡二妹的服务不好，还建议大家不要去那里买东西。什么是差评呢。差评，也就是不好的评价。比如，你去一家餐厅吃饭，觉得食物不好吃，或者服务不好，你就可以在网上写差评。差评本身没有什么问题，因为每个人可以表达自己的感受。但是，这件事后来变得越来越严重。这位顾客写了差评以后，很多人看到了。一些人开始跟着她一起批评胡二妹。有的人说她的服务不好，有的人说她做的食物不好吃，还有人说她的摊位不卫生。

但是，这些人真的都去过她的摊位吗？他们真的了解那天的事情吗？这些，我们都不知道。短短几天，胡二妹的摊位就收到了很多差评。她开始在网上解释发生了什么，也试着和顾客沟通。她希望大家能够理解她，但是事情并没有好转。好转，就是事情变得越来越好。对一个靠卖小吃赚钱的人来说，顾客的评价很重要。如果很多人看到差评以后不再来买东西，她就可能赚不到钱。赚不到钱，她也没办法给家人好的生活。

这给她带来了很大的心理压力。“心理压力”是什么意思呢？心理压力，也就是一个人因为生活中的困难，问题或者别人的批评，感到紧张，难过，或者很难放松下来。胡二妹不只是担心自己的生意，她还要面对大量的差评。她在网上写过，看到这些评论以后，她觉得自己的天空都是黑的。她感到非常难过，也觉得生活很累。

10月9日，也就是那条差评出现三天以后，胡二妹去了河边，结束了她的人生。她留下了一封很长的信，写了自己三十多年的人生，写了收到差评后，她的感受。

后来，新闻写了她的事。很多人才开始了解她的生活。原来，在大家看到的一个小吃摊后面，是一个努力工作、照顾孩子、想让家人过上更好生活的普通人。一条差评，也许只要几秒钟的时间。但是，当很多人一起批评一个人的时候，可能会给这个人带来很大的伤害。

我们当然可以说出自己的看法。如果我们对一家店的服务不满意，可以写评价。但是，我们也应该先了解事情的经过，不要随便跟着别人一起网络暴力别人。

因为在屏幕的另一边，也有一个真实的人。他们可能和我们一样，都是努力生活的普通人。

你怎么看这个事呢？欢迎给我们留言，说说你的想法！
translation:
Hello everyone, welcome back to MaoMi Chinese+!

Today, I want to talk to you about a real story that recently happened in China. The main person in this story is called Hu Ermei. She ran a small street food stall. After receiving a negative review online, she faced a lot of criticism. Three days later, she sadly passed away. Her story made many people feel sad and started a discussion about cyberbullying.

Hu Ermei came from a small town in Sichuan Province, China. Her family was very poor, so when she was 15, she left her hometown and went to Chengdu to find work. At that time, she had not yet finished junior secondary school. Later, she worked as a waitress in a restaurant and also worked in sales. After getting married, she had two children. Later, she returned to her hometown. To look after her family, she and her husband started a small business, selling street food at a night market.

She did not have a shop. She only had a stall at the night market. A stall is a small place where someone sells things. Her stall mainly sold fried potatoes and fried skewers. Fried skewers are vegetables or other foods cooked in hot oil and then covered with seasoning. Her stall was small, but she had to spend a lot of time preparing everything every day. She had to earn money for her family and look after her two children. Life was very hard, but she kept working hard.

So, how did this happen?

On 6 October 2026, a customer came to Hu Ermei’s stall to buy some food. She ordered a set meal where customers could choose the vegetables they liked, put them into a small basket and then ask Hu Ermei to fry them. There were more than twenty different types of vegetables to choose from. Usually, if customers chose only a small amount of food, Hu Ermei would add some potatoes. However, if customers had already chosen a lot of food and the basket was full, she would not add any more potatoes.

That day, the customer felt that Hu Ermei had not given her enough potatoes, so she was unhappy. Later, she posted a negative review online. She said that Hu Ermei’s service was poor and advised other people not to buy food from her stall. So, what is a negative review? A negative review is an unfavourable opinion about a product or service. For example, if you eat at a restaurant and think the food is not good or the service is poor, you can leave a negative review online. There is nothing wrong with negative reviews in themselves, because everyone has the right to express their opinions. However, things became more and more serious. After the customer posted her review, many people saw it. Some people started criticising Hu Ermei as well. Some said her service was poor, some said her food was not good, and others said her stall was unhygienic.

But had all these people actually visited her stall? Did they really know what had happened that day? We simply do not know. Within just a few days, Hu Ermei’s stall received many negative reviews. She started explaining what had happened online and tried to communicate with the customer. She hoped people would understand her, but things did not get better. To get better means to improve or become better. For someone who depends on selling street food to earn a living, customer reviews are very important. If lots of people stop buying from her after seeing the negative reviews, she may not be able to earn enough money. Without enough money, she would also struggle to provide a good life for her family.

This caused her a great deal of psychological stress. So, what does “psychological stress” mean? Psychological stress is the pressure someone feels when facing difficulties in life, problems or criticism from other people. It can make someone feel anxious, sad or unable to relax. Hu Ermei was not only worried about her business. She also had to deal with a large number of negative reviews. She wrote online that, after seeing these comments, she felt as if her whole world had turned dark. She felt deeply upset and found life exhausting.

On 9 October, just three days after the negative review appeared, Hu Ermei went to a river and took her own life. She left behind a long letter in which she wrote about her life over the past thirty years and how she had felt after receiving the negative reviews.

Later, news reports told her story. Only then did many people begin to learn about her life. Behind the small food stall that people saw was an ordinary person who worked hard, looked after her children and wanted to give her family a better life. It may take only a few seconds to write a negative review. However, when lots of people criticise someone together, it can cause that person a great deal of pain.

Of course, we can express our own opinions. If we are unhappy with the service at a shop or restaurant, we can leave a review. However, we should also try to understand what happened before joining in and attacking someone online.

Because on the other side of the screen, there is a real person. They may be ordinary people just like us, trying their best to get through life.

What do you think about this story? Feel free to leave us a comment and share your thoughts!

title: #271 From Kindergartens to Nursing Homes 当幼儿园变成养老院
transcript:
大家好，欢迎回来 MaoMi Chinese！

你有没有想过，有一天，你小时候上过的幼儿园，可能会变成爷爷奶奶生活的地方？最近几年，在中国的一些地方，真的出现了这样的变化：以前照顾小朋友的幼儿园，现在开始照顾老年人了。有些幼儿园关门以后，变成了养老院。为什么会出现这样的变化呢？今天我们就来聊一聊！

在山东济南，有一所开了三十多年的幼儿园。以前，这里有很多小朋友，每天都能听到孩子们唱歌、说话和玩游戏的声音。但是，最近几年，来上学的孩子越来越少了。到了2024年底，这所幼儿园不得不关门。关门以后，这栋楼变成了一家养老服务中心。养老，就是照顾老人。以前幼儿园的园长，现在开始照顾老人。一些以前在幼儿园工作的老师也留下来了。他们学习了新的知识，开始照顾老人。这些人以前照顾小朋友，现在照顾老年人。

那么，为什么中国的幼儿园里，孩子越来越少了呢？其实，这和中国人口的变化有很大的关系。大家可能已经知道，中国现在出生的孩子比以前少了很多。这种情况叫作“少子化”，意思是一个国家出生的孩子越来越少。现在，很多年轻人结婚比较晚，有些人不想结婚，也有些人不打算生孩子。所以，很多地方的小朋友越来越少，幼儿园也就没有以前那么多学生了。很多幼儿园已经没有学生了。

但是，另一边，中国的老年人越来越多了。这种情况叫作“人口老龄化”，意思是一个社会里的老年人越来越多。2025年底，中国六十岁以上的老年人已经超过三亿两千万。老年人多了，养老服务也多了。养老服务，意思是帮助老年人生活，照顾老年人的服务。一边是越来越少的小朋友，一边是越来越多的老年人。所以，一些地方开始想：既然有些幼儿园已经没有足够的学生了，为什么不把这些地方用来照顾老人呢？

除了人口变化，这件事还和中国人的家庭生活有关系。以前，很多中国人相信一句话，叫作“养儿防老”。意思是，父母把孩子养大，希望自己老了以后，孩子可以照顾自己。在过去，一些老年人会和自己的孩子住在一起。孩子长大以后，也会帮助父母做饭、买东西，或者照顾他们的生活。但是，现在的生活和以前不太一样了。很多年轻人离开自己的家乡，到大城市工作。有些人甚至去了其他国家。他们有自己的工作、家庭和孩子，可能没有太多时间每天照顾父母。有些老人也不想离开自己生活了很多年的地方。所以，离家比较近的养老服务中心，就成为了一个新的选择。

中国社会正在面对两个不同的问题：孩子越来越少，老人越来越多。以前，我们可能觉得幼儿园就是给小朋友用的，养老院就是给老年人用的。但是，现在一些地方开始新的方法，让原来的地方可以帮助不同年龄的人。

好啦，今天的节目就先到这里。你觉得，把幼儿园改成养老院是一个好主意吗？如果你住的地方有这样的养老中心，你会愿意让自己的父母去那里吗？欢迎给我们留言，说说你的看法！
translation:
Hello everyone, and welcome back to MaoMi Chinese!

Have you ever imagined that one day, the kindergarten you went to as a child might become a place where elderly people live? In recent years, this has actually started happening in some parts of China. Kindergartens that used to look after young children are now looking after older people. Some kindergartens have even become nursing homes after closing down. So, why is this happening? Let's talk about it today!

In Jinan, Shandong Province, there was a kindergarten that had been open for more than 30 years. In the past, there were lots of children there. Every day, you could hear them singing, talking and playing. However, in recent years, fewer and fewer children have been coming to the kindergarten. By the end of 2024, it had no choice but to close. After it closed, the building became an elderly care centre. Elderly care means looking after older people. The former head of the kindergarten now looks after elderly people instead. Some of the teachers who used to work there have also stayed on. They have learnt new skills and started looking after older people. In the past, they looked after young children. Now, they look after the elderly.

So, why are there fewer and fewer children in Chinese kindergartens? Actually, this has a lot to do with changes in China's population. As you may already know, far fewer babies are being born in China than in the past. This situation is called a declining birth rate, which means that fewer and fewer babies are being born in a country. Nowadays, many young people are getting married later. Some do not want to get married, while others do not plan to have children. As a result, there are fewer and fewer young children in many places, and kindergartens no longer have as many pupils as they used to. Some kindergartens have even run out of pupils altogether.

However, at the same time, the number of elderly people in China is growing. This is called an ageing population, which means that there are more and more older people in a society. By the end of 2025, China had more than 320 million people aged 60 and over. As the number of older people grows, the need for elderly care services also increases. Elderly care services means services that help older people with their daily lives and look after them. On the one hand, there are fewer and fewer children. On the other hand, there are more and more elderly people. So, some places have started to ask: if certain kindergartens no longer have enough pupils, why not use these buildings to look after older people instead?

Apart from changes in the population, this also has something to do with family life in China. In the past, many Chinese people believed in a saying: “Raise children to support you in old age.” This means that parents bring up their children, hoping that their children will look after them when they get old. In the past, some elderly people lived with their children. When their children grew up, they would help their parents cook, do the shopping or look after them in their daily lives. However, life today is quite different from what it used to be. Many young people leave their hometowns to work in big cities. Some even move to other countries. They have their own jobs, families and children, so they may not have enough time to look after their parents every day. Some elderly people also do not want to leave the places where they have lived for many years. So, a nearby elderly care centre has become another option.

Chinese society is now facing two different challenges: there are fewer and fewer children, but more and more elderly people. In the past, we might have thought that kindergartens were only for young children, and nursing homes were only for older people. However, some places in China are now trying new ways to use existing buildings to help people of different ages.

Well, that's all for today's episode! Do you think turning kindergartens into nursing homes is a good idea? If there were an elderly care centre in your neighbourhood, would you be happy for your parents to go there? Leave us a comment and share your thought with us!
